`-vv` debug dump of parsed args reveals two **hidden flags accepted but absent
from help**: `--line-numbers` and `--only-matching`. Both parse fine but had
**no observable effect** on stdin search output (piped or `--stdout-detection
force-tty`): `--python strings --only-matching` still prints the full line
with the `(stdin):L:R-R:` prefix. (Fields `line_numbers: false,
only_matching: false` appear in the `GlobalOptions` debug struct.)

## 4. Environment variables

clap-backed env vars (shown as `[env: X=]` in help):

| Flag | Env | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `-u/--upper` | `UPPER` | `true`/`false` only |
| `-l/--lower` | `LOWER` | `true`/`false` |
| `-t/--titlecase` | `TITLECASE` | `true`/`false` |
| `-n/--normalize` | `NORMALIZE` | `true`/`false` |
| `-s/--squeeze` | `SQUEEZE` | `true`/`false` |
| `-i/--invert` | `INVERT` | `true`/`false` |
| `-L/--literal-string` | `LITERAL_STRING` | `true`/`false` |
| `--german-prefer-original` | `GERMAN_PREFER_ORIGINAL` | `true`/`false` |
| `--german-naive` | `GERMAN_NAIVE` | `true`/`false` |
| REPLACEMENT | `REPLACE` | any string |
| `--c` | `C` | enum |
| `--csharp` | `CSHARP` | enum |
| `--go` | `GO` | enum |
| `--hcl` | `HCL` | enum |
| `--python` | `PYTHON` | enum |
| `--rust` | `RUST` | enum |
| `--typescript` | `TYPESCRIPT` | enum |
| `--c-query` | `C_QUERY` | query string (same pattern for all 7 languages: `X_QUERY`, `X_QUERY_FILE`) |

Verified working: `REPLACE`, `UPPER`, `LOWER`, `TITLECASE`, `NORMALIZE`,
`SQUEEZE`, `LITERAL_STRING`, `INVERT`, `GERMAN_NAIVE`,
`GERMAN_PREFER_ORIGINAL`, `C`, `PYTHON`, `RUST`, `TYPESCRIPT`, `GO`,
`C_QUERY`, `C_QUERY_FILE`.

Boolean env parsing rules (clap):
- `UPPER=true` → flag on; `UPPER=false` → flag off (absent).
- `UPPER=` (empty) → exit 2:
  ```
  error: a value is required for '--upper' but none was supplied
    [possible values: true, false]

  For more information, try '--help'.
  ```
- `UPPER=1`, `UPPER=0`, `UPPER=bogus` → exit 2:
  ```
  error: invalid value '1' for '--upper'
    [possible values: true, false]
  ```
- CLI flag overrides env: `UPPER=false srgn -u` → uppercases.
- Enum env vars behave like CLI values: `PYTHON=strings` works;
  `C=bogus` → same invalid-value error as CLI (exit 2); `PYTHON=` empty →
  `error: a value is required for '--python <PYTHON>' but none was supplied`
  + possible-values list, exit 2.
- `REPLACE=world-replacement` supplies REPLACEMENT; CLI `-- X` overrides env.
  `REPLACE=` (empty) counts as *present* (empty replacement) and triggers the
  delete-conflict error with `-d`.
- No env vars exist for `--german`, `--symbols`, `--delete`, `--glob`,
  `--threads`, `--fail-*`, `--dry-run`, `--hidden`, `--gitignored`, `--sorted`,
  `--stdin/stdout-detection`, `--completions` (none shown in help).

## 5. Logging (`-v`, `RUST_LOG`)

- Logs go to **stderr**. Format (env_logger style):
  `[2026-08-08T10:19:04.084989Z ERROR srgn] message`
  RFC3339 UTC timestamp with 6-digit microseconds, level padded to width 5
  (`ERROR`, `INFO `, `DEBUG`, `TRACE`), target module path (`srgn`,
  `srgn::scoping::view`, `grep_cli`, ...). No colors when piped.
- Base level from `RUST_LOG`, default `error`. Each `-v` raises one step:
  error → warn → info → debug → trace. `-v` alone shows nothing new (no WARN
  lines exist in this path); `-vv` = INFO, `-vvv` = DEBUG, `-vvvv` = TRACE.
- If base + count exceeds trace, this exact plain line (no timestamp) is
  printed to stderr first, and trace is used:
  `Requested additional verbosity on top of env default exceeds maximum, will use maximum`
  (triggered by `-vvvvv` with default base, or `RUST_LOG=trace` with any `-v`).
- `RUST_LOG=off` silences everything (including the ERROR below).
  `RUST_LOG=srgn=debug` works (module filter). `RUST_LOG=bogus` behaves like
  `debug` level (invalid directive → falls back to showing INFO/DEBUG; TRACE
  not observed).
- Key emitted lines (INFO+): `Launching app with args: Args { ... }` (full
  Rust debug of the parsed struct, includes `additional_verbosity: N`),
  `Treating stdout as tty: false.`, `Treating stdin as readable: true.`,
  `Will read from stdin and write to stdout, applying actions.`,
  `Will use stdin to stdout.`, `Done, exiting`. DEBUG adds `Assembling
  scopers.`, `Building view.`, scope internals; `grep_cli` DEBUG explains the
  stdin heuristic: `for heuristic stdin detection on Unix, found that
  is_file=false, is_fifo=true and is_socket=false, and thus concluded that
  is_stdin_readable=true`.

## 6. Runtime behavior & messages

### 6.1 No actions + no language scope (regex scope only, or default)
stderr (ERROR log): `No actions specified, and not in search mode. Will return input unchanged, if any.`
stdin echoed to stdout byte-identically (no trailing newline added), exit 0.
**"Search mode" requires a language scope**; a regex scope alone is not search
mode. **Quirk:** the same ERROR line is (incorrectly) also logged when
`-s`/`SQUEEZE=true` is the only action — squeeze still runs correctly.

### 6.2 Search mode output format (language scope, no actions)
- Piped stdout (`auto` or `force-pipe`): one line per *line of each match*:
  `(stdin):<line>:<startcol>-<endcol>[;<startcol>-<endcol>...]:<full line content>`
  - `(stdin)` literal filename for stdin; real path when globbing (`f1.c:1:7-11:...`).
  - line is 1-based; columns are 0-based, end-exclusive **character** indices
    (unicode: `x = "héllo"` → match `"héllo"` reported as `5-11`, chars not bytes).
  - multiple disjoint matches on one line share one output line, ranges `;`-joined.
  - a multi-line match prints one line per covered line, each with that line's range.
- TTY stdout (`auto` on terminal or `--stdout-detection force-tty`):
  `<line>:<full line content>` (no filename, no column ranges, no ANSI color;
  od-verified). E.g. `1:x = "hi"`, multi-line: `1:def f():` / `2:    pass`.
- No match: no stdout, exit 0.

### 6.3 Exit codes
- 0: success (including "nothing in scope", input echoed unchanged).
- 1: runtime error. stderr is `Error: <message>` (anyhow-style, no timestamp,
  unaffected by RUST_LOG). Observed:
  - `--fail-any` & something in scope: `Error: Error applying: Some input was in scope` (stdout empty)
  - `--fail-none` & nothing in scope: `Error: Error applying: No input was in scope`
  - both flags: whichever condition hits; both can never pass simultaneously unless scope state… (both set + match → "Some input..."; both set + no match → "No input...")
  - `--fail-no-files` with no files: `Error: No files found`
  - bad tree-sitter query: `Error: Error occurred while creating a tree-sitter query: Query error at 1:1. Invalid syntax:\nbogus\n^` (multi-line)
  - missing `--c-query-file`: `Error: I/O error: No such file or directory (os error 2)`
  - invalid UTF-8 on stdin: `Error: I/O error: stream did not contain valid UTF-8` (stdout empty)
  - bad regex scope `(`:
    ```
    Error: Failed building regex

    Caused by:
        Invalid regex: Parsing error at position 1: Opening parenthesis without closing parenthesis
    ```
  - replacement referencing a missing capture group (`'$9'`):
    `Error: Error applying: Error in an action: Action failed in replacement: Error in variable expressions: Undefined variable, unable to substitute: '9'`
- 2: CLI parse error (clap), see §3.

### 6.4 stdin/glob interplay
- Piped stdin + `-G glob`: **glob is ignored**, stdin used. ERROR log:
  `Detected stdin, and request for files: will use stdin and ignore files.`
  (`--fail-no-files` then has no effect.) Exit 0.
- No readable stdin (e.g. `</dev/null`) + `-G 'f*.c'`: files processed
  in-place, matching file names printed to stdout one per line (`f1.c`).
- `--stdin-detection force-unreadable` + piped stdin + `-G`: files win.
  Force-unreadable + piped stdin + no glob: stdin is still read (no other source).
- `--dry-run` with stdin: prints two search-format lines per changed line —
  before then after: `(stdin):1:0-3:abc` then `(stdin):1:0-3:ABC` — and does
  not modify anything; exit 0.

### 6.5 I/O edge cases
- Empty stdin with an action: no output, exit 0, no message.
- No trailing newline: preserved (input `abc` → output `ABC`, no `\n` added).
- Unicode: `-u` on `héllo wörld 😀` → `HÉLLO WÖRLD 😀` (full unicode casing).
- CRLF: `\r` preserved and treated as ordinary content; scope regex `b$` did
  **not** match in `ab\r\n` (the `$` anchors before `\n`, `\r` blocks it).
- Invalid UTF-8 bytes → exit 1, error per §6.3.
- NUL bytes pass through unmodified.
- Replacement capture refs: `'(h)ello' -- '$1ELLO'` → `hELLO ...`;
  named: `(?P<first>h)ello` + `-- '$first!'` → `h!`; undefined → error §6.3.
- Empty regex scope `''` with `-u`: input returned unchanged, exit 0.
- Newlines inside the scope regex work (`$'b\nc'` matches across lines).

### 6.6 Aliases
`--squeeze-repeats` (= `--squeeze`), `--py`, `--rs`, `--ts`, `--cs` all work
long-form. In clap errors the canonical name is shown. No short aliases beyond
those in help.

### 6.7 Miscellaneous verified
- `--fail-any` short-circuits before actions run (stdout empty even with `-u`).
- `-d '.*' --python strings` on `x = "hi"` → `x = ""` (scopes intersect).
- `--completions` values are lowercase-only; bad value → exit 2 invalid-value error.
- All clap parse errors end with the line `For more information, try '--help'.`
  preceded by a blank line; most include a `Usage:` block except
  "a value is required" and "invalid value" errors.

payload.resultSummary:
Done. Full spec at `/workspace/probes/cli/spec.md`, with verbatim artifacts (`help.txt`, `h.txt`, `version.txt`, 5 completion files, ~25 error captures under `err/`). Key findings:

- **`--` positional quirk**: REPLACEMENT is only accepted after `--`; a *leading* `--` sends values to REPLACEMENT, not SCOPE (`-- X` = replace-all-with-X; `-- foo bar` = "[REPLACEMENT] cannot be used multiple times"). Without `--`, a second positional errors.
- **Env vars are strict clap booleans**: `UPPER=1`/`0`/`bogus` → exit 2; only `true`/`false` valid; `UPPER=` empty errors too. `REPLACE=` (empty) counts as present and triggers the delete-conflict error.
- **Help lies about squeeze**: `-s` composes freely with other actions (only `-d` is exclusive), and squeeze-only runs emit a spurious `ERROR ... No actions specified` log line while still working.
- **Hidden flags**: `--line-numbers` and `--only-matching` are accepted but absent from help and have no observable effect on stdin search output.
- **Search output is TTY-dependent**: piped → `(stdin):1:5-7:line` (0-based, end-exclusive *char* columns, `;`-joined multi-ranges); TTY/`force-tty` → bare `1:line`. No ANSI colors anywhere, even on TTY (errors and help included).
- **Inconsistent program naming**: usage lines use argv[0] basename, but version, completions content, and the custom `-L` missing-scope error hardcode `srgn`; the `-L` error is also styled differently (`The following required argument was not provided: scope`).
- **Logging**: `[RFC3339µsZ LEVEL␣target] msg` on stderr; base from `RUST_LOG` (default error), each `-v` +1 level, overflow prints plain warning `Requested additional verbosity...`; `RUST_LOG=bogus` falls back to debug-ish.
- **stdin beats glob**: piped stdin + `-G` ignores the glob with an ERROR log; `--fail-no-files` then does nothing. Exit codes: 0 ok / 1 runtime (`Error: ...` anyhow-style) / 2 clap parse errors.

args.content:
# Behavioral spec: `srgn --go` prepared queries (go-scopes)

Binary: `/workspace/executable` (srgn). All findings from black-box CLI observation only.
(Note: the task brief suggested a filename containing the full task description; that exceeds
the 255-byte filename limit, so this file is `go-scopes.md`.)

All examples below were run against this reference input unless noted (`sample.go`):

```go
package main

// line comment
/* block
   comment */
import (
	"fmt"
	alias "os"
	_ "net/http"
)

type MyInt int

type Alias = string

type MyStruct struct {
	Name string `json:"name" xml:"name"`
	Age  int
}

type MyInterface interface {
	DoThing(x int) string
}

const Pi = 3.14
const (
	A = 1
	B = 2
)

var GlobalVar = 42
var (
	X int
	Y string
)

func init() {
	fmt.Println("init")
}

func freeFunc(a, b int) int {
	return a + b
}

func (s MyStruct) DoThing(x int) string {
	defer fmt.Println("deferred")
	go fmt.Println("goroutine")
	var local = "localstr"
	switch x {
	case 1:
		goto End
	default:
		select {
		case <-make(chan int):
		default:
		}
	}
End:
	fmt.Printf("%v %v", local, s.Name)
	return "done"
}

func Generic[T any, U comparable](t T, u U) T {
	expr := t
	return expr
}
```

## 0. General scope model

- A scope is a set of byte ranges. The positional regex SCOPE (default `.*`) is always
  intersected with language scopes. The default `.*` regex does **not** cross newlines
  (no DOTALL), so a multi-line language range is effectively split into per-line ranges.
  This is observable with replacement: `srgn --go comments -- 'REPL'` on the block comment
  `/* block\n   comment */` yields TWO `REPL` lines, while `srgn --go comments '(?s).*' -- 'REPL'`
  yields ONE `REPL`. For range-detection, `--upper` is unaffected by this.
- Multiple `--go <value>` flags: intersected left to right (set intersection; order does not
  matter observably). With `-j`/`--join-language-scopes`: union. Overlapping joined ranges are
  merged (content processed once).
- `--go` and `--go-query`/`--go-query-file` are mutually exclusive (clap conflict, exit 2).
  Multiple `--go-query` flags ARE allowed and intersect/join like prepared scopes.
- Language scoping works on stdin (parsed as Go regardless of content) and is error-tolerant
  (see §6).
- Env vars: `GO=comments srgn --upper` works exactly like `--go comments`
  (footgun: `GO` is also the Go toolchain env var). Likewise `GO_QUERY`, `GO_QUERY_FILE`.

## 1. Exact ranges per prepared value

Method: `srgn --go <value> --upper` and note which bytes changed; replacement probes
(`-- 'REPL'`) confirm whether delimiters are included.

| value | exact range |
|---|---|
| `comments` | Entire comment **including** `//` / `/*` `*/` delimiters. Line and block comments; trailing comments after code on the same line included. No doc-comment distinction. |
| `strings` | Interpreted `"..."` and raw backtick strings, **including the quotes/backticks** (replacing the scope removes the quotes). **Excludes**: import path strings, struct tags, and rune literals (`'x'` unchanged). Escape sequences included (content uppercased, `\` sequences left as-is by upper). Multi-line raw strings covered wholly. |
| `imports` | Only the import **path string including its quotes** (replacing yields `REPL` without quotes). Import aliases (`alias`), blank `_`, and the `import` keyword/parens are excluded. Works for single-line `import "fmt"` and grouped `import (...)`. |
| `expression` | All expression nodes, unioned: call expressions incl. receiver/args (`fmt.Println("init")`), binary exprs (`a + b`), parenthesized/unary/channel exprs (`<-make(chan int)`), composite literals **including their type part** (`struct{ f int }{f: 1}` in a var value is fully in scope), func literals (`func() { recover() }`), type conversions (`interface{}(0)`), rune literals (`'x'` → `'X'`), string literals, the RHS of `const`/`var` specs, and identifiers on the LHS of short var decls (`expr := t` → `EXPR := T`; tree-sitter models that LHS as `expression_list`). NOT included: keywords (`return`, `defer`, `goto`, `switch`, `case`), `var_spec`/`const_spec` names, label identifiers. |
| `type-def` | Every type declaration **entirely, including the `type` keyword**: simple defs (`type MyInt int`), aliases (`type Alias = string`), structs, interfaces. I.e. superset of struct/interface/type-alias targets. |
| `type-alias` | The alias spec **excluding the `type` keyword**: `Alias = string` only (`type ALIAS = STRING` — `type` stays lowercase). Plain defs are not matched. |
| `struct` | Whole `type Name struct { ... }` declaration: `type` keyword, name, type parameters, all fields, **including struct tags** inside. Anonymous structs (`var x struct{ f int }`) are NOT matched. |
| `interface` | Whole `type Name interface { ... }` declaration, including embedded elements (`io.Reader`) and method elements. |
| `struct~PAT` | Like `struct`, but only structs whose **name** matches regex PAT. |
| `interface~PAT` | Like `interface`, name-filtered. |
| `const` | Each `const_spec` individually, **excluding the `const` keyword**: `Pi = 3.14`, and `A = 1` / `B = 2` inside a grouped `const ( ... )`. The `const ( )` wrapper is not in scope. |
| `var` | Each `var_spec` individually, **excluding the `var` keyword**: `GlobalVar = 42`, `X int`, grouped specs, and also `var local = "localstr"` **inside function bodies**. Includes composite literal values and multiline raw string values. Short var decls (`:=`) are NOT matched. |
| `func` | Whole function/method declarations: `func` keyword, receiver, name, type params, signature, and entire body. Includes methods, `init`, generics. |
| `func~PAT` | Like `func`, filtered by function **name** regex (methods matched by their method name; `func~init` matches BOTH free `func init()` and a method named `init`). |
| `method` | Whole declarations having a receiver (`func (s S) M()`, pointer receivers, generic receivers `func (l *List[T]) Push(v T)`). A method named `init` is a `method`, NOT an `init-func`. Interface method signatures are NOT matched. |
| `free-func` | Whole declarations without a receiver — **includes `func init()`**. |
| `init-func` | Only free `func init()` definitions (whole decl). Method named `init` excluded. |
| `type-params` | Each type parameter element **separately** (`T any`, `U comparable` → two ranges; brackets and commas excluded). Matches both generic funcs (`func Generic[T any]`) and generic type decls (`type List[T any] struct`). |
| `defer` | Whole `defer` statement: keyword + call or func literal incl. its body. |
| `go` | Whole `go` statement: keyword + call. Does not match `goto`. |
| `select` | Whole `select { ... }` statement incl. keyword, braces, all comm clauses. |
| `switch` | Whole **expression** `switch` statement incl. all `case`/`default` clauses and nested statements. **Type switches** (`switch v := x.(type)`) are NOT matched. |
| `labeled` | Whole labeled statement = the label **and** the following statement (`End:` + `fmt.Printf(...)` both in scope). `case`/`default` labels are not labeled statements. |
| `goto` | Whole `goto Label` statement incl. label identifier. |
| `struct-tags` | The tag literal **including backticks** (replacement removes them). Applies to any field declaration tag, including fields of anonymous structs. Not restricted to `struct`-scope targets. |

Notable asymmetries: `const`/`var`/`type-alias` scopes EXCLUDE their leading keyword, while
`func`/`struct`/`interface`/`type-def`/`defer`/`go`/`switch`/`select`/`labeled`/`goto` INCLUDE it.

## 2. `~PAT` dynamic queries

- PAT is a Rust-regex, **case-sensitive, unanchored** (substring) match against the declared name:
  `struct~test` matches `testTwo` not `TestOne`; `struct~[tT]est` matches both; `func~^free` anchors fine.
- Empty pattern (`struct~`) matches all items (empty regex matches every name).
- Invalid regex: exit code **2**, stderr verbatim (note the value shown is just the pattern part):

```
error: invalid value '(' for 'struct'

  tip: error was: regex parse error:
    (
    ^
error: unclosed group

For more information, try '--help'.
```

- Unknown scope value (also case-sensitive: `FUNC` fails): exit **2**, stderr verbatim:

```
error: invalid value 'bogus' for '--go <GO>'
  [possible values: comments, strings, imports, expression, type-def, type-alias, struct, interface, const, var, func, method, free-func, init-func, type-params, defer, select, go, switch, labeled, goto, struct-tags]

For more information, try '--help'.
```

(The possible-values list does NOT mention the `~PAT` variants, unlike `--help`.)

## 3. Intersection / join examples (verified)

- `srgn --go func --go strings --upper` → only strings inside func bodies uppercased.
- `srgn -j --go func --go strings --upper` → whole func bodies AND all strings anywhere uppercased;
  a string inside a func is processed once (ranges merged).
- `srgn --go struct --go strings --upper` → **no matches** (struct tags are excluded from `strings`),
  input unchanged, exit 0 (action mode).
- `srgn --go struct --go struct-tags --upper` → only the tags.
- Regex scope intersects too: `srgn --go func 'defer.*' --upper` → only the defer line (to EOL).
- `--go func --go func` (duplicate) is accepted, behaves as one.
- `--go` + `--go-query` together: exit **2**, stderr verbatim:

```
error: the argument '--go <GO>' cannot be used with '--go-query <TREE-SITTER-QUERY-VALUE>'

Usage: executable --go <GO> --upper [SCOPE] [-- <REPLACEMENT>]

For more information, try '--help'.
```

## 4. `--go-query` custom tree-sitter queries

Grammar is tree-sitter-go. Rules observed:

- **Captures are required**: a query with no `@capture` (e.g. `(comment)`) parses fine but
  matches nothing (exit 0, input unchanged). Capture names are arbitrary (`@c`, `@x`).
- The captured node's exact range becomes the scope: `(function_declaration name: (identifier) @fname)`
  scopes only function names (method declarations are `method_declaration` with `field_identifier`
  names — not matched by `function_declaration`/`identifier` patterns).
- Anonymous tokens capturable: `"func" @kw` scopes just the `func` keywords.
- Predicates work: `((identifier) @id (#match? @id "^init"))` matched only the free func's `init`.
- Quantifiers work: `(comment)+ @c`.
- Multiple captures in one pattern are unioned: `(function_declaration name: (identifier) @n body: (block) @b)`
  scopes name and body. Multiple patterns in one query string are unioned:
  `(function_declaration) @f (call_expression) @c`.
- Empty query string / empty query file: valid, matches nothing, exit 0.
- Two `--go-query` flags intersect by default; `-j` joins them.
- Query errors go to **stderr**, exit **1**, verbatim:
  - Invalid node type: `Error: Error occurred while creating a tree-sitter query: Query error at 1:2. Invalid node type nonexistent_node`
  - Syntax error (`(((` as argument): `Error: Error occurred while creating a tree-sitter query: Query error at 1:4. Invalid syntax:` followed by the query text and a `^` caret line.
  - Same `(((` from a file (file ends with newline): `... Query error at 2:1. Invalid syntax:` then `Unexpected EOF`.
  - Missing query file: `Error: I/O error: No such file or directory (os error 2)` (exit 1).

## 5. Output formats

### Action mode (any action given, e.g. `--upper`, `-d`, replacement)
Prints the FULL (possibly modified) input to stdout, byte-exact otherwise:
no trailing newline stays absent, CRLF line endings preserved, exit 0 — **even when nothing
matched** (input echoed unchanged, exit 0).

With hidden flag `--only-matching` (accepted but NOT shown in `--help`), action mode prints only
the lines that contain matches, one per line, format `(stdin):START-END:CONTENT` (no line number;
START/END are 0-based byte offsets of the matched portion within that line, end-exclusive;
the full line content after modification is printed):

```
(srgn --go strings --only-matching --upper < sample.go)
(stdin):13-19:	fmt.Println("INIT")
(stdin):19-29:	defer fmt.Println("DEFERRED")
...
```

`--line-numbers` is likewise a hidden accepted flag (no observable change in the tested cases).
`--count` does NOT exist: `error: unexpected argument '--count' found\n\n  tip: a similar argument exists: '--c'` (exit 2).

### Search mode (language scope given, NO actions)
- Piped stdout: one line per matched source line:
  `(stdin):LINE:START-END[;START-END...]:CONTENT` where LINE is 1-based, ranges are 0-based
  byte offsets end-exclusive within the line, multiple matches on one line are `;`-separated,
  and multi-line scopes print one record per covered line. Example:

```
(srgn --go func 'Test' < pat.go)
(stdin):7:5-9:func TestFunc() {}
(stdin):8:8-12;23-27:func (t TestOne) MethodTest() {}

(srgn --go struct < sample.go)
(stdin):16:0-22:type MyStruct struct {
(stdin):17:0-37:	Name string `json:"name" xml:"name"`
(stdin):18:0-9:	Age  int
(stdin):19:0-1:}
```

- TTY stdout (also with `--stdout-detection force-tty`): format collapses to `LINE:CONTENT`
  (no `(stdin)` prefix, no ranges). NO ANSI color codes in either mode.
- No trailing newline in input → none in output.
- Search mode with ZERO matches: exit **1**, stderr `Error: Error applying: No input was in scope`.
  (Same error with `--fail-none` in action mode when nothing matched. Without `--fail-none`,
  action mode with no match exits 0 with input unchanged.)
- Regex-only scope with no action is NOT search mode: prints log line
  `[<RFC3339 timestamp> ERROR srgn] No actions specified, and not in search mode. Will return input unchanged, if any.`
  to stderr, echoes input, exit 0.
- `--fail-any` with a match: exit **1**, stderr `Error: Error applying: Some input was in scope`.
- `-d`/`--delete` REQUIRES an explicit positional SCOPE; without it: exit 2,
  `error: the following required arguments were not provided:\n  <SCOPE>\n\nUsage: executable --go <GO> --delete <SCOPE> [-- <REPLACEMENT>]`.

## 6. Syntax errors in the Go input

Parsing is error-tolerant; srgn NEVER fails on malformed Go. For

```go
package main

func broken( {
	x := 
}
```

`--go func --upper` uppercases `FUNC BROKEN( {` and `X := ` (the broken function node still
matches `func`), exit **0**, no warning. `--go comments` finds nothing, exit 0 (action mode).
A custom query `(ERROR) @e` on this input matched NOTHING (exit 0) — srgn appears to skip/dedupe
ERROR-node captures or tree-sitter recovers without a top-level ERROR here; do not rely on
`(ERROR)` captures.

display.content:
# Behavioral spec: `srgn --go` prepared queries (go-scopes)

Binary: `/workspace/executable` (srgn). All findings from black-box CLI observation only.
(Note: the task brief suggested a filename containing the full task description; that exceeds
the 255-byte filename limit, so this file is `go-scopes.md`.)

All examples below were run against this reference input unless noted (`sample.go`):

```go
package main

// line comment
/* block
   comment */
import (
	"fmt"
	alias "os"
	_ "net/http"
)

type MyInt int

type Alias = string

type MyStruct struct {
	Name string `json:"name" xml:"name"`
	Age  int
}

type MyInterface interface {
	DoThing(x int) string
}

const Pi = 3.14
const (
	A = 1
	B = 2
)

var GlobalVar = 42
var (
	X int
	Y string
)

func init() {
	fmt.Println("init")
}

func freeFunc(a, b int) int {
	return a + b
}

func (s MyStruct) DoThing(x int) string {
	defer fmt.Println("deferred")
	go fmt.Println("goroutine")
	var local = "localstr"
	switch x {
	case 1:
		goto End
	default:
		select {
		case <-make(chan int):
		default:
		}
	}
End:
	fmt.Printf("%v %v", local, s.Name)
	return "done"
}

func Generic[T any, U comparable](t T, u U) T {
	expr := t
	return expr
}
```

## 0. General scope model

- A scope is a set of byte ranges. The positional regex SCOPE (default `.*`) is always
  intersected with language scopes. The default `.*` regex does **not** cross newlines
  (no DOTALL), so a multi-line language range is effectively split into per-line ranges.
  This is observable with replacement: `srgn --go comments -- 'REPL'` on the block comment
  `/* block\n   comment */` yields TWO `REPL` lines, while `srgn --go comments '(?s).*' -- 'REPL'`
  yields ONE `REPL`. For range-detection, `--upper` is unaffected by this.
- Multiple `--go <value>` flags: intersected left to right (set intersection; order does not
  matter observably). With `-j`/`--join-language-scopes`: union. Overlapping joined ranges are
  merged (content processed once).
- `--go` and `--go-query`/`--go-query-file` are mutually exclusive (clap conflict, exit 2).
  Multiple `--go-query` flags ARE allowed and intersect/join like prepared scopes.
- Language scoping works on stdin (parsed as Go regardless of content) and is error-tolerant
  (see §6).
- Env vars: `GO=comments srgn --upper` works exactly like `--go comments`
  (footgun: `GO` is also the Go toolchain env var). Likewise `GO_QUERY`, `GO_QUERY_FILE`.

## 1. Exact ranges per prepared value

Method: `srgn --go <value> --upper` and note which bytes changed; replacement probes
(`-- 'REPL'`) confirm whether delimiters are included.

| value | exact range |
|---|---|
| `comments` | Entire comment **including** `//` / `/*` `*/` delimiters. Line and block comments; trailing comments after code on the same line included. No doc-comment distinction. |
| `strings` | Interpreted `"..."` and raw backtick strings, **including the quotes/backticks** (replacing the scope removes the quotes). **Excludes**: import path strings, struct tags, and rune literals (`'x'` unchanged). Escape sequences included (content uppercased, `\` sequences left as-is by upper). Multi-line raw strings covered wholly. |
| `imports` | Only the import **path string including its quotes** (replacing yields `REPL` without quotes). Import aliases (`alias`), blank `_`, and the `import` keyword/parens are excluded. Works for single-line `import "fmt"` and grouped `import (...)`. |
| `expression` | All expression nodes, unioned: call expressions incl. receiver/args (`fmt.Println("init")`), binary exprs (`a + b`), parenthesized/unary/channel exprs (`<-make(chan int)`), composite literals **including their type part** (`struct{ f int }{f: 1}` in a var value is fully in scope), func literals (`func() { recover() }`), type conversions (`interface{}(0)`), rune literals (`'x'` → `'X'`), string literals, the RHS of `const`/`var` specs, and identifiers on the LHS of short var decls (`expr := t` → `EXPR := T`; tree-sitter models that LHS as `expression_list`). NOT included: keywords (`return`, `defer`, `goto`, `switch`, `case`), `var_spec`/`const_spec` names, label identifiers. |
| `type-def` | Every type declaration **entirely, including the `type` keyword**: simple defs (`type MyInt int`), aliases (`type Alias = string`), structs, interfaces. I.e. superset of struct/interface/type-alias targets. |
| `type-alias` | The alias spec **excluding the `type` keyword**: `Alias = string` only (`type ALIAS = STRING` — `type` stays lowercase). Plain defs are not matched. |
| `struct` | Whole `type Name struct { ... }` declaration: `type` keyword, name, type parameters, all fields, **including struct tags** inside. Anonymous structs (`var x struct{ f int }`) are NOT matched. |
| `interface` | Whole `type Name interface { ... }` declaration, including embedded elements (`io.Reader`) and method elements. |
| `struct~PAT` | Like `struct`, but only structs whose **name** matches regex PAT. |
| `interface~PAT` | Like `interface`, name-filtered. |
| `const` | Each `const_spec` individually, **excluding the `const` keyword**: `Pi = 3.14`, and `A = 1` / `B = 2` inside a grouped `const ( ... )`. The `const ( )` wrapper is not in scope. |
| `var` | Each `var_spec` individually, **excluding the `var` keyword**: `GlobalVar = 42`, `X int`, grouped specs, and also `var local = "localstr"` **inside function bodies**. Includes composite literal values and multiline raw string values. Short var decls (`:=`) are NOT matched. |
| `func` | Whole function/method declarations: `func` keyword, receiver, name, type params, signature, and entire body. Includes methods, `init`, generics. |
| `func~PAT` | Like `func`, filtered by function **name** regex (methods matched by their method name; `func~init` matches BOTH free `func init()` and a method named `init`). |
| `method` | Whole declarations having a receiver (`func (s S) M()`, pointer receivers, generic receivers `func (l *List[T]) Push(v T)`). A method named `init` is a `method`, NOT an `init-func`. Interface method signatures are NOT matched. |
| `free-func` | Whole declarations without a receiver — **includes `func init()`**. |
| `init-func` | Only free `func init()` definitions (whole decl). Method named `init` excluded. |
| `type-params` | Each type parameter element **separately** (`T any`, `U comparable` → two ranges; brackets and commas excluded). Matches both generic funcs (`func Generic[T any]`) and generic type decls (`type List[T any] struct`). |
| `defer` | Whole `defer` statement: keyword + call or func literal incl. its body. |
| `go` | Whole `go` statement: keyword + call. Does not match `goto`. |
| `select` | Whole `select { ... }` statement incl. keyword, braces, all comm clauses. |
| `switch` | Whole **expression** `switch` statement incl. all `case`/`default` clauses and nested statements. **Type switches** (`switch v := x.(type)`) are NOT matched. |
| `labeled` | Whole labeled statement = the label **and** the following statement (`End:` + `fmt.Printf(...)` both in scope). `case`/`default` labels are not labeled statements. |
| `goto` | Whole `goto Label` statement incl. label identifier. |
| `struct-tags` | The tag literal **including backticks** (replacement removes them). Applies to any field declaration tag, including fields of anonymous structs. Not restricted to `struct`-scope targets. |

Notable asymmetries: `const`/`var`/`type-alias` scopes EXCLUDE their leading keyword, while
`func`/`struct`/`interface`/`type-def`/`defer`/`go`/`switch`/`select`/`labeled`/`goto` INCLUDE it.

## 2. `~PAT` dynamic queries

- PAT is a Rust-regex, **case-sensitive, unanchored** (substring) match against the declared name:
  `struct~test` matches `testTwo` not `TestOne`; `struct~[tT]est` matches both; `func~^free` anchors fine.
- Empty pattern (`struct~`) matches all items (empty regex matches every name).
- Invalid regex: exit code **2**, stderr verbatim (note the value shown is just the pattern part):

```
error: invalid value '(' for 'struct'

  tip: error was: regex parse error:
    (
    ^
error: unclosed group

For more information, try '--help'.
```

- Unknown scope value (also case-sensitive: `FUNC` fails): exit **2**, stderr verbatim:

```
error: invalid value 'bogus' for '--go <GO>'
  [possible values: comments, strings, imports, expression, type-def, type-alias, struct, interface, const, var, func, method, free-func, init-func, type-params, defer, select, go, switch, labeled, goto, struct-tags]

For more information, try '--help'.
```

(The possible-values list does NOT mention the `~PAT` variants, unlike `--help`.)

## 3. Intersection / join examples (verified)

- `srgn --go func --go strings --upper` → only strings inside func bodies uppercased.
- `srgn -j --go func --go strings --upper` → whole func bodies AND all strings anywhere uppercased;
  a string inside a func is processed once (ranges merged).
- `srgn --go struct --go strings --upper` → **no matches** (struct tags are excluded from `strings`),
  input unchanged, exit 0 (action mode).
- `srgn --go struct --go struct-tags --upper` → only the tags.
- Regex scope intersects too: `srgn --go func 'defer.*' --upper` → only the defer line (to EOL).
- `--go func --go func` (duplicate) is accepted, behaves as one.
- `--go` + `--go-query` together: exit **2**, stderr verbatim:

```
error: the argument '--go <GO>' cannot be used with '--go-query <TREE-SITTER-QUERY-VALUE>'

Usage: executable --go <GO> --upper [SCOPE] [-- <REPLACEMENT>]

For more information, try '--help'.
```

## 4. `--go-query` custom tree-sitter queries

Grammar is tree-sitter-go. Rules observed:

- **Captures are required**: a query with no `@capture` (e.g. `(comment)`) parses fine but
  matches nothing (exit 0, input unchanged). Capture names are arbitrary (`@c`, `@x`).
- The captured node's exact range becomes the scope: `(function_declaration name: (identifier) @fname)`
  scopes only function names (method declarations are `method_declaration` with `field_identifier`
  names — not matched by `function_declaration`/`identifier` patterns).
- Anonymous tokens capturable: `"func" @kw` scopes just the `func` keywords.
- Predicates work: `((identifier) @id (#match? @id "^init"))` matched only the free func's `init`.
- Quantifiers work: `(comment)+ @c`.
- Multiple captures in one pattern are unioned: `(function_declaration name: (identifier) @n body: (block) @b)`
  scopes name and body. Multiple patterns in one query string are unioned:
  `(function_declaration) @f (call_expression) @c`.
- Empty query string / empty query file: valid, matches nothing, exit 0.
- Two `--go-query` flags intersect by default; `-j` joins them.
- Query errors go to **stderr**, exit **1**, verbatim:
  - Invalid node type: `Error: Error occurred while creating a tree-sitter query: Query error at 1:2. Invalid node type nonexistent_node`
  - Syntax error (`(((` as argument): `Error: Error occurred while creating a tree-sitter query: Query error at 1:4. Invalid syntax:` followed by the query text and a `^` caret line.
  - Same `(((` from a file (file ends with newline): `... Query error at 2:1. Invalid syntax:` then `Unexpected EOF`.
  - Missing query file: `Error: I/O error: No such file or directory (os error 2)` (exit 1).

## 5. Output formats

### Action mode (any action given, e.g. `--upper`, `-d`, replacement)
Prints the FULL (possibly modified) input to stdout, byte-exact otherwise:
no trailing newline stays absent, CRLF line endings preserved, exit 0 — **even when nothing
matched** (input echoed unchanged, exit 0).

With hidden flag `--only-matching` (accepted but NOT shown in `--help`), action mode prints only
the lines that contain matches, one per line, format `(stdin):START-END:CONTENT` (no line number;
START/END are 0-based byte offsets of the matched portion within that line, end-exclusive;
the full line content after modification is printed):

```
(srgn --go strings --only-matching --upper < sample.go)
(stdin):13-19:	fmt.Println("INIT")
(stdin):19-29:	defer fmt.Println("DEFERRED")
...
```

`--line-numbers` is likewise a hidden accepted flag (no observable change in the tested cases).
`--count` does NOT exist: `error: unexpected argument '--count' found\n\n  tip: a similar argument exists: '--c'` (exit 2).

### Search mode (language scope given, NO actions)
- Piped stdout: one line per matched source line:
  `(stdin):LINE:START-END[;START-END...]:CONTENT` where LINE is 1-based, ranges are 0-based
  byte offsets end-exclusive within the line, multiple matches on one line are `;`-separated,
  and multi-line scopes print one record per covered line. Example:

```
(srgn --go func 'Test' < pat.go)
(stdin):7:5-9:func TestFunc() {}
(stdin):8:8-12;23-27:func (t TestOne) MethodTest() {}

(srgn --go struct < sample.go)
(stdin):16:0-22:type MyStruct struct {
(stdin):17:0-37:	Name string `json:"name" xml:"name"`
(stdin):18:0-9:	Age  int
(stdin):19:0-1:}
```

- TTY stdout (also with `--stdout-detection force-tty`): format collapses to `LINE:CONTENT`
  (no `(stdin)` prefix, no ranges). NO ANSI color codes in either mode.
- No trailing newline in input → none in output.
- Search mode with ZERO matches: exit **1**, stderr `Error: Error applying: No input was in scope`.
  (Same error with `--fail-none` in action mode when nothing matched. Without `--fail-none`,
  action mode with no match exits 0 with input unchanged.)
- Regex-only scope with no action is NOT search mode: prints log line
  `[<RFC3339 timestamp> ERROR srgn] No actions specified, and not in search mode. Will return input unchanged, if any.`
  to stderr, echoes input, exit 0.
- `--fail-any` with a match: exit **1**, stderr `Error: Error applying: Some input was in scope`.
- `-d`/`--delete` REQUIRES an explicit positional SCOPE; without it: exit 2,
  `error: the following required arguments were not provided:\n  <SCOPE>\n\nUsage: executable --go <GO> --delete <SCOPE> [-- <REPLACEMENT>]`.

## 6. Syntax errors in the Go input

Parsing is error-tolerant; srgn NEVER fails on malformed Go. For

```go
package main

func broken( {
	x := 
}
```

`--go func --upper` uppercases `FUNC BROKEN( {` and `X := ` (the broken function node still
matches `func`), exit **0**, no warning. `--go comments` finds nothing, exit 0 (action mode).
A custom query `(ERROR) @e` on this input matched NOTHING (exit 0) — srgn appears to skip/dedupe
ERROR-node captures or tree-sitter recovers without a top-level ERROR here; do not rely on
`(ERROR)` captures.

## 7. Edge cases (all verified byte-exact with `od -c`)

- Empty stdin, action mode: empty stdout, exit 0. Empty stdin, search mode:
  `Error: Error applying: No input was in scope`, exit 1.
- Invalid UTF-8 anywhere: stdout empty, stderr `Error: I/O error: stream did not contain valid UTF-8`, exit **1**.
- Unicode works: `--go comments --upper` on `// héllo 😀 welt` → `// HÉLLO 😀 WELT`
  (é→É, emoji untouched).
- CRLF preserved exactly in action mode; comment scoping unaffected.
- Missing trailing newline preserved exactly.
- Search-mode byte offsets count BYTES (é = 2 columns): `// été` matched by `t.` reports `2:5-8`.

## 8. Exit code summary

| condition | exit |
|---|---|
| success (matches or, in action mode, no matches) | 0 |
| tree-sitter query compile error, missing query file, invalid UTF-8 input, search mode with no match, `--fail-any` matched, `--fail-none` no match | 1 |
| CLI usage errors: unknown `--go` value, bad `~PAT` regex, `--go` with `--go-query`, missing SCOPE for `-d`, unknown flag | 2 |

payload.resultSummary:
Done. Full spec written to `/workspace/probes/go-scopes.md`. Key findings:

- **Keyword inclusion is inconsistent**: `const`, `var`, and `type-alias` scopes exclude the leading keyword (`const PI = 3.14` — `const` stays), while `func`, `struct`, `interface`, `type-def`, `defer`, `go`, `switch`, `select`, `labeled`, `goto` include it.
- **`strings` excludes import paths, struct tags, and rune literals**; consequently `--go struct --go strings` intersects to *empty* (tags live only in `struct-tags`). `imports` scopes only the quoted path (quotes included; aliases excluded).
- **`switch` matches only expression switches** — type switches (`x.(type)`) are silently excluded. **`free-func` includes `init`**, but a *method* named `init` is `method`, not `init-func`. `labeled` covers the label **plus** its statement. `type-params` yields one range per parameter (brackets excluded), on both generic funcs and types.
- **Default regex `.*` is not DOTALL**: replacement splits multi-line ranges per line (block comment → two replacements); `(?s).*` fixes it.
- **Custom queries**: captures are mandatory (capture-less query matches nothing, exit 0), names arbitrary, predicates/quantifiers/anonymous tokens all work; compile errors exit 1 with `Error: Error occurred while creating a tree-sitter query: Query error at L:C...` on stderr. `--go` + `--go-query` conflict → exit 2. `(ERROR) @e` captures match nothing on broken input.
- **Syntax-broken Go never fails** — partial scoping, exit 0, no warning. Invalid UTF-8 → exit 1 (`stream did not contain valid UTF-8`).
- **Search-mode output**: piped = `(stdin):LINE:BYTE_START-END[;...]:content` (0-based end-exclusive byte ranges), TTY = `LINE:content`, no ANSI colors either way; zero matches in search mode → exit 1 (`No input was in scope`). `--only-matching`/`--line-numbers` exist as hidden flags; `--count` doesn't (README is ahead of the binary).
- **Footgun**: the `GO` environment variable feeds `--go` directly (`GO=comments srgn --upper` works).

args.content:
# srgn core-engine behavioral specification

Binary under test: `srgn 0.14.1` (`/workspace/executable --version` → `srgn 0.14.1`).
All probes used stdin piping. Invocation shape: `srgn [OPTIONS] [SCOPE] [-- <REPLACEMENT>]`.
Default `SCOPE` is `.*`.

Note on flags: `--only-matching` and `--line-numbers` exist and work but are **hidden**
(do not appear in `-h` or `--help`). `-o` does NOT exist (clap error, exit 2).
`--count` does NOT exist (exit 2).

---

## 1. Regex engine semantics

**The regex engine supports lookahead, lookbehind and backreferences** (behaves like
`fancy-regex`, NOT the plain Rust `regex` crate — despite the README/help implying
"Rust-regex-compatible"):

- `a(?=b)`, `a(?!b)`, `(?<=a)b`, `(?<!a)b` all work.
- Backreferences work: `(a)\1` matches `aa`; named: `(?P<w>ab)(?P=w)` and
  `(?P<w>ab)\k<w>` both match `abab`.
- Both named-group syntaxes work: `(?P<n>a)` and `(?<n>a)`.
- Duplicate group names are accepted: `(?P<n>a)(?P<n>a)` matches `aa`.
- `\b` word boundary, `\w`, `\d`, `\p{Greek}` (Unicode properties) work.
- `\w` is Unicode-aware: `\w+` on `héllo w0rld` matches `héllo` and `w0rld`.
- `(?i)` inline case-insensitive flag works and is Unicode-aware:
  `(?i)été` matches both `ÉTÉ` and `été`.
- `(?s)` dotall works: `(?s)a.b` matches `a\nb`.
- `(?m)` multiline works (see anchors).
- `(?-u)` (disabling Unicode) is rejected:
  ```
  Error: Failed building regex

  Caused by:
      Invalid regex: Parsing error at position 3: Disabling Unicode not supported
  ```
  (position 3 = index of `u` in `(?-u)...`)

### Invalid regex errors (verbatim, stderr, exit code 1, stdout empty)

Two error families exist. Format is an anyhow-style chain:

Pattern `(`:
```
Error: Failed building regex

Caused by:
    Invalid regex: Parsing error at position 1: Opening parenthesis without closing parenthesis
```

Pattern `a**`:
```
Error: Failed building regex

Caused by:
    Invalid regex: Parsing error at position 2: Target of repeat operator is invalid
```

Patterns `a{2,1}` and `[z-a]` (delegated to the inner regex crate):
```
Error: Failed building regex

Caused by:
    Invalid regex: Error compiling regex: Regex error: error parsing pattern 0
```

Exact bytes: `Error: Failed building regex\n\nCaused by:\n    Invalid regex: ...\n`
(4-space indent before `Invalid regex`). Exit code **1**. Nothing on stdout.
No ANSI colors even when stderr is a TTY.

### Anchors

- `^`/`$` without `(?m)`: match start/end of the ENTIRE input only.
  - `^foo` on `foo\nbar\nfoo\n` → replaces only the first `foo`.
  - `bar$` on `foo bar\n` → NO match (`$` does not match before a trailing `\n`).
- `(?m)^foo` on `foo\nbar\nfoo\n` → matches both `foo`s.
- `(?m)bar$` on `foo bar\n` → matches.
- CRLF: `ar$` and even `(?m)ar$` do NOT match `foo\r\nbar\r\n` (the `\r` sits before
  the `\n`). `(?m)ar\r$` DOES match.
- `\A` matches start of input. `\z` matches absolute end of input (NOT before trailing
  newline): `bar\z` matches `foo\nbar` but not `foo\nbar\n`.

### Empty matches are discarded

Any match of length 0 is completely ignored — it produces no scope, no replacement,
no output line in `--only-matching`, and does not count for `--fail-any`/`--fail-none`:

- `x*` on `abc\n` with replacement `X` → output `abc\n` unchanged.
- Empty pattern `''` on `abc\n` → unchanged. `--only-matching ''` prints nothing.
- `(?=(aa))` on `aaaa` with replacement `[$1]` → `aaaa` unchanged (zero-width overall
  matches ignored even though group 1 is non-empty; no overlapping trick possible).
- `.*` on `abc\n` → `X\n`: `.*` matches `abc` (0–3); the empty match at position 3 is
  discarded. `.*` on input `\n` → output `\n` unchanged (only empty matches).
- `--fail-none '' -- 'X'` on `foo\n` → fails with "No input was in scope" (empty
  matches don't count). `--fail-any 'x*' -- 'X'` on `abc\n` → exit 0.

### Matching / overlapping behavior

- Leftmost-first, non-overlapping, matching resumes after the end of the previous match:
  - `aa` on `aaaa\n` → `XX`; `aa` on `aaa\n` → `Xa`.
- `.` matches any single Unicode scalar value except `\n`: `.` on `a😀b\n` → `XXX`
  (the 4-byte emoji is one match). `.` does not match `\n` (unless `(?s)`).
- Default scope `.*` on `ab\ncd\n` → `X\nX\n` (per-line runs; newline never matched;
  interstitial empty matches discarded).

---

## 2. Literal-string mode (`-L` / `--literal-string`, env `LITERAL_STRING`)

- Scope is matched as a literal byte string: `-L 'a.c'` on `a.c abc a*c` → `X abc a*c`.
- Case-sensitive: `-L 'foo'` on `Foo FOO foo` replaces only the last.
- Regex-special characters need no escaping: `-L 'a(b'` works.
- Literal may contain newlines: `-L 'b\nc'` (actual newline) on `ab\ncd\n` → `aXd\n`.
- Empty literal `-L '' -- 'X'` → no-op, input unchanged, exit 0 (consistent with
  empty matches being discarded).
- Non-overlapping, left to right: `-L 'aa'` on `aaaa` → `XX`.
- In `-L` mode, replacement variables are NOT expanded — there are no capture groups,
  and even `$0` stays literal: `-L 'foo' -- '[$0]'` on `foo foo` → `[$0] [$0]`.
  Same for `$1` → literal. (Escape sequences like `\n` in the replacement ARE still
  interpreted in `-L` mode.)
- `-L` without a scope argument:
  ```
  error: The following required argument was not provided: scope

  Usage: srgn [OPTIONS] [SCOPE] [-- <REPLACEMENT>]

  For more information, try '--help'.
  ```
  Exit 2. (Note: custom message, lowercase `scope`, and usage says `srgn`, unlike
  clap-generated errors which say `executable` — see §7.)

---

## 3. Replacement action (`-- <REPLACEMENT>`, env `REPLACE`)

- Must follow a literal `--`: `srgn 'o' 'X'` fails with
  `error: unexpected argument 'X' found` (exit 2). Everything after `--` is positional,
  so flags must come before `--`: `--upper 'o' -- 'x'`.
- `REPLACE` env var supplies the replacement if the positional is absent
  (`REPLACE='X' srgn 'o'` works; `REPLACE=''` deletes matches).
- Runs BEFORE all other actions: `--upper 'o' -- 'x'` on `foo` → `fXX`;
  `--lower '(?i)o' -- 'X'` on `Foo` → `Fxx`.
- Subsequent composable actions run in a fixed pipeline order independent of CLI flag
  order (observed: replacement → upper → lower → titlecase; `-t -u` and `-u -t` both
  yield `Hello` from `hello`; `-u -l` and `-l -u` both yield lowercase).
- Non-participating / undefined variables raise errors and abort (see below).

### Variables

- `$0` / `${0}` = entire match. `$1`, `$2`, ... numbered groups; `${1}` equivalent.
- `$name` / `${name}` for named groups (both `(?P<>)` and `(<>)` syntaxes).
- Parsing after `$`:
  - digits are consumed greedily: `$10` = variable `10` (NOT `$1`+`0`); use `${1}0`.
  - a digit-run stops at the first non-digit: `$1abc` = `$1` + literal `abc`.
  - names consume `[A-Za-z0-9_]` greedily: `$n_2`, `$n2` are whole names.
  - `$$` = literal dollar sign: `-- '$$1'` → literal `$1` per match.
  - a lone trailing `$` is literal: `-- 'a$'` → `a$`.
  - `${}` (empty braces) is left literal: `-- '[${}]'` → `[${}]`.
  - `${1x}` or unclosed `${1` / `${b` → error "Mismatched braces" (below).
- `\1`-style backrefs in the replacement are NOT supported (invalid escape, below).

### Undefined variable error (verbatim, stderr, exit 1, stdout empty)

```
Error: Error applying: Error in an action: Action failed in replacement: Error in variable expressions: Undefined variable, unable to substitute: '3'
```
(same text with `'nope'` for `$nope`/`${nope}`; `'10'` for `$10`).

A group that EXISTS in the pattern but did not participate in the current match also
raises this: `(a)|(x)` with replacement `[$2]` on `ab` → error `... substitute: '2'`,
exit 1, stdout empty (processing aborts; partial results are not printed).

Mismatched braces (verbatim):
```
Error: Error applying: Error in an action: Action failed in replacement: Error in variable expressions: Mismatched braces for variable: '1'
```
(raised for `${1x}`, `${1` (unclosed), `a${b`; variable name shown is the consumed prefix).

### Escape sequences in the replacement string

Interpreted at "replacement string build" time, before matching. Verified valid set:

| escape | result |
|---|---|
| `\n` | newline (0x0A) |
| `\t` | tab |
| `\r` | carriage return |
| `\f` | form feed (0x0C) |
| `\b` | backspace (0x08) |
| `\\` | backslash |
| `\"` | `"` |
| `\'` | `'` |

Invalid escapes — `\0`, `\a`, `\v`, `\e`, `\x`, `\␣` (backslash-space), `\$`, `\-`,
`\1` (any backslash-digit) — abort before any processing with (stderr, exit 1,
stdout empty):
```
Error: Failed building replacement string

Caused by:
    Contains invalid escape sequences: 'a\xb'
```
(the whole original replacement string is quoted). Note `$$` (not `\$`) is the
dollar escape. An actual newline byte inside the replacement argument is fine.

---

## 4. `--only-matching` and `--line-numbers` output formats (exact)

Both are hidden flags. They reformat the OUTPUT (whether search results or
action-modified content) and do NOT suppress the "No actions specified" error (§6).

Line numbers are 1-based. Column ranges are **0-based byte offsets, end-exclusive,
relative to the start of each line** (bytes, not chars: in `héllo wörld`, `o` is
range `5-6`; in `a😀b`, `b` is `5-6`). Multiple ranges on one line are `;`-separated,
in ascending order, adjacent ranges allowed (`1-2;2-3`). If a match includes the
trailing `\n`, the range covers it (pattern `\n` on `ab\n` → range `2-3`).

### Piped (stdout not a TTY) — machine-readable

General shape: `(stdin):[<LINE>:]<RANGES>:<LINE-CONTENT>` per output line, where the
line content is printed raw (including its own trailing `\n`; no trailing newline is
added if the input lacks one).

- `--only-matching 'o'` on `hello world\n`:
  ```
  (stdin):4-5;7-8:hello world
  ```
  Only lines containing ≥1 (non-empty) match are printed.
- `--line-numbers 'o'` on the same:
  ```
  (stdin):1:4-5;7-8:hello world
  ```
  `--line-numbers` prints ALL lines; non-matching lines get an EMPTY range field:
  input `foo bar\nbaz qux\n` with scope `foo`:
  ```
  (stdin):1:0-3:foo bar
  (stdin):2::baz qux
  ```
  (note `2::` — empty ranges between the two colons). An empty input line prints as
  `(stdin):2::` followed by its newline.
- Both flags: line number + only matching lines:
  ```
  (stdin):1:0-3:foo bar
  ```
- With an action, the CONTENT is post-action and the RANGES are post-action byte
  ranges of where the scoped content ended up:
  `--only-matching 'foo' -- 'X'` on `foo bar\nbaz qux\n` → `(stdin):0-1:X bar`
  (range `0-1`, not `0-3`). `'a+|b+' -- 'X'` on `aaa bbb` → `(stdin):0-1;2-3:X X`.
- Multi-line matches are split per line: `--only-matching 'b\nc'` on `ab\ncd\n`:
  ```
  (stdin):1-3:ab
  (stdin):0-1:cd
  ```
  (range `1-3` on line 1 covers `b` plus the `\n`).
- Deletion yields empty post-action ranges: `--only-matching -d 'foo'` prints NOTHING
  for `foo bar foo\n`; `--line-numbers -d 'foo'` prints `(stdin):1:: bar \n`... exact
  bytes: `(stdin):1:: bar ` + `\n` (content is the post-deletion line ` bar `).
- In search mode (language scope), piped output uses the same format with the range
  being the in-scope portion of each printed line; only in-scope lines are printed:
  `--python 'def'` on `def f():\n    pass\n\nx = 1\n`:
  ```
  (stdin):1:0-8:def f():
  (stdin):2:0-8:    pass
  ```
- The `(stdin)` label is literal when reading stdin; with `-G` file processing the
  filename is used (file mode itself is out of scope here).

### TTY stdout — human-readable

Detected via `isatty`; force with `--stdout-detection force-tty|force-pipe`.
**No ANSI color codes are ever emitted** (verified with `script -qec`).

- `--only-matching 'foo'` (TTY, no action): prints only MATCHING LINES, whole line,
  no prefix, no ranges: `foo bar`.
- `--line-numbers 'foo'` (TTY): prints ALL lines as `N:<content>`:
  `1:foo bar`, `2:baz qux`.
- Both flags (TTY): `1:foo bar` (only matching lines, numbered).
- With actions (TTY): same line filtering; content is the modified line:
  `--only-matching 'o' -- 'X'` on `hello world` → `hellX wXrld`;
  `--line-numbers 'o' --upper` → `1:hellO wOrld`.
- Search mode (language scope) on TTY: `N:<line>` for each in-scope line:
  `1:def f():`, `2:    pass`.

---

## 5. `--fail-any` / `--fail-none`

- `--fail-any`, something in scope: stderr `Error: Error applying: Some input was in scope`,
  exit **1**, stdout EMPTY (normal output is suppressed entirely).
- `--fail-any`, nothing in scope: normal output, exit 0.
- `--fail-none`, nothing in scope: stderr `Error: Error applying: No input was in scope`,
  exit **1**, stdout empty.
- `--fail-none`, something in scope: normal output, exit 0.
- Both flags: fail-any wins when there is a match, fail-none when there isn't.
- "In scope" means at least one NON-EMPTY match (see §1): patterns `''` or `x*`
  producing only empty matches count as "nothing in scope".
- Default scope `.*` on EMPTY input counts as nothing in scope (`--fail-none` fires).
- Works identically in search mode (language scope) and with no action at all
  (the "No actions specified" ERROR log line is still emitted first in that case).
- **Search mode implies fail-none**: `--python 'def'` (no actions) with no matches on
  stdin exits 1 with `Error: Error applying: No input was in scope` — even without
  `--fail-none`. The same input WITH an action (`--python 'def' --upper`) exits 0 and
  returns the input unchanged. Regex `--only-matching` with no match (no language
  scope) exits 0 silently (aside from the §6 log line).

---

## 6. The "No actions specified" ERROR log line

Exact format (stderr, single line, LF-terminated):

```
[2026-08-08T10:23:20.912848Z ERROR srgn] No actions specified, and not in search mode. Will return input unchanged, if any.
```

- Timestamp: RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 UTC with 6 fractional second digits and `Z`
  (`[%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%6fZ ERROR srgn] `). This is a tracing-style log line;
  the level field is padded to 5 chars (`INFO  srgn` at lower levels).
- Emitted at log level ERROR; base level comes from `RUST_LOG` (default `error`), so
  `RUST_LOG=off` suppresses it. `-v` flags raise verbosity from the base.
- **Emitted when**: reading stdin (or files), NO action is given, and no language
  scope is given (i.e. not search mode). The input is then echoed unchanged to stdout
  and the exit code is still 0. Also emitted with `--only-matching` / `--line-numbers`
  (they are output formatters, NOT actions and NOT search mode).
- **Suppressed by**: any of replacement (`-- 'X'` incl. empty string and env
  `REPLACE`), `-u/--upper`, `-l/--lower`, `-t/--titlecase`, `-n/--normalize`,
  `-g/--german`, `-S/--symbols`, `-d/--delete`, or any language scope
  (`--python`, `--rust`, ...; search mode).
- **QUIRK**: `-s/--squeeze` alone does NOT suppress the line — it is emitted even
  though squeeze does run and modifies the output (`-s 'o'` on `fooo` → `fo` plus the
  ERROR line). Combining `-s` with any composable action (`-s -u`) suppresses it.
- Also emitted when the input is empty ("...if any.").

A second stderr ERROR line exists for file mode: when stdin is piped AND `-G` is
given, stdin wins:
```
[... ERROR srgn] Detected stdin, and request for files: will use stdin and ignore files.
```

---

## 7. Exit codes & clap usage errors

- `0` — success (including no-match with actions, no-action passthrough).
- `1` — runtime errors, always `Error: <message>` on stderr (anyhow chain format
  with `Caused by:` blocks where applicable), stdout empty:
  invalid regex, invalid replacement escapes, undefined/mismatched variables,
  fail-any/fail-none, invalid UTF-8 input.
- `2` — CLI/usage errors from clap, on stderr, format:
  ```
  error: unexpected argument '--bogus' found

  Usage: executable [OPTIONS] [SCOPE] [-- <REPLACEMENT>]

  For more information, try '--help'.
  ```
  Other examples: `-d` without scope:
  ```
  error: the following required arguments were not provided:
    <SCOPE>

  Usage: executable --delete <SCOPE> [-- <REPLACEMENT>]
  ```
  `-d` combined with other actions:
  ```
  error: the argument '--delete' cannot be used with:
    [REPLACEMENT]
    --upper
    --lower
    --titlecase
    --normalize
    --german
    --symbols
  ```
  `-s -d`:
  ```
  error: the argument '--squeeze' cannot be used with '--delete'
  ```
  (Note `-s` IS composable with everything except `-d` — `-s -u 'o'` and
  `-s 'o' -- 'X'` both work, replacement running first, despite the help text calling
  squeeze "only usable alone".)
- Invalid UTF-8 on stdin: `Error: I/O error: stream did not contain valid UTF-8`,
  exit 1, stdout empty.

---

## 8. Input handling edge cases

- Input is read from stdin to EOF as UTF-8 text; processed as ONE string (newlines
  included) — regexes can match across lines.
- **No trailing newline**: preserved byte-for-byte; srgn never adds one.
  `printf 'foo bar' | srgn 'bar' -- 'X'` → `foo X` (no newline). `--only-matching`
  output likewise ends without newline: `(stdin):4-7:foo bar`.
- Empty input: actions exit 0 with empty stdout (`.*` matches only empties → nothing
  to do). No-action passthrough emits the §6 ERROR line and exits 0.
- CRLF: `\r` is an ordinary character (lines are split on `\n` only). Output preserves
  `\r\n`. `--line-numbers` on `foo\r\nbar\r\n`:
  ```
  (stdin):1::foo\r\n
  (stdin):2:0-3:bar\r\n
  ```
  i.e. the `\r` is part of the printed line content. `$`/`(?m)$` match only before
  `\n`, so `bar$` does not match a CRLF line (need `bar\r$`).
- Unicode/emoji: matching and ranges are byte-based; regex chars are Unicode scalar
  values (see §1, §4).
- Env vars: every action flag has an env equivalent (`UPPER`, `LOWER`, `REPLACE`, ...);
  boolean envs must be exactly `true`/`false` (`UPPER=1` → clap error exit 2:
  `error: invalid value '1' for '--upper'\n  [possible values: true, false]`).

## 9. Composition / intersection of scopes

- Regex scope INTERSECTS with language scopes (actions apply only where both agree):
  `--python 'def' 'o' -- 'O'` uppercases... replaces `o` only inside `def` blocks:
  `def foo():\n    x = 1\n\ndef bar():\n    y = 2\n` → `def fOO():` (rest unchanged).
  `--python 'strings' 'o' -- 'O'` touches only `o`s inside string literals.
- `-j/--join-language-scopes` ORs multiple language scopes but never affects the
  regex scope, which always intersects (per `--help`).
- Multiple regex matches within scope are each replaced independently, in one
  left-to-right pass (no re-scanning of replaced text).

## 10. Handy verified input→output table

| command (stdin piped) | stdout | exit |
|---|---|---|
| `echo 'Hello World!' \| srgn '[wW]orld' -- 'there'` | `Hello there!` | 0 |
| `echo 'Hello World!' \| srgn '[wW]orld'` | `Hello World!` (+ ERROR log on stderr) | 0 |
| `echo 'foo' \| srgn -u 'o'` | `fOO` | 0 |
| `printf 'foo\n' \| srgn -d 'foo'` | `\n` | 0 |
| `printf 'foo bar foo\n' \| srgn -d 'foo'` | ` bar \n` | 0 |
| `printf 'fooooo bar\n' \| srgn -s 'o'` | `fo bar` (+ ERROR log) | 0 |
| `printf 'hello world\n' \| srgn -t '\w+'` | `Hello World` | 0 |
| `printf 'café\n' \| srgn -n 'café'` | `cafe` (NFD + marks dropped) | 0 |
| `printf 'a != b\n' \| srgn -S '!='` | `a ≠ b` | 0 |
| `printf 'foo\n' \| srgn '(f)(o+)' -- '[$0][$1][$2][${1}]'` | `[foo][f][oo][f] bar`... (on `foo bar`) | 0 |
| `printf 'aaaa\n' \| srgn 'aa' -- 'X'` | `XX` | 0 |
| `printf 'abc\n' \| srgn 'x*' -- 'X'` | `abc` | 0 |
| `printf 'foo\n' \| srgn '(?=(o))' -- '[$1]'` | `foo` (zero-width ignored) | 0 |
| `printf 'foo\n' \| srgn '(f)o' -- '$3'` | (stderr Undefined variable '3') | 1 |
| `printf 'foo\n' \| srgn 'o' -- 'a\nb'` | `fa\nba\nb` (escapes interpreted) | 0 |
| `printf 'foo\n' \| srgn --fail-any 'foo' -- 'X'` | (stderr Some input was in scope) | 1 |
| `printf 'foo\n' \| srgn --fail-none 'zzz' -- 'X'` | (stderr No input was in scope) | 1 |
