display.content:
# srgn core-engine behavioral specification

Binary under test: `srgn 0.14.1` (`/workspace/executable --version` → `srgn 0.14.1`).
All probes used stdin piping. Invocation shape: `srgn [OPTIONS] [SCOPE] [-- <REPLACEMENT>]`.
Default `SCOPE` is `.*`.

Note on flags: `--only-matching` and `--line-numbers` exist and work but are **hidden**
(do not appear in `-h` or `--help`). `-o` does NOT exist (clap error, exit 2).
`--count` does NOT exist (exit 2).

---

## 1. Regex engine semantics

**The regex engine supports lookahead, lookbehind and backreferences** (behaves like
`fancy-regex`, NOT the plain Rust `regex` crate — despite the README/help implying
"Rust-regex-compatible"):

- `a(?=b)`, `a(?!b)`, `(?<=a)b`, `(?<!a)b` all work.
- Backreferences work: `(a)\1` matches `aa`; named: `(?P<w>ab)(?P=w)` and
  `(?P<w>ab)\k<w>` both match `abab`.
- Both named-group syntaxes work: `(?P<n>a)` and `(?<n>a)`.
- Duplicate group names are accepted: `(?P<n>a)(?P<n>a)` matches `aa`.
- `\b` word boundary, `\w`, `\d`, `\p{Greek}` (Unicode properties) work.
- `\w` is Unicode-aware: `\w+` on `héllo w0rld` matches `héllo` and `w0rld`.
- `(?i)` inline case-insensitive flag works and is Unicode-aware:
  `(?i)été` matches both `ÉTÉ` and `été`.
- `(?s)` dotall works: `(?s)a.b` matches `a\nb`.
- `(?m)` multiline works (see anchors).
- `(?-u)` (disabling Unicode) is rejected:
  ```
  Error: Failed building regex

  Caused by:
      Invalid regex: Parsing error at position 3: Disabling Unicode not supported
  ```
  (position 3 = index of `u` in `(?-u)...`)

### Invalid regex errors (verbatim, stderr, exit code 1, stdout empty)

Two error families exist. Format is an anyhow-style chain:

Pattern `(`:
```
Error: Failed building regex

Caused by:
    Invalid regex: Parsing error at position 1: Opening parenthesis without closing parenthesis
```

Pattern `a**`:
```
Error: Failed building regex

Caused by:
    Invalid regex: Parsing error at position 2: Target of repeat operator is invalid
```

Patterns `a{2,1}` and `[z-a]` (delegated to the inner regex crate):
```
Error: Failed building regex

Caused by:
    Invalid regex: Error compiling regex: Regex error: error parsing pattern 0
```

Exact bytes: `Error: Failed building regex\n\nCaused by:\n    Invalid regex: ...\n`
(4-space indent before `Invalid regex`). Exit code **1**. Nothing on stdout.
No ANSI colors even when stderr is a TTY.

### Anchors

- `^`/`$` without `(?m)`: match start/end of the ENTIRE input only.
  - `^foo` on `foo\nbar\nfoo\n` → replaces only the first `foo`.
  - `bar$` on `foo bar\n` → NO match (`$` does not match before a trailing `\n`).
- `(?m)^foo` on `foo\nbar\nfoo\n` → matches both `foo`s.
- `(?m)bar$` on `foo bar\n` → matches.
- CRLF: `ar$` and even `(?m)ar$` do NOT match `foo\r\nbar\r\n` (the `\r` sits before
  the `\n`). `(?m)ar\r$` DOES match.
- `\A` matches start of input. `\z` matches absolute end of input (NOT before trailing
  newline): `bar\z` matches `foo\nbar` but not `foo\nbar\n`.

### Empty matches are discarded

Any match of length 0 is completely ignored — it produces no scope, no replacement,
no output line in `--only-matching`, and does not count for `--fail-any`/`--fail-none`:

- `x*` on `abc\n` with replacement `X` → output `abc\n` unchanged.
- Empty pattern `''` on `abc\n` → unchanged. `--only-matching ''` prints nothing.
- `(?=(aa))` on `aaaa` with replacement `[$1]` → `aaaa` unchanged (zero-width overall
  matches ignored even though group 1 is non-empty; no overlapping trick possible).
- `.*` on `abc\n` → `X\n`: `.*` matches `abc` (0–3); the empty match at position 3 is
  discarded. `.*` on input `\n` → output `\n` unchanged (only empty matches).
- `--fail-none '' -- 'X'` on `foo\n` → fails with "No input was in scope" (empty
  matches don't count). `--fail-any 'x*' -- 'X'` on `abc\n` → exit 0.

### Matching / overlapping behavior

- Leftmost-first, non-overlapping, matching resumes after the end of the previous match:
  - `aa` on `aaaa\n` → `XX`; `aa` on `aaa\n` → `Xa`.
- `.` matches any single Unicode scalar value except `\n`: `.` on `a😀b\n` → `XXX`
  (the 4-byte emoji is one match). `.` does not match `\n` (unless `(?s)`).
- Default scope `.*` on `ab\ncd\n` → `X\nX\n` (per-line runs; newline never matched;
  interstitial empty matches discarded).

---

## 2. Literal-string mode (`-L` / `--literal-string`, env `LITERAL_STRING`)

- Scope is matched as a literal byte string: `-L 'a.c'` on `a.c abc a*c` → `X abc a*c`.
- Case-sensitive: `-L 'foo'` on `Foo FOO foo` replaces only the last.
- Regex-special characters need no escaping: `-L 'a(b'` works.
- Literal may contain newlines: `-L 'b\nc'` (actual newline) on `ab\ncd\n` → `aXd\n`.
- Empty literal `-L '' -- 'X'` → no-op, input unchanged, exit 0 (consistent with
  empty matches being discarded).
- Non-overlapping, left to right: `-L 'aa'` on `aaaa` → `XX`.
- In `-L` mode, replacement variables are NOT expanded — there are no capture groups,
  and even `$0` stays literal: `-L 'foo' -- '[$0]'` on `foo foo` → `[$0] [$0]`.
  Same for `$1` → literal. (Escape sequences like `\n` in the replacement ARE still
  interpreted in `-L` mode.)
- `-L` without a scope argument:
  ```
  error: The following required argument was not provided: scope

  Usage: srgn [OPTIONS] [SCOPE] [-- <REPLACEMENT>]

  For more information, try '--help'.
  ```
  Exit 2. (Note: custom message, lowercase `scope`, and usage says `srgn`, unlike
  clap-generated errors which say `executable` — see §7.)

---

## 3. Replacement action (`-- <REPLACEMENT>`, env `REPLACE`)

- Must follow a literal `--`: `srgn 'o' 'X'` fails with
  `error: unexpected argument 'X' found` (exit 2). Everything after `--` is positional,
  so flags must come before `--`: `--upper 'o' -- 'x'`.
- `REPLACE` env var supplies the replacement if the positional is absent
  (`REPLACE='X' srgn 'o'` works; `REPLACE=''` deletes matches).
- Runs BEFORE all other actions: `--upper 'o' -- 'x'` on `foo` → `fXX`;
  `--lower '(?i)o' -- 'X'` on `Foo` → `Fxx`.
- Subsequent composable actions run in a fixed pipeline order independent of CLI flag
  order (observed: replacement → upper → lower → titlecase; `-t -u` and `-u -t` both
  yield `Hello` from `hello`; `-u -l` and `-l -u` both yield lowercase).
- Non-participating / undefined variables raise errors and abort (see below).

### Variables

- `$0` / `${0}` = entire match. `$1`, `$2`, ... numbered groups; `${1}` equivalent.
- `$name` / `${name}` for named groups (both `(?P<>)` and `(<>)` syntaxes).
- Parsing after `$`:
  - digits are consumed greedily: `$10` = variable `10` (NOT `$1`+`0`); use `${1}0`.
  - a digit-run stops at the first non-digit: `$1abc` = `$1` + literal `abc`.
  - names consume `[A-Za-z0-9_]` greedily: `$n_2`, `$n2` are whole names.
  - `$$` = literal dollar sign: `-- '$$1'` → literal `$1` per match.
  - a lone trailing `$` is literal: `-- 'a$'` → `a$`.
  - `${}` (empty braces) is left literal: `-- '[${}]'` → `[${}]`.
  - `${1x}` or unclosed `${1` / `${b` → error "Mismatched braces" (below).
- `\1`-style backrefs in the replacement are NOT supported (invalid escape, below).

### Undefined variable error (verbatim, stderr, exit 1, stdout empty)

```
Error: Error applying: Error in an action: Action failed in replacement: Error in variable expressions: Undefined variable, unable to substitute: '3'
```
(same text with `'nope'` for `$nope`/`${nope}`; `'10'` for `$10`).

A group that EXISTS in the pattern but did not participate in the current match also
raises this: `(a)|(x)` with replacement `[$2]` on `ab` → error `... substitute: '2'`,
exit 1, stdout empty (processing aborts; partial results are not printed).

Mismatched braces (verbatim):
```
Error: Error applying: Error in an action: Action failed in replacement: Error in variable expressions: Mismatched braces for variable: '1'
```
(raised for `${1x}`, `${1` (unclosed), `a${b`; variable name shown is the consumed prefix).

### Escape sequences in the replacement string

Interpreted at "replacement string build" time, before matching. Verified valid set:

| escape | result |
|---|---|
| `\n` | newline (0x0A) |
| `\t` | tab |
| `\r` | carriage return |
| `\f` | form feed (0x0C) |
| `\b` | backspace (0x08) |
| `\\` | backslash |
| `\"` | `"` |
| `\'` | `'` |

Invalid escapes — `\0`, `\a`, `\v`, `\e`, `\x`, `\␣` (backslash-space), `\$`, `\-`,
`\1` (any backslash-digit) — abort before any processing with (stderr, exit 1,
stdout empty):
```
Error: Failed building replacement string

Caused by:
    Contains invalid escape sequences: 'a\xb'
```
(the whole original replacement string is quoted). Note `$$` (not `\$`) is the
dollar escape. An actual newline byte inside the replacement argument is fine.

---

## 4. `--only-matching` and `--line-numbers` output formats (exact)

Both are hidden flags. They reformat the OUTPUT (whether search results or
action-modified content) and do NOT suppress the "No actions specified" error (§6).

Line numbers are 1-based. Column ranges are **0-based byte offsets, end-exclusive,
relative to the start of each line** (bytes, not chars: in `héllo wörld`, `o` is
range `5-6`; in `a😀b`, `b` is `5-6`). Multiple ranges on one line are `;`-separated,
in ascending order, adjacent ranges allowed (`1-2;2-3`). If a match includes the
trailing `\n`, the range covers it (pattern `\n` on `ab\n` → range `2-3`).

### Piped (stdout not a TTY) — machine-readable

General shape: `(stdin):[<LINE>:]<RANGES>:<LINE-CONTENT>` per output line, where the
line content is printed raw (including its own trailing `\n`; no trailing newline is
added if the input lacks one).

- `--only-matching 'o'` on `hello world\n`:
  ```
  (stdin):4-5;7-8:hello world
  ```
  Only lines containing ≥1 (non-empty) match are printed.
- `--line-numbers 'o'` on the same:
  ```
  (stdin):1:4-5;7-8:hello world
  ```
  `--line-numbers` prints ALL lines; non-matching lines get an EMPTY range field:
  input `foo bar\nbaz qux\n` with scope `foo`:
  ```
  (stdin):1:0-3:foo bar
  (stdin):2::baz qux
  ```
  (note `2::` — empty ranges between the two colons). An empty input line prints as
  `(stdin):2::` followed by its newline.
- Both flags: line number + only matching lines:
  ```
  (stdin):1:0-3:foo bar
  ```
- With an action, the CONTENT is post-action and the RANGES are post-action byte
  ranges of where the scoped content ended up:
  `--only-matching 'foo' -- 'X'` on `foo bar\nbaz qux\n` → `(stdin):0-1:X bar`
  (range `0-1`, not `0-3`). `'a+|b+' -- 'X'` on `aaa bbb` → `(stdin):0-1;2-3:X X`.
- Multi-line matches are split per line: `--only-matching 'b\nc'` on `ab\ncd\n`:
  ```
  (stdin):1-3:ab
  (stdin):0-1:cd
  ```
  (range `1-3` on line 1 covers `b` plus the `\n`).
- Deletion yields empty post-action ranges: `--only-matching -d 'foo'` prints NOTHING
  for `foo bar foo\n`; `--line-numbers -d 'foo'` prints `(stdin):1:: bar \n`... exact
  bytes: `(stdin):1:: bar ` + `\n` (content is the post-deletion line ` bar `).
- In search mode (language scope), piped output uses the same format with the range
  being the in-scope portion of each printed line; only in-scope lines are printed:
  `--python 'def'` on `def f():\n    pass\n\nx = 1\n`:
  ```
  (stdin):1:0-8:def f():
  (stdin):2:0-8:    pass
  ```
- The `(stdin)` label is literal when reading stdin; with `-G` file processing the
  filename is used (file mode itself is out of scope here).

### TTY stdout — human-readable

Detected via `isatty`; force with `--stdout-detection force-tty|force-pipe`.
**No ANSI color codes are ever emitted** (verified with `script -qec`).

- `--only-matching 'foo'` (TTY, no action): prints only MATCHING LINES, whole line,
  no prefix, no ranges: `foo bar`.
- `--line-numbers 'foo'` (TTY): prints ALL lines as `N:<content>`:
  `1:foo bar`, `2:baz qux`.
- Both flags (TTY): `1:foo bar` (only matching lines, numbered).
- With actions (TTY): same line filtering; content is the modified line:
  `--only-matching 'o' -- 'X'` on `hello world` → `hellX wXrld`;
  `--line-numbers 'o' --upper` → `1:hellO wOrld`.
- Search mode (language scope) on TTY: `N:<line>` for each in-scope line:
  `1:def f():`, `2:    pass`.

---

## 5. `--fail-any` / `--fail-none`

- `--fail-any`, something in scope: stderr `Error: Error applying: Some input was in scope`,
  exit **1**, stdout EMPTY (normal output is suppressed entirely).
- `--fail-any`, nothing in scope: normal output, exit 0.
- `--fail-none`, nothing in scope: stderr `Error: Error applying: No input was in scope`,
  exit **1**, stdout empty.
- `--fail-none`, something in scope: normal output, exit 0.
- Both flags: fail-any wins when there is a match, fail-none when there isn't.
- "In scope" means at least one NON-EMPTY match (see §1): patterns `''` or `x*`
  producing only empty matches count as "nothing in scope".
- Default scope `.*` on EMPTY input counts as nothing in scope (`--fail-none` fires).
- Works identically in search mode (language scope) and with no action at all
  (the "No actions specified" ERROR log line is still emitted first in that case).
- **Search mode implies fail-none**: `--python 'def'` (no actions) with no matches on
  stdin exits 1 with `Error: Error applying: No input was in scope` — even without
  `--fail-none`. The same input WITH an action (`--python 'def' --upper`) exits 0 and
  returns the input unchanged. Regex `--only-matching` with no match (no language
  scope) exits 0 silently (aside from the §6 log line).

---

## 6. The "No actions specified" ERROR log line

Exact format (stderr, single line, LF-terminated):

```
[2026-08-08T10:23:20.912848Z ERROR srgn] No actions specified, and not in search mode. Will return input unchanged, if any.
```

- Timestamp: RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 UTC with 6 fractional second digits and `Z`
  (`[%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%6fZ ERROR srgn] `). This is a tracing-style log line;
  the level field is padded to 5 chars (`INFO  srgn` at lower levels).
- Emitted at log level ERROR; base level comes from `RUST_LOG` (default `error`), so
  `RUST_LOG=off` suppresses it. `-v` flags raise verbosity from the base.
- **Emitted when**: reading stdin (or files), NO action is given, and no language
  scope is given (i.e. not search mode). The input is then echoed unchanged to stdout
  and the exit code is still 0. Also emitted with `--only-matching` / `--line-numbers`
  (they are output formatters, NOT actions and NOT search mode).
- **Suppressed by**: any of replacement (`-- 'X'` incl. empty string and env
  `REPLACE`), `-u/--upper`, `-l/--lower`, `-t/--titlecase`, `-n/--normalize`,
  `-g/--german`, `-S/--symbols`, `-d/--delete`, or any language scope
  (`--python`, `--rust`, ...; search mode).
- **QUIRK**: `-s/--squeeze` alone does NOT suppress the line — it is emitted even
  though squeeze does run and modifies the output (`-s 'o'` on `fooo` → `fo` plus the
  ERROR line). Combining `-s` with any composable action (`-s -u`) suppresses it.
- Also emitted when the input is empty ("...if any.").

A second stderr ERROR line exists for file mode: when stdin is piped AND `-G` is
given, stdin wins:
```
[... ERROR srgn] Detected stdin, and request for files: will use stdin and ignore files.
```

---

## 7. Exit codes & clap usage errors

- `0` — success (including no-match with actions, no-action passthrough).
- `1` — runtime errors, always `Error: <message>` on stderr (anyhow chain format
  with `Caused by:` blocks where applicable), stdout empty:
  invalid regex, invalid replacement escapes, undefined/mismatched variables,
  fail-any/fail-none, invalid UTF-8 input.
- `2` — CLI/usage errors from clap, on stderr, format:
  ```
  error: unexpected argument '--bogus' found

  Usage: executable [OPTIONS] [SCOPE] [-- <REPLACEMENT>]

  For more information, try '--help'.
  ```
  Other examples: `-d` without scope:
  ```
  error: the following required arguments were not provided:
    <SCOPE>

  Usage: executable --delete <SCOPE> [-- <REPLACEMENT>]
  ```
  `-d` combined with other actions:
  ```
  error: the argument '--delete' cannot be used with:
    [REPLACEMENT]
    --upper
    --lower
    --titlecase
    --normalize
    --german
    --symbols
  ```
  `-s -d`:
  ```
  error: the argument '--squeeze' cannot be used with '--delete'
  ```
  (Note `-s` IS composable with everything except `-d` — `-s -u 'o'` and
  `-s 'o' -- 'X'` both work, replacement running first, despite the help text calling
  squeeze "only usable alone".)
- Invalid UTF-8 on stdin: `Error: I/O error: stream did not contain valid UTF-8`,
  exit 1, stdout empty.

---

## 8. Input handling edge cases

- Input is read from stdin to EOF as UTF-8 text; processed as ONE string (newlines
  included) — regexes can match across lines.
- **No trailing newline**: preserved byte-for-byte; srgn never adds one.
  `printf 'foo bar' | srgn 'bar' -- 'X'` → `foo X` (no newline). `--only-matching`
  output likewise ends without newline: `(stdin):4-7:foo bar`.
- Empty input: actions exit 0 with empty stdout (`.*` matches only empties → nothing
  to do). No-action passthrough emits the §6 ERROR line and exits 0.
- CRLF: `\r` is an ordinary character (lines are split on `\n` only). Output preserves
  `\r\n`. `--line-numbers` on `foo\r\nbar\r\n`:
  ```
  (stdin):1::foo\r\n
  (stdin):2:0-3:bar\r\n
  ```
  i.e. the `\r` is part of the printed line content. `$`/`(?m)$` match only before
  `\n`, so `bar$` does not match a CRLF line (need `bar\r$`).
- Unicode/emoji: matching and ranges are byte-based; regex chars are Unicode scalar
  values (see §1, §4).
- Env vars: every action flag has an env equivalent (`UPPER`, `LOWER`, `REPLACE`, ...);
  boolean envs must be exactly `true`/`false` (`UPPER=1` → clap error exit 2:
  `error: invalid value '1' for '--upper'\n  [possible values: true, false]`).

## 9. Composition / intersection of scopes

- Regex scope INTERSECTS with language scopes (actions apply only where both agree):
  `--python 'def' 'o' -- 'O'` uppercases... replaces `o` only inside `def` blocks:
  `def foo():\n    x = 1\n\ndef bar():\n    y = 2\n` → `def fOO():` (rest unchanged).
  `--python 'strings' 'o' -- 'O'` touches only `o`s inside string literals.
- `-j/--join-language-scopes` ORs multiple language scopes but never affects the
  regex scope, which always intersects (per `--help`).
- Multiple regex matches within scope are each replaced independently, in one
  left-to-right pass (no re-scanning of replaced text).

## 10. Handy verified input→output table

| command (stdin piped) | stdout | exit |
|---|---|---|
| `echo 'Hello World!' \| srgn '[wW]orld' -- 'there'` | `Hello there!` | 0 |
| `echo 'Hello World!' \| srgn '[wW]orld'` | `Hello World!` (+ ERROR log on stderr) | 0 |
| `echo 'foo' \| srgn -u 'o'` | `fOO` | 0 |
| `printf 'foo\n' \| srgn -d 'foo'` | `\n` | 0 |
| `printf 'foo bar foo\n' \| srgn -d 'foo'` | ` bar \n` | 0 |
| `printf 'fooooo bar\n' \| srgn -s 'o'` | `fo bar` (+ ERROR log) | 0 |
| `printf 'hello world\n' \| srgn -t '\w+'` | `Hello World` | 0 |
| `printf 'café\n' \| srgn -n 'café'` | `cafe` (NFD + marks dropped) | 0 |
| `printf 'a != b\n' \| srgn -S '!='` | `a ≠ b` | 0 |
| `printf 'foo\n' \| srgn '(f)(o+)' -- '[$0][$1][$2][${1}]'` | `[foo][f][oo][f] bar`... (on `foo bar`) | 0 |
| `printf 'aaaa\n' \| srgn 'aa' -- 'X'` | `XX` | 0 |
| `printf 'abc\n' \| srgn 'x*' -- 'X'` | `abc` | 0 |
| `printf 'foo\n' \| srgn '(?=(o))' -- '[$1]'` | `foo` (zero-width ignored) | 0 |
| `printf 'foo\n' \| srgn '(f)o' -- '$3'` | (stderr Undefined variable '3') | 1 |
| `printf 'foo\n' \| srgn 'o' -- 'a\nb'` | `fa\nba\nb` (escapes interpreted) | 0 |
| `printf 'foo\n' \| srgn --fail-any 'foo' -- 'X'` | (stderr Some input was in scope) | 1 |
| `printf 'foo\n' \| srgn --fail-none 'zzz' -- 'X'` | (stderr No input was in scope) | 1 |

args.content:
# srgn — Python language scopes (`--python` / `--py`, `--python-query`, `--python-query-file`)

Behavioral specification derived purely from black-box observation of the binary
(`srgn 0.14.1`). All examples were run against stdin. `§` is used below as a visible
marker: the command `srgn --python <SCOPE> '.*' -- '§$0§'` wraps every regex match in
`§...§`, which reveals the exact character ranges the language scope selects.

Conventions used throughout:

- `PROG` = the binary under test.
- Unless noted, commands exit `0` and print nothing to stderr.
- The regex scope (first positional) defaults to `.*`.

---

## 1. Global mechanics that matter for every scope

### 1.1 How scopes + regex + replacement interact

- The language scope produces a set of character ranges. The regex scope is then applied
  *within* those ranges only (language scope ∩ regex scope, always intersection — `-j`
  does **not** affect the regex scope).
- Replacement `'§$0§'` wraps each regex match individually. `$0` is the whole match;
  `$1`, `$2`, ... / `$NAME` reference capture groups
  (verified: `srgn --python strings '(hello) (world)' -- '[$2|$1]'` on `x = "hello world"`
  → `x = "[world|hello]"`).
- The regex engine is multi-line aware **within** a scope range: `\n` in the pattern
  matches newlines inside a multi-line scope, but `.` does **not** match `\n`
  (dotall off). Example: docstring `"""ab\ncd"""` with pattern `ab.cd` → no match;
  pattern `line1\n` inside a docstring matches `line1\n` including the newline.
- With pattern `.*` applied to a multi-line scope, each line is matched separately
  (one replacement per line). Empty matches are **not** replaced: blank lines inside a
  multi-line string stay blank (no `§§`), and `a = ""` under `--python strings '.*'
  -- '§$0§'` stays `a = ""`.
- Unicode/emoji content works transparently. Offsets printed in search mode are **byte
  offsets** (see §6): `    ééage = 1` (é = 2 bytes) gives range `8-11` for `age`.

### 1.2 Multiple `--python` scopes: sequential re-parsing (CRITICAL, non-obvious)

Multiple language scopes do **not** intersect as raw character ranges. Instead they are
applied **left to right, sequentially**: the text selected by the first scoper is
**re-parsed as a fresh, standalone Python source**, and the next scoper runs on that
text. Consequences (all verified):

- `--python strings --python strings` on `x = "s"` → **nothing** (the content `s`,
  re-parsed, contains no string). Same for `doc-strings`, `imports`, `types`,
  `function-names`, `function-calls`, `globals`, `variable-identifiers`,
  `class-methods`, `static-methods`, `methods` applied after a scoper that strips the
  syntactic context they need.
- Self-intersection **is** non-empty for scopers whose selected text re-parses to the
  same construct: `comments`, `identifiers`, `with`, `try`, `lambda`, `def`,
  `async-def`, `class`.
  - `# hi` → comments∩comments = `# hi` ✓
  - `foo = 1` → identifiers∩identifiers = `foo` ✓
  - `class A:\n    pass` → class∩class = whole class ✓
- `--python strings --python comments` on `x = "# inner"` → matches `# inner`
  (string content re-parsed as code yields a comment).
- `--python comments --python strings` on `# a "str in comment"` → **nothing**
  (re-parsed comment text is still just a comment; the quotes inside are not a string
  node).
- `--python strings --python strings` **does** match on `x = '''"nested"'''`
  (content `"nested"` re-parses to a string): output `x = '''"§nested§"'''`.
- `--python strings --python def` on `x = "def f():\n    pass"` matches the whole
  content. Each scope region is re-parsed **independently**: with
  `s1 = "def f():"` / `s2 = "    pass"`, only `s1`'s content matches `def`.
- Order matters: `--python class --python def` finds defs inside classes, but
  `--python methods --python class` finds nothing (method text contains no class).
- `--python def --python class` on a class nested inside a def works:
  `def f():\n    class C:\n        pass` → class body wrapped.
- `--python def --python methods` → empty (method re-parsed at top level is not a
  method).
- `--python-query` behaves the same way: two successive queries intersect via re-parse
  (`(identifier) @a` twice on `x = 1` still matches `x`; `(assignment) @a` then
  `(integer) @b` matches `1`).

### 1.3 `-j` / `--join-language-scopes`

- Joins all language scopes (logical OR) instead of sequential intersection. Order of
  the flags then does not matter.
- Overlapping regions are de-duplicated (acted on once):
  `--python strings --python doc-strings -j` wraps a docstring's content once, not twice.
- Example: `x = "s" # c` + `with a:\n    pass` under `-j` with
  `strings, comments, with` → `x = "§s§" §# c§` and the whole `with` block wrapped.
- No effect when only one language scope is given; never affects the regex scope.

### 1.4 No `~` dynamic syntax for Python

Unlike `--go`/`--rust`, `--python 'class~Foo'` is rejected at argument-parse time,
exit code `2`, stderr verbatim:

```
error: invalid value 'class~Foo' for '--python <PYTHON>'
  [possible values: comments, strings, imports, doc-strings, function-names, function-calls, class, def, async-def, methods, class-methods, static-methods, with, try, lambda, globals, variable-identifiers, types, identifiers]

  tip: a similar value exists: 'class'

For more information, try '--help'.
```

(`def~top` likewise, with `tip: a similar value exists: 'def'`.)

Any other unknown value, e.g. `--python bogus`, exits `2` with:

```
error: invalid value 'bogus' for '--python <PYTHON>'
  [possible values: comments, strings, imports, doc-strings, function-names, function-calls, class, def, async-def, methods, class-methods, static-methods, with, try, lambda, globals, variable-identifiers, types, identifiers]

For more information, try '--help'.
```

(note: no `tip:` line when there is no similar value).

### 1.5 Alias and env var

- `--py` is an alias of `--python` (verified `--py strings`).
- Env var `PYTHON=strings` is honored (`PYTHON=strings srgn '.*' -- '§$0§'` works).

---

## 2. The 19 prepared queries — exact scoped ranges

The fixture (abbreviated `F`) used for most of these:

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python
# A top comment
import os
import sys as system
from collections import OrderedDict
from . import sibling
from pkg.sub import thing as alias, other

GLOBAL_VAR = 42
global_string = "hello"

def top_func(x: int, y: str = "default") -> bool:
    """Docstring of top_func."""
    local = x + 1
    return True

async def top_async(a, b):
    "Doc of async."
    await b

@decorator
class MyClass(BaseClass):
    """Class docstring.

    Multi-line docstring body.
    """

    class_attr: float = 3.14

    def __init__(self):
        self.age = 0

    @classmethod
    def make(cls, val):
        return cls()

    @staticmethod
    def helper(x):
        return x * 2

    def method(self, s: str) -> None:
        # method comment
        result = helper("inner")
        def nested():
            pass
        with open("f.txt") as f:
            data = f.read()
        try:
            risky()
        except ValueError as e:
            handle(e)
        finally:
            cleanup()
        fn = lambda z: z + 1
        return result

call_result = top_func(1, "two")
x = MyClass()
```

### 2.1 `comments`
- Range: the entire comment **including** `#`, **excluding** leading whitespace.
- The shebang line `#!/usr/bin/env python` is a comment.
- Example: `    # method comment` → `    §# method comment§`; `x = "s" # cmt` →
  `x = "s" §# cmt§`.

### 2.2 `strings`
- Range: string **content only — quotes are excluded**, for every flavor:
  `'...'`, `"..."`, `'''...'''`, `"""..."""`, `r"..."`, `b"..."`, `rb"..."`, `f"..."`.
- Docstrings are strings too (content matched under `strings` regardless of quote style).
- f-strings: only the literal parts are in scope; interpolations `{expr}` are excluded.
  `f"fstring {name} end"` → `f"§fstring §{name}§ end§"`. A string *inside* an
  interpolation is its own string node and is matched: `f"nested {d['key']} done"` →
  `f"§nested §{d['§key§']}§ done§"`.
- Implicit concatenation: each literal scoped separately: `"concat" "adjacent"` →
  `"§concat§" "§adjacent§"`.
- Empty string `""` has empty content; nothing is ever matched/replaced there.
- Prefixes (`r`, `b`, `u`, `f`, combinations, any case) stay outside the scope;
  only content between the quotes is scoped. Escape sequences are not special:
  `r"raw \n string"` → `r"§raw \n string§"`.

### 2.3 `imports`
- Range: the **module path only**, including periods; never the imported names,
  aliases, `import`/`from`/`as` keywords, or `*`.
- `import os` → `os`; `import sys as system` → `sys` only;
  `import a, b.c` → `a` and `b.c`; `import os.path` → `os.path`;
  `from collections import OrderedDict` → `collections` only;
  `from . import sibling` → `.` (the bare dot is matched);
  `from pkg.sub import thing as alias, other` → `pkg.sub` only;
  `from x import (y, z)` → `x` only; `from mod import *` → `mod` only (not `*`).

### 2.4 `doc-strings`
- Range: content only (quotes excluded), but **only** for strings that:
  1. are a bare `expression_statement` (a string alone on its own statement —
     position does **not** matter: module level, class level, function level, inside
     `if` blocks, and even *non-first* statements all match), and
  2. open with **exactly `"""`** (triple double quote).
- NOT matched: `'...'`, `"..."`, `'''...'''` docstrings (any position); any prefixed
  form — `r"""..."""`, `f"""..."""`, `u"""..."""`, `b"""..."""`, `R"""..."""` are all
  excluded; strings used as values (`x = """..."""`, `["""..."""]`, `print("""...""")`);
  implicit concatenations `"""a""" """b"""` (a `concatenated_string`, not a `string`).
- Verified examples (fix3): `"""Module docstring triple-double."""` matches;
  `"""Module string, not first."""` (after `x = 1`) matches; both first and second
  `"""..."""` expression statements inside a function/class match;
  `"""inside if block"""` inside an `if` body matches.

### 2.5 `function-names`
- Range: just the name identifier at the definition site, for **all** `def`s —
  top-level, nested, async, and methods (incl. `__init__`, classmethod, staticmethod).
  `def §top_func§(...)`, `async def §top_async§(...)`, `def §nested§():` etc.

### 2.6 `function-calls`
- Range: the callee name, **only when the callee is a bare identifier**. Arguments are
  never included.
- Matched: `§helper§("inner")`, `§open§("f.txt")`, `§cls§()`, `§top_func§(1, "two")`,
  `§MyClass§()`, `§f§(x=1, *a, **k)`, and the inner call in `(§get_thing§())()`.
- NOT matched: attribute calls (`obj.method(1)`, `a.b.c("x")`, `mod.sub.func()`,
  `f.read()`), subscript calls (`d['key']()`, `lst[0](1)`), calls of parenthesized
  expressions.

### 2.7 `class`
- Range: from the `class` keyword through the **entire body** (everything: docstring,
  attributes, methods with their decorators, nested classes, comments), excluding the
  class's own decorator lines and excluding the trailing newline.
- Example: in `F`, `§class MyClass(BaseClass):§` ... every body line wrapped down to
  `§        return result§`; the `@decorator` line and the blank line after the class
  are outside.
- Nested classes are included as part of the outer class body.
- Deleting (`-d`) a class leaves the newlines of its lines behind:
  `class A:\n    pass\n\ny = 1\n` → `\n\n\ny = 1\n`.

### 2.8 `def`
- Range: from the `def`/`async def` keyword through the entire body; **includes async
  defs**; **excludes decorator lines**; includes nested defs (as part of the outer
  body). Verified: `@dec\ndef decorated_free():\n    def inner():\n        pass` →
  `@dec` untouched, everything from `def` on wrapped.

### 2.9 `async-def`
- Range: entire `async def` block, top-level or inside classes; decorators excluded.

### 2.10 `methods`
- Range: function definitions **directly inside a `class` body** — including async
  methods and — unlike `def`/`class-methods`/`static-methods` — **including their
  decorator lines** (all of them, any decorator).
- Nested functions inside a free function are NOT methods.
  `@other_decorator\n    def decorated_method(self):` → both lines wrapped.

### 2.11 `class-methods`
- Range: `def` block decorated with a **bare identifier** `@classmethod` anywhere in the
  decorator stack; **decorator lines excluded** (starts at `def`).
- NOT matched: `@classmethod(arg)` (call form), `@a.classmethod` (attribute form).

### 2.12 `static-methods`
- Same as 2.11 for `@staticmethod`.

### 2.13 `with`
- Range: the entire `with` statement including body; `async with` included.
  `§with open("f.txt") as f:§\n§            data = f.read()§`.

### 2.14 `try`
- Range: the entire `try` statement including all `except` clauses, `else`, and
  `finally` — from `try:` through the end of the last clause's body.

### 2.15 `lambda`
- Range: from the `lambda` keyword through the end of the body expression.
  `fn = §lambda z: z + 1§`; defaults/varargs included: `g = §lambda x=1, *a: x§`.

### 2.16 `globals`
- Range: the **name identifier only** (not the value) of module-level simple and
  annotated assignments: `§GLOBAL_VAR§ = 42`, `§attr§: int`, `§ann§: str = "v"`.
- Chained assignment `a = b = 1`: only the **first/outermost** target `a` is a global
  (contrast `variable-identifiers`, which marks both).
- NOT globals: assignments inside any block (functions, loops, `if`, `with`, ...),
  augmented `e += 3`, tuple/list destructuring, `obj.attr = 1`, walrus.

### 2.17 `variable-identifiers`
- Range: name identifiers on the left-hand side of **any** simple or annotated
  assignment, at any nesting level: module level, in functions, in `with`/`try` bodies.
- Chained `a = b = 1` marks **both** `§a§` and `§b§`. Bare annotation `§attr§: int`
  counts.
- NOT matched: tuple/list destructuring (`c, d = 1, 2`, `(f, g) = ...`, `[h, i] = ...`),
  augmented assignment (`e += 3`), walrus (`m := 5`), `for j in ...`, `with ... as fh`,
  `except ... as exc`, function parameters, attribute targets (`obj.attr = 1`),
  `global` declarations (the later assignment `glob_decl = 1` inside the function **is**
  matched, though it is not a `globals` match).

### 2.18 `types`
- Range: the **entire type annotation expression** in parameter annotations, return
  annotations, and variable annotations: `x: §int§`, `-> §bool§`,
  `a: §List[int]§`, `-> §dict[str, int]§`, `c: §tuple[int, ...]§`, `f: §int | str§`,
  `e: §typing.Final§`, and even quoted annotations including their quotes:
  `d: §"quoted hint"§`.
- NOT matched: base classes / class keyword args (`class Generic(MyBase[int],
  metaclass=Meta)` — nothing).

### 2.19 `identifiers`
- Range: every `identifier` token — variable names, function names (def and call
  sites), class names, parameter names, attribute names (`§self§.§age§` — both parts),
  decorator names (`§classmethod§`), imported names and aliases (`import §sys§ as
  §system§`, `from §pkg§.§sub§ import §thing§ as §alias§, §other§`), `except ValueError
  as §e§`, lambda parameters, etc.
- NOT identifiers: `True`, `False`, `None`, keywords, operators, literals.

---

## 3. Syntax errors in the Python input

- Tree-sitter parses with error recovery; **no error is reported**, exit code stays `0`,
  and scoping proceeds on the partially-recovered tree.
- `def broken(:\n    pass\nx = 1\n` under `--python identifiers`:
  `def §broken§(:\n    pass\n§x§ = 1\n` — the broken def's name is still found.
- Under `--python def`, the broken def still scopes (search mode shows both lines).
- Totally unparseable input `}{](` under `--python strings '.*' -- '§$0§'` →
  input echoed unchanged, exit `0`.

## 4. `--python-query` / `--python-query-file`

- `--python-query '(identifier) @foo'` on `foo = bar(1)` → `§foo§ = §bar§(1)`.
  Capture name is irrelevant; every capture of the query is scoped.
- Multiple captures in one query all count:
  `[(identifier) @a (string) @b]` on `foo = "bar"` → `§foo§ = §"bar"§`
  (note: for a custom query the **whole `string` node including quotes** is scoped —
  quote-stripping is a feature of the prepared `strings` query only).
- A query with **no captures** (`(identifier)`) silently matches nothing, exit `0`.
- `--python-query` may be repeated; successive queries intersect via re-parse (§1.2).
- `--python-query-file q.scm` reads the query from a file (works). Missing file:
  stderr `Error: I/O error: No such file or directory (os error 2)`, exit `1`.
- `--python` and `--python-query` are **mutually exclusive** (clap), exit `2`:

```
error: the argument '--python <PYTHON>' cannot be used with '--python-query <TREE-SITTER-QUERY-VALUE>'

Usage: executable --python <PYTHON> <SCOPE> -- <REPLACEMENT>

For more information, try '--help'.
```

- Invalid node type, stderr verbatim, exit `1`:

```
Error: Error occurred while creating a tree-sitter query: Query error at 1:2. Invalid node type nonexistent_node
```

- Unbalanced parens / invalid query syntax, stderr verbatim, exit `1` (note the caret
  rendering and trailing newline structure):

```
Error: Error occurred while creating a tree-sitter query: Query error at 1:4. Invalid syntax:
(((
   ^
```

## 5. Replacement / deletion mode (stdout is the full modified input)

- Full input is echoed with replacements applied; exit `0` even when nothing matched.
- No trailing newline in input → none added in output
  (`x = "hi"` → `x = "X"` exactly, no `\n`).
- CRLF line endings are preserved byte-for-byte.
- With `--only-matching` **plus** a replacement, output becomes annotated lines:
  `x = "hi" and "yo"` under `--python strings --only-matching '.*' -- 'X'` gives

```
(stdin):5-6;13-14:x = "X" and "X"
```

  i.e. `(stdin):` + semicolon-separated byte ranges of all matches on the line + `:` +
  the modified line.
- `-d` deletes the scoped characters only (newlines remain; see §2.7).

## 6. Search mode output format (language scope, no action)

Search mode activates when a language scope is given and no action is. Only lines
containing at least one in-scope match are printed.

### 6.1 stdin, stdout piped (machine format)

```
(stdin):LINE:START-END:LINE-CONTENT
```

- `LINE` is 1-based. `START-END` are **byte offsets within the line**, half-open.
- `LINE-CONTENT` is the **entire source line** (leading whitespace included), not just
  the match — even with `--only-matching` (which has no visible effect here) or
  `--line-numbers`.
- Multiple matches on one line: ranges joined with `;`:
  `    age = age2` → `(stdin):2:4-7;10-13:    age = age2`.
- A multi-line scope is reported per line, each line getting its own range covering the
  scoped segment (whole line when the scope spans it):
  `--python class` on `class Foo:\n    x = 1\n    y = 2\nz = 3` →

```
(stdin):1:0-10:class Foo:
(stdin):2:0-9:    x = 1
(stdin):3:0-9:    y = 2
```

- Works the same for `--python-query` scopes: `(stdin):1:0-3:foo = 1`.

### 6.2 stdin, stdout is a TTY (human format)

`script -qec` verification — **no ANSI colors** in any mode, and the format changes to
just `LINE:CONTENT` (no `(stdin):`, no ranges):

```
2:    age = 1
```

`--stdout-detection force-tty` / `force-pipe` switch between these two formats
deterministically. TTY output observed through a pty arrives with `\r\n` line endings
(pty line discipline), but srgn itself emits `\n`.

### 6.3 Files (`-G 'files/*.py'`), stdout piped

```
files/b.py:2:4-7:    age = 5
files/a.py:31:13-16:        self.age = 0
```

- Same machine format with the file path instead of `(stdin)`.
- Default file order is **not** sorted (parallel; `b.py` appeared before `a.py`);
  `--sorted` gives lexicographic order.
- If stdin is detected together with `-G`, stderr gets
  `[<timestamp> ERROR srgn] Detected stdin, and request for files: will use stdin and ignore files.`
  and the glob is ignored (then, with empty stdin: `Error: Error applying: No input was
  in scope`, exit `1`).

### 6.4 Files, stdout is a TTY

Filename on its own line, then `LINE:CONTENT` lines, then a blank line; groups repeat
per file:

```
files/b.py
2:    age = 5

files/a.py
31:        self.age = 0

```

### 6.5 No-match / fail conditions in search mode

- Zero final matches (language scope empty, or regex matches nothing within it):
  stderr `Error: Error applying: No input was in scope`, exit `1`.
- `--fail-any` with a match: stderr `Error: Error applying: Some input was in scope`,
  exit `1`.
- `--fail-none` without a match: stderr `Error: Error applying: No input was in scope`,
  exit `1`.

## 7. Input edge cases

- **Empty stdin**, replacement mode: no output, exit `0`.
- **Empty stdin**, search mode: `Error: Error applying: No input was in scope`, exit `1`.
- **Invalid UTF-8** (`x = "hi\xff"`): stderr
  `Error: I/O error: stream did not contain valid UTF-8`, exit `1`, no stdout.
- **CRLF**: preserved exactly in replacement mode; scopes see logical content
  (replacement `x = "hi"\r\n` → `x = "X"\r\n`).
- **No trailing newline**: preserved (not added).
- **Unicode/emoji**: fine; byte offsets in search-mode ranges.

## 8. Non-search mode without actions (regex only, no language scope)

For completeness (core behavior, not Python-specific): a regex scope with no language
scope and no action is *not* search mode. stderr gets a timestamped log line:

```
[2026-08-08T10:26:15.686667Z ERROR srgn] No actions specified, and not in search mode. Will return input unchanged, if any.
```

and the input is echoed unchanged, exit `0`. With `--line-numbers` the echoed lines are
prefixed `(stdin):N:RANGE:` where RANGE is the match range on matching lines and empty
on non-matching lines, e.g. `(stdin):1::foo` / `(stdin):2:0-2:bar`.

## 9. Clap-level errors (exit `2`)

- Unknown `--python` value: see §1.4 (verbatim texts).
- `--python` + `--python-query` together: see §4.
- `--count` does not exist in this build (README is stale): `error: unexpected argument
  '--count' found` + tip about `--c`, usage line, exit `2`.
- Passing two positional replacements (`srgn --python strings -- 's' '§$0§'`):
  `error: the argument '[REPLACEMENT]' cannot be used multiple times`, exit `2`.

## 10. Summary of scope-range rules (quick reference)

| scope | includes | excludes |
|---|---|---|
| comments | `#` char, shebang | leading whitespace |
| strings | content of all string flavors; f-string literal parts | quotes, prefixes, interpolations |
| imports | module path incl. dots (and bare `.`) | imported names, aliases, keywords, `*` |
| doc-strings | content of bare `"""`-only expression-statement strings (any position) | quotes; all other quote styles/prefixes; concatenations |
| function-names | name at def site (all defs incl. async/nested/methods) | everything else |
| function-calls | callee when bare identifier | args; attribute/subscript callees |
| class | `class` keyword + entire body incl. nested classes/method decorators | class decorators, trailing newline |
| def | `def`/`async def` + entire body, nested defs | decorators |
| async-def | `async def` + entire body | decorators |
| methods | defs directly in class body **+ their decorator lines** | nested-inside-method defs (covered via outer) |
| class-methods | `def` block with bare `@classmethod` | decorator lines; `@classmethod(...)`, `@a.classmethod` |
| static-methods | same for `@staticmethod` | same |
| with | entire `with`/`async with` + body | — |
| try | entire `try` + except/else/finally | — |
| lambda | `lambda` through end of body expr | — |
| globals | name of module-level simple/annotated assignment (first target only in chains) | values, block-level, augmented, destructuring |
| variable-identifiers | LHS names of any simple/annotated assignment (all chain targets) | destructuring, augmented, walrus, `as`-targets, params, attributes |
| types | entire annotation expressions (params, returns, variables; quoted hints incl. quotes) | base classes, metaclass args |
| identifiers | every identifier token incl. attributes, aliases | `True`/`False`/`None`, keywords |

display.content:
# srgn — Python language scopes (`--python` / `--py`, `--python-query`, `--python-query-file`)

Behavioral specification derived purely from black-box observation of the binary
(`srgn 0.14.1`). All examples were run against stdin. `§` is used below as a visible
marker: the command `srgn --python <SCOPE> '.*' -- '§$0§'` wraps every regex match in
`§...§`, which reveals the exact character ranges the language scope selects.

Conventions used throughout:

- `PROG` = the binary under test.
- Unless noted, commands exit `0` and print nothing to stderr.
- The regex scope (first positional) defaults to `.*`.

---

## 1. Global mechanics that matter for every scope

### 1.1 How scopes + regex + replacement interact

- The language scope produces a set of character ranges. The regex scope is then applied
  *within* those ranges only (language scope ∩ regex scope, always intersection — `-j`
  does **not** affect the regex scope).
- Replacement `'§$0§'` wraps each regex match individually. `$0` is the whole match;
  `$1`, `$2`, ... / `$NAME` reference capture groups
  (verified: `srgn --python strings '(hello) (world)' -- '[$2|$1]'` on `x = "hello world"`
  → `x = "[world|hello]"`).
- The regex engine is multi-line aware **within** a scope range: `\n` in the pattern
  matches newlines inside a multi-line scope, but `.` does **not** match `\n`
  (dotall off). Example: docstring `"""ab\ncd"""` with pattern `ab.cd` → no match;
  pattern `line1\n` inside a docstring matches `line1\n` including the newline.
- With pattern `.*` applied to a multi-line scope, each line is matched separately
  (one replacement per line). Empty matches are **not** replaced: blank lines inside a
  multi-line string stay blank (no `§§`), and `a = ""` under `--python strings '.*'
  -- '§$0§'` stays `a = ""`.
- Unicode/emoji content works transparently. Offsets printed in search mode are **byte
  offsets** (see §6): `    ééage = 1` (é = 2 bytes) gives range `8-11` for `age`.

### 1.2 Multiple `--python` scopes: sequential re-parsing (CRITICAL, non-obvious)

Multiple language scopes do **not** intersect as raw character ranges. Instead they are
applied **left to right, sequentially**: the text selected by the first scoper is
**re-parsed as a fresh, standalone Python source**, and the next scoper runs on that
text. Consequences (all verified):

- `--python strings --python strings` on `x = "s"` → **nothing** (the content `s`,
  re-parsed, contains no string). Same for `doc-strings`, `imports`, `types`,
  `function-names`, `function-calls`, `globals`, `variable-identifiers`,
  `class-methods`, `static-methods`, `methods` applied after a scoper that strips the
  syntactic context they need.
- Self-intersection **is** non-empty for scopers whose selected text re-parses to the
  same construct: `comments`, `identifiers`, `with`, `try`, `lambda`, `def`,
  `async-def`, `class`.
  - `# hi` → comments∩comments = `# hi` ✓
  - `foo = 1` → identifiers∩identifiers = `foo` ✓
  - `class A:\n    pass` → class∩class = whole class ✓
- `--python strings --python comments` on `x = "# inner"` → matches `# inner`
  (string content re-parsed as code yields a comment).
- `--python comments --python strings` on `# a "str in comment"` → **nothing**
  (re-parsed comment text is still just a comment; the quotes inside are not a string
  node).
- `--python strings --python strings` **does** match on `x = '''"nested"'''`
  (content `"nested"` re-parses to a string): output `x = '''"§nested§"'''`.
- `--python strings --python def` on `x = "def f():\n    pass"` matches the whole
  content. Each scope region is re-parsed **independently**: with
  `s1 = "def f():"` / `s2 = "    pass"`, only `s1`'s content matches `def`.
- Order matters: `--python class --python def` finds defs inside classes, but
  `--python methods --python class` finds nothing (method text contains no class).
- `--python def --python class` on a class nested inside a def works:
  `def f():\n    class C:\n        pass` → class body wrapped.
- `--python def --python methods` → empty (method re-parsed at top level is not a
  method).
- `--python-query` behaves the same way: two successive queries intersect via re-parse
  (`(identifier) @a` twice on `x = 1` still matches `x`; `(assignment) @a` then
  `(integer) @b` matches `1`).

### 1.3 `-j` / `--join-language-scopes`

- Joins all language scopes (logical OR) instead of sequential intersection. Order of
  the flags then does not matter.
- Overlapping regions are de-duplicated (acted on once):
  `--python strings --python doc-strings -j` wraps a docstring's content once, not twice.
- Example: `x = "s" # c` + `with a:\n    pass` under `-j` with
  `strings, comments, with` → `x = "§s§" §# c§` and the whole `with` block wrapped.
- No effect when only one language scope is given; never affects the regex scope.

### 1.4 No `~` dynamic syntax for Python

Unlike `--go`/`--rust`, `--python 'class~Foo'` is rejected at argument-parse time,
exit code `2`, stderr verbatim:

```
error: invalid value 'class~Foo' for '--python <PYTHON>'
  [possible values: comments, strings, imports, doc-strings, function-names, function-calls, class, def, async-def, methods, class-methods, static-methods, with, try, lambda, globals, variable-identifiers, types, identifiers]

  tip: a similar value exists: 'class'

For more information, try '--help'.
```

(`def~top` likewise, with `tip: a similar value exists: 'def'`.)

Any other unknown value, e.g. `--python bogus`, exits `2` with:

```
error: invalid value 'bogus' for '--python <PYTHON>'
  [possible values: comments, strings, imports, doc-strings, function-names, function-calls, class, def, async-def, methods, class-methods, static-methods, with, try, lambda, globals, variable-identifiers, types, identifiers]

For more information, try '--help'.
```

(note: no `tip:` line when there is no similar value).

### 1.5 Alias and env var

- `--py` is an alias of `--python` (verified `--py strings`).
- Env var `PYTHON=strings` is honored (`PYTHON=strings srgn '.*' -- '§$0§'` works).

---

## 2. The 19 prepared queries — exact scoped ranges

The fixture (abbreviated `F`) used for most of these:

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python
# A top comment
import os
import sys as system
from collections import OrderedDict
from . import sibling
from pkg.sub import thing as alias, other

GLOBAL_VAR = 42
global_string = "hello"

def top_func(x: int, y: str = "default") -> bool:
    """Docstring of top_func."""
    local = x + 1
    return True

async def top_async(a, b):
    "Doc of async."
    await b

@decorator
class MyClass(BaseClass):
    """Class docstring.

    Multi-line docstring body.
    """

    class_attr: float = 3.14

    def __init__(self):
        self.age = 0

    @classmethod
    def make(cls, val):
        return cls()

    @staticmethod
    def helper(x):
        return x * 2

    def method(self, s: str) -> None:
        # method comment
        result = helper("inner")
        def nested():
            pass
        with open("f.txt") as f:
            data = f.read()
        try:
            risky()
        except ValueError as e:
            handle(e)
        finally:
            cleanup()
        fn = lambda z: z + 1
        return result

call_result = top_func(1, "two")
x = MyClass()
```

### 2.1 `comments`
- Range: the entire comment **including** `#`, **excluding** leading whitespace.
- The shebang line `#!/usr/bin/env python` is a comment.
- Example: `    # method comment` → `    §# method comment§`; `x = "s" # cmt` →
  `x = "s" §# cmt§`.

### 2.2 `strings`
- Range: string **content only — quotes are excluded**, for every flavor:
  `'...'`, `"..."`, `'''...'''`, `"""..."""`, `r"..."`, `b"..."`, `rb"..."`, `f"..."`.
- Docstrings are strings too (content matched under `strings` regardless of quote style).
- f-strings: only the literal parts are in scope; interpolations `{expr}` are excluded.
  `f"fstring {name} end"` → `f"§fstring §{name}§ end§"`. A string *inside* an
  interpolation is its own string node and is matched: `f"nested {d['key']} done"` →
  `f"§nested §{d['§key§']}§ done§"`.
- Implicit concatenation: each literal scoped separately: `"concat" "adjacent"` →
  `"§concat§" "§adjacent§"`.
- Empty string `""` has empty content; nothing is ever matched/replaced there.
- Prefixes (`r`, `b`, `u`, `f`, combinations, any case) stay outside the scope;
  only content between the quotes is scoped. Escape sequences are not special:
  `r"raw \n string"` → `r"§raw \n string§"`.

### 2.3 `imports`
- Range: the **module path only**, including periods; never the imported names,
  aliases, `import`/`from`/`as` keywords, or `*`.
- `import os` → `os`; `import sys as system` → `sys` only;
  `import a, b.c` → `a` and `b.c`; `import os.path` → `os.path`;
  `from collections import OrderedDict` → `collections` only;
  `from . import sibling` → `.` (the bare dot is matched);
  `from pkg.sub import thing as alias, other` → `pkg.sub` only;
  `from x import (y, z)` → `x` only; `from mod import *` → `mod` only (not `*`).

### 2.4 `doc-strings`
- Range: content only (quotes excluded), but **only** for strings that:
  1. are a bare `expression_statement` (a string alone on its own statement —
     position does **not** matter: module level, class level, function level, inside
     `if` blocks, and even *non-first* statements all match), and
  2. open with **exactly `"""`** (triple double quote).
- NOT matched: `'...'`, `"..."`, `'''...'''` docstrings (any position); any prefixed
  form — `r"""..."""`, `f"""..."""`, `u"""..."""`, `b"""..."""`, `R"""..."""` are all
  excluded; strings used as values (`x = """..."""`, `["""..."""]`, `print("""...""")`);
  implicit concatenations `"""a""" """b"""` (a `concatenated_string`, not a `string`).
- Verified examples (fix3): `"""Module docstring triple-double."""` matches;
  `"""Module string, not first."""` (after `x = 1`) matches; both first and second
  `"""..."""` expression statements inside a function/class match;
  `"""inside if block"""` inside an `if` body matches.

### 2.5 `function-names`
- Range: just the name identifier at the definition site, for **all** `def`s —
  top-level, nested, async, and methods (incl. `__init__`, classmethod, staticmethod).
  `def §top_func§(...)`, `async def §top_async§(...)`, `def §nested§():` etc.

### 2.6 `function-calls`
- Range: the callee name, **only when the callee is a bare identifier**. Arguments are
  never included.
- Matched: `§helper§("inner")`, `§open§("f.txt")`, `§cls§()`, `§top_func§(1, "two")`,
  `§MyClass§()`, `§f§(x=1, *a, **k)`, and the inner call in `(§get_thing§())()`.
- NOT matched: attribute calls (`obj.method(1)`, `a.b.c("x")`, `mod.sub.func()`,
  `f.read()`), subscript calls (`d['key']()`, `lst[0](1)`), calls of parenthesized
  expressions.

### 2.7 `class`
- Range: from the `class` keyword through the **entire body** (everything: docstring,
  attributes, methods with their decorators, nested classes, comments), excluding the
  class's own decorator lines and excluding the trailing newline.
- Example: in `F`, `§class MyClass(BaseClass):§` ... every body line wrapped down to
  `§        return result§`; the `@decorator` line and the blank line after the class
  are outside.
- Nested classes are included as part of the outer class body.
- Deleting (`-d`) a class leaves the newlines of its lines behind:
  `class A:\n    pass\n\ny = 1\n` → `\n\n\ny = 1\n`.

### 2.8 `def`
- Range: from the `def`/`async def` keyword through the entire body; **includes async
  defs**; **excludes decorator lines**; includes nested defs (as part of the outer
  body). Verified: `@dec\ndef decorated_free():\n    def inner():\n        pass` →
  `@dec` untouched, everything from `def` on wrapped.

### 2.9 `async-def`
- Range: entire `async def` block, top-level or inside classes; decorators excluded.

### 2.10 `methods`
- Range: function definitions **directly inside a `class` body** — including async
  methods and — unlike `def`/`class-methods`/`static-methods` — **including their
  decorator lines** (all of them, any decorator).
- Nested functions inside a free function are NOT methods.
  `@other_decorator\n    def decorated_method(self):` → both lines wrapped.

### 2.11 `class-methods`
- Range: `def` block decorated with a **bare identifier** `@classmethod` anywhere in the
  decorator stack; **decorator lines excluded** (starts at `def`).
- NOT matched: `@classmethod(arg)` (call form), `@a.classmethod` (attribute form).

### 2.12 `static-methods`
- Same as 2.11 for `@staticmethod`.

### 2.13 `with`
- Range: the entire `with` statement including body; `async with` included.
  `§with open("f.txt") as f:§\n§            data = f.read()§`.

### 2.14 `try`
- Range: the entire `try` statement including all `except` clauses, `else`, and
  `finally` — from `try:` through the end of the last clause's body.

### 2.15 `lambda`
- Range: from the `lambda` keyword through the end of the body expression.
  `fn = §lambda z: z + 1§`; defaults/varargs included: `g = §lambda x=1, *a: x§`.

### 2.16 `globals`
- Range: the **name identifier only** (not the value) of module-level simple and
  annotated assignments: `§GLOBAL_VAR§ = 42`, `§attr§: int`, `§ann§: str = "v"`.
- Chained assignment `a = b = 1`: only the **first/outermost** target `a` is a global
  (contrast `variable-identifiers`, which marks both).
- NOT globals: assignments inside any block (functions, loops, `if`, `with`, ...),
  augmented `e += 3`, tuple/list destructuring, `obj.attr = 1`, walrus.

### 2.17 `variable-identifiers`
- Range: name identifiers on the left-hand side of **any** simple or annotated
  assignment, at any nesting level: module level, in functions, in `with`/`try` bodies.
- Chained `a = b = 1` marks **both** `§a§` and `§b§`. Bare annotation `§attr§: int`
  counts.
- NOT matched: tuple/list destructuring (`c, d = 1, 2`, `(f, g) = ...`, `[h, i] = ...`),
  augmented assignment (`e += 3`), walrus (`m := 5`), `for j in ...`, `with ... as fh`,
  `except ... as exc`, function parameters, attribute targets (`obj.attr = 1`),
  `global` declarations (the later assignment `glob_decl = 1` inside the function **is**
  matched, though it is not a `globals` match).

### 2.18 `types`
- Range: the **entire type annotation expression** in parameter annotations, return
  annotations, and variable annotations: `x: §int§`, `-> §bool§`,
  `a: §List[int]§`, `-> §dict[str, int]§`, `c: §tuple[int, ...]§`, `f: §int | str§`,
  `e: §typing.Final§`, and even quoted annotations including their quotes:
  `d: §"quoted hint"§`.
- NOT matched: base classes / class keyword args (`class Generic(MyBase[int],
  metaclass=Meta)` — nothing).

### 2.19 `identifiers`
- Range: every `identifier` token — variable names, function names (def and call
  sites), class names, parameter names, attribute names (`§self§.§age§` — both parts),
  decorator names (`§classmethod§`), imported names and aliases (`import §sys§ as
  §system§`, `from §pkg§.§sub§ import §thing§ as §alias§, §other§`), `except ValueError
  as §e§`, lambda parameters, etc.
- NOT identifiers: `True`, `False`, `None`, keywords, operators, literals.

---

## 3. Syntax errors in the Python input

- Tree-sitter parses with error recovery; **no error is reported**, exit code stays `0`,
  and scoping proceeds on the partially-recovered tree.
- `def broken(:\n    pass\nx = 1\n` under `--python identifiers`:
  `def §broken§(:\n    pass\n§x§ = 1\n` — the broken def's name is still found.
- Under `--python def`, the broken def still scopes (search mode shows both lines).
- Totally unparseable input `}{](` under `--python strings '.*' -- '§$0§'` →
  input echoed unchanged, exit `0`.

## 4. `--python-query` / `--python-query-file`

- `--python-query '(identifier) @foo'` on `foo = bar(1)` → `§foo§ = §bar§(1)`.
  Capture name is irrelevant; every capture of the query is scoped.
- Multiple captures in one query all count:
  `[(identifier) @a (string) @b]` on `foo = "bar"` → `§foo§ = §"bar"§`
  (note: for a custom query the **whole `string` node including quotes** is scoped —
  quote-stripping is a feature of the prepared `strings` query only).
- A query with **no captures** (`(identifier)`) silently matches nothing, exit `0`.
- `--python-query` may be repeated; successive queries intersect via re-parse (§1.2).
- `--python-query-file q.scm` reads the query from a file (works). Missing file:
  stderr `Error: I/O error: No such file or directory (os error 2)`, exit `1`.
- `--python` and `--python-query` are **mutually exclusive** (clap), exit `2`:

```
error: the argument '--python <PYTHON>' cannot be used with '--python-query <TREE-SITTER-QUERY-VALUE>'

Usage: executable --python <PYTHON> <SCOPE> -- <REPLACEMENT>

For more information, try '--help'.
```

- Invalid node type, stderr verbatim, exit `1`:

```
Error: Error occurred while creating a tree-sitter query: Query error at 1:2. Invalid node type nonexistent_node
```

- Unbalanced parens / invalid query syntax, stderr verbatim, exit `1` (note the caret
  rendering and trailing newline structure):

```
Error: Error occurred while creating a tree-sitter query: Query error at 1:4. Invalid syntax:
(((
   ^
```

## 5. Replacement / deletion mode (stdout is the full modified input)

- Full input is echoed with replacements applied; exit `0` even when nothing matched.
- No trailing newline in input → none added in output
  (`x = "hi"` → `x = "X"` exactly, no `\n`).
- CRLF line endings are preserved byte-for-byte.
- With `--only-matching` **plus** a replacement, output becomes annotated lines:
  `x = "hi" and "yo"` under `--python strings --only-matching '.*' -- 'X'` gives

```
(stdin):5-6;13-14:x = "X" and "X"
```

  i.e. `(stdin):` + semicolon-separated byte ranges of all matches on the line + `:` +
  the modified line.
- `-d` deletes the scoped characters only (newlines remain; see §2.7).

## 6. Search mode output format (language scope, no action)

Search mode activates when a language scope is given and no action is. Only lines
containing at least one in-scope match are printed.

### 6.1 stdin, stdout piped (machine format)

```
(stdin):LINE:START-END:LINE-CONTENT
```

- `LINE` is 1-based. `START-END` are **byte offsets within the line**, half-open.
- `LINE-CONTENT` is the **entire source line** (leading whitespace included), not just
  the match — even with `--only-matching` (which has no visible effect here) or
  `--line-numbers`.
- Multiple matches on one line: ranges joined with `;`:
  `    age = age2` → `(stdin):2:4-7;10-13:    age = age2`.
- A multi-line scope is reported per line, each line getting its own range covering the
  scoped segment (whole line when the scope spans it):
  `--python class` on `class Foo:\n    x = 1\n    y = 2\nz = 3` →

```
(stdin):1:0-10:class Foo:
(stdin):2:0-9:    x = 1
(stdin):3:0-9:    y = 2
```

- Works the same for `--python-query` scopes: `(stdin):1:0-3:foo = 1`.

### 6.2 stdin, stdout is a TTY (human format)

`script -qec` verification — **no ANSI colors** in any mode, and the format changes to
just `LINE:CONTENT` (no `(stdin):`, no ranges):

```
2:    age = 1
```

`--stdout-detection force-tty` / `force-pipe` switch between these two formats
deterministically. TTY output observed through a pty arrives with `\r\n` line endings
(pty line discipline), but srgn itself emits `\n`.

### 6.3 Files (`-G 'files/*.py'`), stdout piped

```
files/b.py:2:4-7:    age = 5
files/a.py:31:13-16:        self.age = 0
```

- Same machine format with the file path instead of `(stdin)`.
- Default file order is **not** sorted (parallel; `b.py` appeared before `a.py`);
  `--sorted` gives lexicographic order.
- If stdin is detected together with `-G`, stderr gets
  `[<timestamp> ERROR srgn] Detected stdin, and request for files: will use stdin and ignore files.`
  and the glob is ignored (then, with empty stdin: `Error: Error applying: No input was
  in scope`, exit `1`).

### 6.4 Files, stdout is a TTY

Filename on its own line, then `LINE:CONTENT` lines, then a blank line; groups repeat
per file:

```
files/b.py
2:    age = 5

files/a.py
31:        self.age = 0

```

### 6.5 No-match / fail conditions in search mode

- Zero final matches (language scope empty, or regex matches nothing within it):
  stderr `Error: Error applying: No input was in scope`, exit `1`.
- `--fail-any` with a match: stderr `Error: Error applying: Some input was in scope`,
  exit `1`.
- `--fail-none` without a match: stderr `Error: Error applying: No input was in scope`,
  exit `1`.

## 7. Input edge cases

- **Empty stdin**, replacement mode: no output, exit `0`.
- **Empty stdin**, search mode: `Error: Error applying: No input was in scope`, exit `1`.
- **Invalid UTF-8** (`x = "hi\xff"`): stderr
  `Error: I/O error: stream did not contain valid UTF-8`, exit `1`, no stdout.
- **CRLF**: preserved exactly in replacement mode; scopes see logical content
  (replacement `x = "hi"\r\n` → `x = "X"\r\n`).
- **No trailing newline**: preserved (not added).
- **Unicode/emoji**: fine; byte offsets in search-mode ranges.

## 8. Non-search mode without actions (regex only, no language scope)

For completeness (core behavior, not Python-specific): a regex scope with no language
scope and no action is *not* search mode. stderr gets a timestamped log line:

```
[2026-08-08T10:26:15.686667Z ERROR srgn] No actions specified, and not in search mode. Will return input unchanged, if any.
```

and the input is echoed unchanged, exit `0`. With `--line-numbers` the echoed lines are
prefixed `(stdin):N:RANGE:` where RANGE is the match range on matching lines and empty
on non-matching lines, e.g. `(stdin):1::foo` / `(stdin):2:0-2:bar`.

## 9. Clap-level errors (exit `2`)

- Unknown `--python` value: see §1.4 (verbatim texts).
- `--python` + `--python-query` together: see §4.
- `--count` does not exist in this build (README is stale): `error: unexpected argument
  '--count' found` + tip about `--c`, usage line, exit `2`.
- Passing two positional replacements (`srgn --python strings -- 's' '§$0§'`):
  `error: the argument '[REPLACEMENT]' cannot be used multiple times`, exit `2`.

## 10. Summary of scope-range rules (quick reference)

| scope | includes | excludes |
|---|---|---|
| comments | `#` char, shebang | leading whitespace |
| strings | content of all string flavors; f-string literal parts | quotes, prefixes, interpolations |
| imports | module path incl. dots (and bare `.`) | imported names, aliases, keywords, `*` |
| doc-strings | content of bare `"""`-only expression-statement strings (any position) | quotes; all other quote styles/prefixes; concatenations |
| function-names | name at def site (all defs incl. async/nested/methods) | everything else |
| function-calls | callee when bare identifier | args; attribute/subscript callees |
| class | `class` keyword + entire body incl. nested classes/method decorators | class decorators, trailing newline |
| def | `def`/`async def` + entire body, nested defs | decorators |
| async-def | `async def` + entire body | decorators |
| methods | defs directly in class body **+ their decorator lines** | nested-inside-method defs (covered via outer) |
| class-methods | `def` block with bare `@classmethod` | decorator lines; `@classmethod(...)`, `@a.classmethod` |
| static-methods | same for `@staticmethod` | same |
| with | entire `with`/`async with` + body | — |
| try | entire `try` + except/else/finally | — |
| lambda | `lambda` through end of body expr | — |
| globals | name of module-level simple/annotated assignment (first target only in chains) | values, block-level, augmented, destructuring |
| variable-identifiers | LHS names of any simple/annotated assignment (all chain targets) | destructuring, augmented, walrus, `as`-targets, params, attributes |
| types | entire annotation expressions (params, returns, variables; quoted hints incl. quotes) | base classes, metaclass args |
| identifiers | every identifier token incl. attributes, aliases | `True`/`False`/`None`, keywords |

payload.resultSummary:
Spec written to `/workspace/probes/python-scopes.md`. Key findings:

- **Multiple language scopes are NOT set intersections of ranges.** They apply sequentially: each scoper's selected text is **re-parsed as fresh standalone Python** before the next scoper runs. This explains everything: `strings∩strings` is empty (`x = "s"` → content `s` has no string) but works on `'''\"nested\"'''`; `strings→comments` matches `x = "# inner"`; order matters (`methods→class` empty, `class→methods` works). `-j` switches to union with overlap dedup.
- **`strings` scopes content only** (quotes/prefixes excluded) for all flavors; f-string `{interpolations}` excluded, but strings *inside* interpolations match. **`doc-strings` is bizarrely narrow**: only bare `"""`-triple-double-quoted, unprefixed, non-concatenated strings that are standalone expression statements — position irrelevant (`'''`, `"`, `r"""`, `f"""`, assigned/call-arg strings all excluded).
- **`function-calls` matches only bare-identifier callees** (`obj.m()`, `d[k]()` excluded); **`methods` includes decorator lines** while `def`/`class`/`class-methods`/`static-methods` exclude them; `class-methods` requires the bare `@classmethod` form (not `@classmethod(...)` or `@a.classmethod`); `globals` marks only the first target of `a = b = 1` while `variable-identifiers` marks both.
- **No `~` dynamic syntax for Python** — clap rejects with exit 2 (verbatim error recorded).
- **Search-mode format is pipe/TTY-dependent, no colors anywhere**: piped = `(stdin):LINE:BYTE_START-BYTE_END:FULL_LINE` (ranges `;`-joined, byte offsets, `--only-matching` has no effect); TTY = plain `LINE:CONTENT`; with `-G` files piped it's `FILE:LINE:START-END:CONTENT`, TTY groups by filename with blank-line separators. Multi-line scopes emit one annotated line per source line.
- **Errors**: syntax errors in input are silently tolerated (partial tree, exit 0); invalid UTF-8 → `Error: I/O error: stream did not contain valid UTF-8` (exit 1); invalid tree-sitter queries → verbatim `Error: Error occurred while creating a tree-sitter query: ...` (exit 1); no-match in search mode → `Error: Error applying: No input was in scope` (exit 1); `--python` + `--python-query` mutually exclusive (exit 2). Also: empty regex matches are never replaced, CRLF/missing-final-newline preserved, regex `\n` matches across lines within a scope but `.` does not.
