args.content:
# srgn core-engine behavioral specification

(Requested filename was the full area description; it exceeds the 255-byte filename
limit, so this spec lives at `core-engine.md`.)

Binary under test: `srgn 0.14.1` (`/workspace/executable --version` → `srgn 0.14.1`).
All probes used stdin piping. Invocation shape: `srgn [OPTIONS] [SCOPE] [-- <REPLACEMENT>]`.
Default `SCOPE` is `.*`.

Note on flags: `--only-matching` and `--line-numbers` exist and work but are **hidden**
(do not appear in `-h` or `--help`). `-o` does NOT exist (clap error, exit 2).
`--count` does NOT exist (exit 2).

---

## 1. Regex engine semantics

**The regex engine supports lookahead, lookbehind and backreferences** (behaves like
`fancy-regex`, NOT the plain Rust `regex` crate):

- `a(?=b)`, `a(?!b)`, `(?<=a)b`, `(?<!a)b` all work.
- Backreferences work: `(a)\1` matches `aa`; named: `(?P<w>ab)(?P=w)` and
  `(?P<w>ab)\k<w>` both match `abab`.
- Both named-group syntaxes work: `(?P<n>a)` and `(?<n>a)`.
- Duplicate group names are accepted: `(?P<n>a)(?P<n>a)` matches `aa`.
- `\b` word boundary, `\w`, `\d`, `\p{Greek}` (Unicode properties) work.
- `\w` is Unicode-aware: `\w+` on `héllo w0rld` matches `héllo` and `w0rld`.
- `(?i)` inline case-insensitive flag works and is Unicode-aware:
  `(?i)été` matches both `ÉTÉ` and `été`.
- `(?s)` dotall works: `(?s)a.b` matches `a\nb`.
- `(?m)` multiline works (see anchors).
- `(?-u)` (disabling Unicode) is rejected:
  ```
  Error: Failed building regex

  Caused by:
      Invalid regex: Parsing error at position 3: Disabling Unicode not supported
  ```
  (position 3 = index of `u` in `(?-u)...`)

### Invalid regex errors (verbatim, stderr, exit code 1, stdout empty)

Two error families exist. Format is an anyhow-style chain:

Pattern `(`:
```
Error: Failed building regex

Caused by:
    Invalid regex: Parsing error at position 1: Opening parenthesis without closing parenthesis
```

Pattern `a**`:
```
Error: Failed building regex

Caused by:
    Invalid regex: Parsing error at position 2: Target of repeat operator is invalid
```

Patterns `a{2,1}` and `[z-a]` (delegated to the inner regex crate):
```
Error: Failed building regex

Caused by:
    Invalid regex: Error compiling regex: Regex error: error parsing pattern 0
```

Exact bytes: `Error: Failed building regex\n\nCaused by:\n    Invalid regex: ...\n`
(4-space indent before `Invalid regex`). Exit code **1**. Nothing on stdout.
No ANSI colors even when stderr is a TTY.

### Anchors

- `^`/`$` without `(?m)`: match start/end of the ENTIRE input only.
  - `^foo` on `foo\nbar\nfoo\n` → replaces only the first `foo`.
  - `bar$` on `foo bar\n` → NO match (`$` does not match before a trailing `\n`).
- `(?m)^foo` on `foo\nbar\nfoo\n` → matches both `foo`s.
- `(?m)bar$` on `foo bar\n` → matches.
- CRLF: `ar$` and even `(?m)ar$` do NOT match `foo\r\nbar\r\n` (the `\r` sits before
  the `\n`). `(?m)ar\r$` DOES match.
- `\A` matches start of input. `\z` matches absolute end of input (NOT before trailing
  newline): `bar\z` matches `foo\nbar` but not `foo\nbar\n`.

### Empty matches are discarded

Any match of length 0 is completely ignored — it produces no scope, no replacement,
no output line in `--only-matching`, and does not count for `--fail-any`/`--fail-none`:

- `x*` on `abc\n` with replacement `X` → output `abc\n` unchanged.
- Empty pattern `''` on `abc\n` → unchanged. `--only-matching ''` prints nothing.
- `(?=(aa))` on `aaaa` with replacement `[$1]` → `aaaa` unchanged (zero-width overall
  matches ignored even though group 1 is non-empty; no overlapping trick possible).
- `.*` on `abc\n` → `X\n`: `.*` matches `abc` (0–3); the empty match at position 3 is
  discarded. `.*` on input `\n` → output `\n` unchanged (only empty matches).
- `--fail-none '' -- 'X'` on `foo\n` → fails with "No input was in scope" (empty
  matches don't count). `--fail-any 'x*' -- 'X'` on `abc\n` → exit 0.

### Matching / overlapping behavior

- Leftmost-first, non-overlapping, matching resumes after the end of the previous match:
  - `aa` on `aaaa\n` → `XX`; `aa` on `aaa\n` → `Xa`.
- `.` matches any single Unicode scalar value except `\n`: `.` on `a😀b\n` → `XXX`
  (the 4-byte emoji is one match). `.` does not match `\n` (unless `(?s)`).
- Default scope `.*` on `ab\ncd\n` → `X\nX\n` (per-line runs; newline never matched;
  interstitial empty matches discarded).

---

## 2. Literal-string mode (`-L` / `--literal-string`, env `LITERAL_STRING`)

- Scope is matched as a literal byte string: `-L 'a.c'` on `a.c abc a*c` → `X abc a*c`.
- Case-sensitive: `-L 'foo'` on `Foo FOO foo` replaces only the last.
- Regex-special characters need no escaping: `-L 'a(b'` works.
- Literal may contain newlines: `-L 'b\nc'` (actual newline) on `ab\ncd\n` → `aXd\n`.
- Empty literal `-L '' -- 'X'` → no-op, input unchanged, exit 0 (consistent with
  empty matches being discarded).
- Non-overlapping, left to right: `-L 'aa'` on `aaaa` → `XX`.
- In `-L` mode, replacement variables are NOT expanded — there are no capture groups,
  and even `$0` stays literal: `-L 'foo' -- '[$0]'` on `foo foo` → `[$0] [$0]`.
  Same for `$1` → literal. (Escape sequences like `\n` in the replacement ARE still
  interpreted in `-L` mode.)
- `-L` without a scope argument:
  ```
  error: The following required argument was not provided: scope

  Usage: srgn [OPTIONS] [SCOPE] [-- <REPLACEMENT>]

  For more information, try '--help'.
  ```
  Exit 2. (Note: custom message, lowercase `scope`, and usage says `srgn`, unlike
  clap-generated errors which say `executable` — see §7.)

---

## 3. Replacement action (`-- <REPLACEMENT>`, env `REPLACE`)

- Must follow a literal `--`: `srgn 'o' 'X'` fails with
  `error: unexpected argument 'X' found` (exit 2). Everything after `--` is positional,
  so flags must come before `--`: `--upper 'o' -- 'x'`.
- `REPLACE` env var supplies the replacement if the positional is absent
  (`REPLACE='X' srgn 'o'` works; `REPLACE=''` deletes matches).
- Runs BEFORE all other actions: `--upper 'o' -- 'x'` on `foo` → `fXX`;
  `--lower '(?i)o' -- 'X'` on `Foo` → `Fxx`.
- Subsequent composable actions run in a fixed pipeline order independent of CLI flag
  order (observed: replacement → upper → lower → titlecase; `-t -u` and `-u -t` both
  yield `Hello` from `hello`; `-u -l` and `-l -u` both yield lowercase).
- Non-participating / undefined variables raise errors and abort (see below).

### Variables

- `$0` / `${0}` = entire match. `$1`, `$2`, ... numbered groups; `${1}` equivalent.
- `$name` / `${name}` for named groups (both `(?P<>)` and `(<>)` syntaxes).
- Parsing after `$`:
  - digits are consumed greedily: `$10` = variable `10` (NOT `$1`+`0`); use `${1}0`.
  - a digit-run stops at the first non-digit: `$1abc` = `$1` + literal `abc`.
  - names consume `[A-Za-z0-9_]` greedily: `$n_2`, `$n2` are whole names.
  - `$$` = literal dollar sign: `-- '$$1'` → literal `$1` per match.
  - a lone trailing `$` is literal: `-- 'a$'` → `a$`.
  - `${}` (empty braces) is left literal: `-- '[${}]'` → `[${}]`.
  - `${1x}` or unclosed `${1` / `${b` → error "Mismatched braces" (below).
- `\1`-style backrefs in the replacement are NOT supported (invalid escape, below).

### Undefined variable error (verbatim, stderr, exit 1, stdout empty)

```
Error: Error applying: Error in an action: Action failed in replacement: Error in variable expressions: Undefined variable, unable to substitute: '3'
```
(same text with `'nope'` for `$nope`/`${nope}`; `'10'` for `$10`).

A group that EXISTS in the pattern but did not participate in the current match also
raises this: `(a)|(x)` with replacement `[$2]` on `ab` → error `... substitute: '2'`,
exit 1, stdout empty (processing aborts; partial results are not printed).

Mismatched braces (verbatim):
```
Error: Error applying: Error in an action: Action failed in replacement: Error in variable expressions: Mismatched braces for variable: '1'
```
(raised for `${1x}`, `${1` (unclosed), `a${b`; variable name shown is the consumed prefix).

### Escape sequences in the replacement string

Interpreted at "replacement string build" time, before matching. Verified valid set:

| escape | result |
|---|---|
| `\n` | newline (0x0A) |
| `\t` | tab |
| `\r` | carriage return |
| `\f` | form feed (0x0C) |
| `\b` | backspace (0x08) |
| `\\` | backslash |
| `\"` | `"` |
| `\'` | `'` |

Invalid escapes — `\0`, `\a`, `\v`, `\e`, `\x`, `\␣` (backslash-space), `\$`, `\-`,
`\1` (any backslash-digit) — abort before any processing with (stderr, exit 1,
stdout empty):
```
Error: Failed building replacement string

Caused by:
    Contains invalid escape sequences: 'a\xb'
```
(the whole original replacement string is quoted). Note `$$` (not `\$`) is the
dollar escape. An actual newline byte inside the replacement argument is fine.

---

## 4. `--only-matching` and `--line-numbers` output formats (exact)

Both are hidden flags. They reformat the OUTPUT (whether search results or
action-modified content) and do NOT suppress the "No actions specified" error (§6).

Line numbers are 1-based. Column ranges are **0-based byte offsets, end-exclusive,
relative to the start of each line** (bytes, not chars: in `héllo wörld`, `o` is
range `5-6`; in `a😀b`, `b` is `5-6`). Multiple ranges on one line are `;`-separated,
in ascending order, adjacent ranges allowed (`1-2;2-3`). If a match includes the
trailing `\n`, the range covers it (pattern `\n` on `ab\n` → range `2-3`).

### Piped (stdout not a TTY) — machine-readable

General shape: `(stdin):[<LINE>:]<RANGES>:<LINE-CONTENT>` per output line, where the
line content is printed raw (including its own trailing `\n`; no trailing newline is
added if the input lacks one).

- `--only-matching 'o'` on `hello world\n`:
  ```
  (stdin):4-5;7-8:hello world
  ```
  Only lines containing ≥1 (non-empty) match are printed.
- `--line-numbers 'o'` on the same:
  ```
  (stdin):1:4-5;7-8:hello world
  ```
  `--line-numbers` prints ALL lines; non-matching lines get an EMPTY range field:
  input `foo bar\nbaz qux\n` with scope `foo`:
  ```
  (stdin):1:0-3:foo bar
  (stdin):2::baz qux
  ```
  (note `2::` — empty ranges between the two colons). An empty input line prints as
  `(stdin):2::` followed by its newline.
- Both flags: line number + only matching lines:
  ```
  (stdin):1:0-3:foo bar
  ```
- With an action, the CONTENT is post-action and the RANGES are post-action byte
  ranges of where the scoped content ended up:
  `--only-matching 'foo' -- 'X'` on `foo bar\nbaz qux\n` → `(stdin):0-1:X bar`
  (range `0-1`, not `0-3`). `'a+|b+' -- 'X'` on `aaa bbb` → `(stdin):0-1;2-3:X X`.
- Multi-line matches are split per line: `--only-matching 'b\nc'` on `ab\ncd\n`:
  ```
  (stdin):1-3:ab
  (stdin):0-1:cd
  ```
  (range `1-3` on line 1 covers `b` plus the `\n`).
- Deletion yields empty post-action ranges: `--only-matching -d 'foo'` prints NOTHING
  for `foo bar foo\n`; `--line-numbers -d 'foo'` prints `(stdin):1:: bar ` + `\n`
  (content is the post-deletion line ` bar `).
- In search mode (language scope), piped output uses the same format with the range
  being the in-scope portion of each printed line; only in-scope lines are printed:
  `--python 'def'` on `def f():\n    pass\n\nx = 1\n`:
  ```
  (stdin):1:0-8:def f():
  (stdin):2:0-8:    pass
  ```
- The `(stdin)` label is literal when reading stdin; with `-G` file processing the
  filename is used (file mode itself is out of scope here).

### TTY stdout — human-readable

Detected via `isatty`; force with `--stdout-detection force-tty|force-pipe`.
**No ANSI color codes are ever emitted** (verified with `script -qec`).

- `--only-matching 'foo'` (TTY, no action): prints only MATCHING LINES, whole line,
  no prefix, no ranges: `foo bar`.
- `--line-numbers 'foo'` (TTY): prints ALL lines as `N:<content>`:
  `1:foo bar`, `2:baz qux`.
- Both flags (TTY): `1:foo bar` (only matching lines, numbered).
- With actions (TTY): same line filtering; content is the modified line:
  `--only-matching 'o' -- 'X'` on `hello world` → `hellX wXrld`;
  `--line-numbers 'o' --upper` → `1:hellO wOrld`.
- Search mode (language scope) on TTY: `N:<line>` for each in-scope line:
  `1:def f():`, `2:    pass`.

---

## 5. `--fail-any` / `--fail-none`

- `--fail-any`, something in scope: stderr `Error: Error applying: Some input was in scope`,
  exit **1**, stdout EMPTY (normal output is suppressed entirely).
- `--fail-any`, nothing in scope: normal output, exit 0.
- `--fail-none`, nothing in scope: stderr `Error: Error applying: No input was in scope`,
  exit **1**, stdout empty.
- `--fail-none`, something in scope: normal output, exit 0.
- Both flags: fail-any wins when there is a match, fail-none when there isn't.
- "In scope" means at least one NON-EMPTY match (see §1): patterns `''` or `x*`
  producing only empty matches count as "nothing in scope".
- Default scope `.*` on EMPTY input counts as nothing in scope (`--fail-none` fires).
- Works identically in search mode (language scope) and with no action at all
  (the "No actions specified" ERROR log line is still emitted first in that case).
- **Search mode implies fail-none**: `--python 'def'` (no actions) with no matches on
  stdin exits 1 with `Error: Error applying: No input was in scope` — even without
  `--fail-none`. The same input WITH an action (`--python 'def' --upper`) exits 0 and
  returns the input unchanged. Regex `--only-matching` with no match (no language
  scope) exits 0 silently (aside from the §6 log line).

---

## 6. The "No actions specified" ERROR log line

Exact format (stderr, single line, LF-terminated):

```
[2026-08-08T10:23:20.912848Z ERROR srgn] No actions specified, and not in search mode. Will return input unchanged, if any.
```

- Timestamp: RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 UTC with 6 fractional second digits and `Z`
  (`[%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%6fZ ERROR srgn] `). This is a tracing-style log line;
  the level field is padded to 5 chars (`INFO  srgn` at lower levels).
- Emitted at log level ERROR; base level comes from `RUST_LOG` (default `error`), so
  `RUST_LOG=off` suppresses it. `-v` flags raise verbosity from the base.
- **Emitted when**: reading stdin (or files), NO action is given, and no language
  scope is given (i.e. not search mode). The input is then echoed unchanged to stdout
  and the exit code is still 0. Also emitted with `--only-matching` / `--line-numbers`
  (they are output formatters, NOT actions and NOT search mode).
- **Suppressed by**: any of replacement (`-- 'X'` incl. empty string and env
  `REPLACE`), `-u/--upper`, `-l/--lower`, `-t/--titlecase`, `-n/--normalize`,
  `-g/--german`, `-S/--symbols`, `-d/--delete`, or any language scope
  (`--python`, `--rust`, ...; search mode).
- **QUIRK**: `-s/--squeeze` alone does NOT suppress the line — it is emitted even
  though squeeze does run and modifies the output (`-s 'o'` on `fooo` → `fo` plus the
  ERROR line). Combining `-s` with any composable action (`-s -u`) suppresses it.
- Also emitted when the input is empty ("...if any.").

A second stderr ERROR line exists for file mode: when stdin is piped AND `-G` is
given, stdin wins:
```
[... ERROR srgn] Detected stdin, and request for files: will use stdin and ignore files.
```

---

## 7. Exit codes & clap usage errors

- `0` — success (including no-match with actions, no-action passthrough).
- `1` — runtime errors, always `Error: <message>` on stderr (anyhow chain format
  with `Caused by:` blocks where applicable), stdout empty:
  invalid regex, invalid replacement escapes, undefined/mismatched variables,
  fail-any/fail-none, invalid UTF-8 input.
- `2` — CLI/usage errors from clap, on stderr, format:
  ```
  error: unexpected argument '--bogus' found

  Usage: executable [OPTIONS] [SCOPE] [-- <REPLACEMENT>]

  For more information, try '--help'.
  ```
  Other examples: `-d` without scope:
  ```
  error: the following required arguments were not provided:
    <SCOPE>

  Usage: executable --delete <SCOPE> [-- <REPLACEMENT>]
  ```
  `-d` combined with other actions:
  ```
  error: the argument '--delete' cannot be used with:
    [REPLACEMENT]
    --upper
    --lower
    --titlecase
    --normalize
    --german
    --symbols
  ```
  `-s -d`:
  ```
  error: the argument '--squeeze' cannot be used with '--delete'
  ```
  (Note `-s` IS composable with everything except `-d` — `-s -u 'o'` and
  `-s 'o' -- 'X'` both work, replacement running first, despite the help text calling
  squeeze "only usable alone".)
- Invalid UTF-8 on stdin: `Error: I/O error: stream did not contain valid UTF-8`,
  exit 1, stdout empty.

---

## 8. Input handling edge cases

- Input is read from stdin to EOF as UTF-8 text; processed as ONE string (newlines
  included) — regexes can match across lines.
- **No trailing newline**: preserved byte-for-byte; srgn never adds one.
  `printf 'foo bar' | srgn 'bar' -- 'X'` → `foo X` (no newline). `--only-matching`
  output likewise ends without newline: `(stdin):4-7:foo bar`.
- Empty input: actions exit 0 with empty stdout (`.*` matches only empties → nothing
  to do). No-action passthrough emits the §6 ERROR line and exits 0.
- CRLF: `\r` is an ordinary character (lines are split on `\n` only). Output preserves
  `\r\n`. `--line-numbers` on `foo\r\nbar\r\n`:
  ```
  (stdin):1::foo\r\n
  (stdin):2:0-3:bar\r\n
  ```
  i.e. the `\r` is part of the printed line content. `$`/`(?m)$` match only before
  `\n`, so `bar$` does not match a CRLF line (need `bar\r$`).
- Unicode/emoji: matching and ranges are byte-based; regex chars are Unicode scalar
  values (see §1, §4).
- Env vars: every action flag has an env equivalent (`UPPER`, `LOWER`, `REPLACE`, ...);
  boolean envs must be exactly `true`/`false` (`UPPER=1` → clap error exit 2:
  `error: invalid value '1' for '--upper'\n  [possible values: true, false]`).

## 9. Composition / intersection of scopes

- Regex scope INTERSECTS with language scopes (actions apply only where both agree):
  `--python 'def' 'o' -- 'O'` replaces `o` only inside `def` blocks:
  `def foo():\n    x = 1\n\ndef bar():\n    y = 2\n` → `def fOO():` (rest unchanged).
  `--python 'strings' 'o' -- 'O'` touches only `o`s inside string literals.
- `-j/--join-language-scopes` ORs multiple language scopes but never affects the
  regex scope, which always intersects (per `--help`).
- Multiple regex matches within scope are each replaced independently, in one
  left-to-right pass (no re-scanning of replaced text).

## 10. Handy verified input→output table

| command (stdin piped) | stdout | exit |
|---|---|---|
| `echo 'Hello World!' \| srgn '[wW]orld' -- 'there'` | `Hello there!` | 0 |
| `echo 'Hello World!' \| srgn '[wW]orld'` | `Hello World!` (+ ERROR log on stderr) | 0 |
| `echo 'foo' \| srgn -u 'o'` | `fOO` | 0 |
| `printf 'foo\n' \| srgn -d 'foo'` | `\n` | 0 |
| `printf 'foo bar foo\n' \| srgn -d 'foo'` | ` bar \n` | 0 |
| `printf 'fooooo bar\n' \| srgn -s 'o'` | `fo bar` (+ ERROR log) | 0 |
| `printf 'hello world\n' \| srgn -t '\w+'` | `Hello World` | 0 |
| `printf 'café\n' \| srgn -n 'café'` | `cafe` (NFD + marks dropped) | 0 |
| `printf 'a != b\n' \| srgn -S '!='` | `a ≠ b` | 0 |
| `printf 'foo bar\n' \| srgn '(f)(o+)' -- '[$0][$1][$2][${1}]'` | `[foo][f][oo][f] bar` | 0 |
| `printf 'aaaa\n' \| srgn 'aa' -- 'X'` | `XX` | 0 |
| `printf 'abc\n' \| srgn 'x*' -- 'X'` | `abc` | 0 |
| `printf 'foo\n' \| srgn '(?=(o))' -- '[$1]'` | `foo` (zero-width ignored) | 0 |
| `printf 'foo\n' \| srgn '(f)o' -- '$3'` | (stderr Undefined variable '3') | 1 |
| `printf 'foo\n' \| srgn 'o' -- 'a\nb'` | `fa\nba\nb` (escapes interpreted) | 0 |
| `printf 'foo\n' \| srgn --fail-any 'foo' -- 'X'` | (stderr Some input was in scope) | 1 |
| `printf 'foo\n' \| srgn --fail-none 'zzz' -- 'X'` | (stderr No input was in scope) | 1 |

# srgn core-engine behavioral specification

(Requested filename was the full area description; it exceeds the 255-byte filename
limit, so this spec lives at `core-engine.md`.)

Binary under test: `srgn 0.14.1` (`/workspace/executable --version` → `srgn 0.14.1`).
All probes used stdin piping. Invocation shape: `srgn [OPTIONS] [SCOPE] [-- <REPLACEMENT>]`.
Default `SCOPE` is `.*`.

(do not appear in `-h` or `--help`). `-o` does NOT exist (clap error, exit 2).
`--count` does NOT exist (exit 2).

## 1. Regex engine semantics

`fancy-regex`, NOT the plain Rust `regex` crate):

- `a(?=b)`, `a(?!b)`, `(?<=a)b`, `(?<!a)b` all work.
- Backreferences work: `(a)\1` matches `aa`; named: `(?P<w>ab)(?P=w)` and
  `(?P<w>ab)\k<w>` both match `abab`.
- Both named-group syntaxes work: `(?P<n>a)` and `(?<n>a)`.
- Duplicate group names are accepted: `(?P<n>a)(?P<n>a)` matches `aa`.
- `\b` word boundary, `\w`, `\d`, `\p{Greek}` (Unicode properties) work.
- `\w` is Unicode-aware: `\w+` on `héllo w0rld` matches `héllo` and `w0rld`.
- `(?i)` inline case-insensitive flag works and is Unicode-aware:
  `(?i)été` matches both `ÉTÉ` and `été`.
- `(?s)` dotall works: `(?s)a.b` matches `a\nb`.
- `(?m)` multiline works (see anchors).
- `(?-u)` (disabling Unicode) is rejected:
  ```
  Error: Failed building regex

  Caused by:
      Invalid regex: Parsing error at position 3: Disabling Unicode not supported
  ```
  (position 3 = index of `u` in `(?-u)...`)

### Invalid regex errors (verbatim, stderr, exit code 1, stdout empty)

Two error families exist. Format is an anyhow-style chain:

Pattern `(`:
```
Error: Failed building regex

Caused by:
    Invalid regex: Parsing error at position 1: Opening parenthesis without closing parenthesis
```

Pattern `a**`:
```
Error: Failed building regex

Caused by:
    Invalid regex: Parsing error at position 2: Target of repeat operator is invalid
```

Patterns `a{2,1}` and `[z-a]` (delegated to the inner regex crate):
```
Error: Failed building regex

Caused by:
    Invalid regex: Error compiling regex: Regex error: error parsing pattern 0
```

Exact bytes: `Error: Failed building regex\n\nCaused by:\n    Invalid regex: ...\n`
(4-space indent before `Invalid regex`). Exit code **1**. Nothing on stdout.
No ANSI colors even when stderr is a TTY.

### Anchors

- `^`/`$` without `(?m)`: match start/end of the ENTIRE input only.
  - `^foo` on `foo\nbar\nfoo\n` → replaces only the first `foo`.
  - `bar$` on `foo bar\n` → NO match (`$` does not match before a trailing `\n`).
- `(?m)^foo` on `foo\nbar\nfoo\n` → matches both `foo`s.
- `(?m)bar$` on `foo bar\n` → matches.
- CRLF: `ar$` and even `(?m)ar$` do NOT match `foo\r\nbar\r\n` (the `\r` sits before
  the `\n`). `(?m)ar\r$` DOES match.
- `\A` matches start of input. `\z` matches absolute end of input (NOT before trailing
  newline): `bar\z` matches `foo\nbar` but not `foo\nbar\n`.

### Empty matches are discarded

Any match of length 0 is completely ignored — it produces no scope, no replacement,
no output line in `--only-matching`, and does not count for `--fail-any`/`--fail-none`:

- `x*` on `abc\n` with replacement `X` → output `abc\n` unchanged.
- Empty pattern `''` on `abc\n` → unchanged. `--only-matching ''` prints nothing.
- `(?=(aa))` on `aaaa` with replacement `[$1]` → `aaaa` unchanged (zero-width overall
  matches ignored even though group 1 is non-empty; no overlapping trick possible).
- `.*` on `abc\n` → `X\n`: `.*` matches `abc` (0–3); the empty match at position 3 is
  discarded. `.*` on input `\n` → output `\n` unchanged (only empty matches).
- `--fail-none '' -- 'X'` on `foo\n` → fails with "No input was in scope" (empty
  matches don't count). `--fail-any 'x*' -- 'X'` on `abc\n` → exit 0.

### Matching / overlapping behavior

- Leftmost-first, non-overlapping, matching resumes after the end of the previous match:
  - `aa` on `aaaa\n` → `XX`; `aa` on `aaa\n` → `Xa`.
- `.` matches any single Unicode scalar value except `\n`: `.` on `a😀b\n` → `XXX`
  (the 4-byte emoji is one match). `.` does not match `\n` (unless `(?s)`).
- Default scope `.*` on `ab\ncd\n` → `X\nX\n` (per-line runs; newline never matched;
  interstitial empty matches discarded).

---

## 2. Literal-string mode (`-L` / `--literal-string`, env `LITERAL_STRING`)

- Scope is matched as a literal byte string: `-L 'a.c'` on `a.c abc a*c` → `X abc a*c`.
- Case-sensitive: `-L 'foo'` on `Foo FOO foo` replaces only the last.
- Regex-special characters need no escaping: `-L 'a(b'` works.
- Literal may contain newlines: `-L 'b\nc'` (actual newline) on `ab\ncd\n` → `aXd\n`.
- Empty literal `-L '' -- 'X'` → no-op, input unchanged, exit 0 (consistent with
  empty matches being discarded).
- Non-overlapping, left to right: `-L 'aa'` on `aaaa` → `XX`.
- In `-L` mode, replacement variables are NOT expanded — there are no capture groups,
  and even `$0` stays literal: `-L 'foo' -- '[$0]'` on `foo foo` → `[$0] [$0]`.
  Same for `$1` → literal. (Escape sequences like `\n` in the replacement ARE still
  interpreted in `-L` mode.)
- `-L` without a scope argument:
  ```
  error: The following required argument was not provided: scope

  Usage: srgn [OPTIONS] [SCOPE] [-- <REPLACEMENT>]

  For more information, try '--help'.
  ```
  Exit 2. (Note: custom message, lowercase `scope`, and usage says `srgn`, unlike
  clap-generated errors which say `executable` — see §7.)

---

## 3. Replacement action (`-- <REPLACEMENT>`, env `REPLACE`)

- Must follow a literal `--`: `srgn 'o' 'X'` fails with
  `error: unexpected argument 'X' found` (exit 2). Everything after `--` is positional,
  so flags must come before `--`: `--upper 'o' -- 'x'`.
- `REPLACE` env var supplies the replacement if the positional is absent
  (`REPLACE='X' srgn 'o'` works; `REPLACE=''` deletes matches).
- Runs BEFORE all other actions: `--upper 'o' -- 'x'` on `foo` → `fXX`;
  `--lower '(?i)o' -- 'X'` on `Foo` → `Fxx`.
- Subsequent composable actions run in a fixed pipeline order independent of CLI flag
  order (observed: replacement → upper → lower → titlecase; `-t -u` and `-u -t` both
  yield `Hello` from `hello`; `-u -l` and `-l -u` both yield lowercase).
- Non-participating / undefined variables raise errors and abort (see below).

### Variables

- `$0` / `${0}` = entire match. `$1`, `$2`, ... numbered groups; `${1}` equivalent.
- `$name` / `${name}` for named groups (both `(?P<>)` and `(<>)` syntaxes).
- Parsing after `$`:
  - digits are consumed greedily: `$10` = variable `10` (NOT `$1`+`0`); use `${1}0`.
  - a digit-run stops at the first non-digit: `$1abc` = `$1` + literal `abc`.
  - names consume `[A-Za-z0-9_]` greedily: `$n_2`, `$n2` are whole names.
  - `$$` = literal dollar sign: `-- '$$1'` → literal `$1` per match.
  - a lone trailing `$` is literal: `-- 'a$'` → `a$`.
  - `${}` (empty braces) is left literal: `-- '[${}]'` → `[${}]`.
  - `${1x}` or unclosed `${1` / `${b` → error "Mismatched braces" (below).
- `\1`-style backrefs in the replacement are NOT supported (invalid escape, below).

### Undefined variable error (verbatim, stderr, exit 1, stdout empty)

```
Error: Error applying: Error in an action: Action failed in replacement: Error in variable expressions: Undefined variable, unable to substitute: '3'
```
(same text with `'nope'` for `$nope`/`${nope}`; `'10'` for `$10`).

A group that EXISTS in the pattern but did not participate in the current match also
raises this: `(a)|(x)` with replacement `[$2]` on `ab` → error `... substitute: '2'`,
exit 1, stdout empty (processing aborts; partial results are not printed).

Mismatched braces (verbatim):
```
Error: Error applying: Error in an action: Action failed in replacement: Error in variable expressions: Mismatched braces for variable: '1'
```
(raised for `${1x}`, `${1` (unclosed), `a${b`; variable name shown is the consumed prefix).

### Escape sequences in the replacement string

Interpreted at "replacement string build" time, before matching. Verified valid set:

| escape | result |
|---|---|
| `\n` | newline (0x0A) |
| `\t` | tab |
| `\r` | carriage return |
| `\f` | form feed (0x0C) |
| `\b` | backspace (0x08) |
| `\\` | backslash |
| `\"` | `"` |
| `\'` | `'` |

Invalid escapes — `\0`, `\a`, `\v`, `\e`, `\x`, `\␣` (backslash-space), `\$`, `\-`,
`\1` (any backslash-digit) — abort before any processing with (stderr, exit 1,
stdout empty):
```
Error: Failed building replacement string

Caused by:
    Contains invalid escape sequences: 'a\xb'
```
(the whole original replacement string is quoted). Note `$$` (not `\$`) is the
dollar escape. An actual newline byte inside the replacement argument is fine.

---

## 4. `--only-matching` and `--line-numbers` output formats (exact)

Both are hidden flags. They reformat the OUTPUT (whether search results or
action-modified content) and do NOT suppress the "No actions specified" error (§6).

Line numbers are 1-based. Column ranges are **0-based byte offsets, end-exclusive,
relative to the start of each line** (bytes, not chars: in `héllo wörld`, `o` is
range `5-6`; in `a😀b`, `b` is `5-6`). Multiple ranges on one line are `;`-separated,
in ascending order, adjacent ranges allowed (`1-2;2-3`). If a match includes the
trailing `\n`, the range covers it (pattern `\n` on `ab\n` → range `2-3`).

### Piped (stdout not a TTY) — machine-readable

General shape: `(stdin):[<LINE>:]<RANGES>:<LINE-CONTENT>` per output line, where the
line content is printed raw (including its own trailing `\n`; no trailing newline is
added if the input lacks one).

- `--only-matching 'o'` on `hello world\n`:
  ```
  (stdin):4-5;7-8:hello world
  ```
  Only lines containing ≥1 (non-empty) match are printed.
- `--line-numbers 'o'` on the same:
  ```
  (stdin):1:4-5;7-8:hello world
  ```
  `--line-numbers` prints ALL lines; non-matching lines get an EMPTY range field:
  input `foo bar\nbaz qux\n` with scope `foo`:
  ```
  (stdin):1:0-3:foo bar
  (stdin):2::baz qux
  ```
  (note `2::` — empty ranges between the two colons). An empty input line prints as
  `(stdin):2::` followed by its newline.
- Both flags: line number + only matching lines:
  ```
  (stdin):1:0-3:foo bar
  ```
- With an action, the CONTENT is post-action and the RANGES are post-action byte
  ranges of where the scoped content ended up:
  `--only-matching 'foo' -- 'X'` on `foo bar\nbaz qux\n` → `(stdin):0-1:X bar`
  (range `0-1`, not `0-3`). `'a+|b+' -- 'X'` on `aaa bbb` → `(stdin):0-1;2-3:X X`.
- Multi-line matches are split per line: `--only-matching 'b\nc'` on `ab\ncd\n`:
  ```
  (stdin):1-3:ab
  (stdin):0-1:cd
  ```
  (range `1-3` on line 1 covers `b` plus the `\n`).
- Deletion yields empty post-action ranges: `--only-matching -d 'foo'` prints NOTHING
  for `foo bar foo\n`; `--line-numbers -d 'foo'` prints `(stdin):1:: bar ` + `\n`
  (content is the post-deletion line ` bar `).
- In search mode (language scope), piped output uses the same format with the range
  being the in-scope portion of each printed line; only in-scope lines are printed:
  `--python 'def'` on `def f():\n    pass\n\nx = 1\n`:
  ```
  (stdin):1:0-8:def f():
  (stdin):2:0-8:    pass
  ```
- The `(stdin)` label is literal when reading stdin; with `-G` file processing the
  filename is used (file mode itself is out of scope here).

### TTY stdout — human-readable

Detected via `isatty`; force with `--stdout-detection force-tty|force-pipe`.
**No ANSI color codes are ever emitted** (verified with `script -qec`).

- `--only-matching 'foo'` (TTY, no action): prints only MATCHING LINES, whole line,
  no prefix, no ranges: `foo bar`.
- `--line-numbers 'foo'` (TTY): prints ALL lines as `N:<content>`:
  `1:foo bar`, `2:baz qux`.
- Both flags (TTY): `1:foo bar` (only matching lines, numbered).
- With actions (TTY): same line filtering; content is the modified line:
  `--only-matching 'o' -- 'X'` on `hello world` → `hellX wXrld`;
  `--line-numbers 'o' --upper` → `1:hellO wOrld`.
- Search mode (language scope) on TTY: `N:<line>` for each in-scope line:
  `1:def f():`, `2:    pass`.

---

## 5. `--fail-any` / `--fail-none`

- `--fail-any`, something in scope: stderr `Error: Error applying: Some input was in scope`,
  exit **1**, stdout EMPTY (normal output is suppressed entirely).
- `--fail-any`, nothing in scope: normal output, exit 0.
- `--fail-none`, nothing in scope: stderr `Error: Error applying: No input was in scope`,
  exit **1**, stdout empty.
- `--fail-none`, something in scope: normal output, exit 0.
- Both flags: fail-any wins when there is a match, fail-none when there isn't.
- "In scope" means at least one NON-EMPTY match (see §1): patterns `''` or `x*`
  producing only empty matches count as "nothing in scope".
- Default scope `.*` on EMPTY input counts as nothing in scope (`--fail-none` fires).
- Works identically in search mode (language scope) and with no action at all
  (the "No actions specified" ERROR log line is still emitted first in that case).
- **Search mode implies fail-none**: `--python 'def'` (no actions) with no matches on
  stdin exits 1 with `Error: Error applying: No input was in scope` — even without
  `--fail-none`. The same input WITH an action (`--python 'def' --upper`) exits 0 and
  returns the input unchanged. Regex `--only-matching` with no match (no language
  scope) exits 0 silently (aside from the §6 log line).

---

## 6. The "No actions specified" ERROR log line

Exact format (stderr, single line, LF-terminated):

```
[2026-08-08T10:23:20.912848Z ERROR srgn] No actions specified, and not in search mode. Will return input unchanged, if any.
```

- Timestamp: RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 UTC with 6 fractional second digits and `Z`
  (`[%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%6fZ ERROR srgn] `). This is a tracing-style log line;
  the level field is padded to 5 chars (`INFO  srgn` at lower levels).
- Emitted at log level ERROR; base level comes from `RUST_LOG` (default `error`), so
  `RUST_LOG=off` suppresses it. `-v` flags raise verbosity from the base.
- **Emitted when**: reading stdin (or files), NO action is given, and no language
  scope is given (i.e. not search mode). The input is then echoed unchanged to stdout
  and the exit code is still 0. Also emitted with `--only-matching` / `--line-numbers`
  (they are output formatters, NOT actions and NOT search mode).
- **Suppressed by**: any of replacement (`-- 'X'` incl. empty string and env
  `REPLACE`), `-u/--upper`, `-l/--lower`, `-t/--titlecase`, `-n/--normalize`,
  `-g/--german`, `-S/--symbols`, `-d/--delete`, or any language scope
  (`--python`, `--rust`, ...; search mode).
- **QUIRK**: `-s/--squeeze` alone does NOT suppress the line — it is emitted even
  though squeeze does run and modifies the output (`-s 'o'` on `fooo` → `fo` plus the
  ERROR line). Combining `-s` with any composable action (`-s -u`) suppresses it.
- Also emitted when the input is empty ("...if any.").

A second stderr ERROR line exists for file mode: when stdin is piped AND `-G` is
given, stdin wins:
```
[... ERROR srgn] Detected stdin, and request for files: will use stdin and ignore files.
```

---

## 7. Exit codes & clap usage errors

- `0` — success (including no-match with actions, no-action passthrough).
- `1` — runtime errors, always `Error: <message>` on stderr (anyhow chain format
  with `Caused by:` blocks where applicable), stdout empty:
  invalid regex, invalid replacement escapes, undefined/mismatched variables,
  fail-any/fail-none, invalid UTF-8 input.
- `2` — CLI/usage errors from clap, on stderr, format:
  ```
  error: unexpected argument '--bogus' found

  Usage: executable [OPTIONS] [SCOPE] [-- <REPLACEMENT>]

  For more information, try '--help'.
  ```
  Other examples: `-d` without scope:
  ```
  error: the following required arguments were not provided:
    <SCOPE>

  Usage: executable --delete <SCOPE> [-- <REPLACEMENT>]
  ```
  `-d` combined with other actions:
  ```
  error: the argument '--delete' cannot be used with:
    [REPLACEMENT]
    --upper
    --lower
    --titlecase
    --normalize
    --german
    --symbols
  ```
  `-s -d`:
  ```
  error: the argument '--squeeze' cannot be used with '--delete'
  ```
  (Note `-s` IS composable with everything except `-d` — `-s -u 'o'` and
  `-s 'o' -- 'X'` both work, replacement running first, despite the help text calling
  squeeze "only usable alone".)
- Invalid UTF-8 on stdin: `Error: I/O error: stream did not contain valid UTF-8`,
  exit 1, stdout empty.

---

## 8. Input handling edge cases

- Input is read from stdin to EOF as UTF-8 text; processed as ONE string (newlines
  included) — regexes can match across lines.
- **No trailing newline**: preserved byte-for-byte; srgn never adds one.
  `printf 'foo bar' | srgn 'bar' -- 'X'` → `foo X` (no newline). `--only-matching`
  output likewise ends without newline: `(stdin):4-7:foo bar`.
- Empty input: actions exit 0 with empty stdout (`.*` matches only empties → nothing
  to do). No-action passthrough emits the §6 ERROR line and exits 0.
- CRLF: `\r` is an ordinary character (lines are split on `\n` only). Output preserves
  `\r\n`. `--line-numbers` on `foo\r\nbar\r\n`:
  ```
  (stdin):1::foo\r\n
  (stdin):2:0-3:bar\r\n
  ```
  i.e. the `\r` is part of the printed line content. `$`/`(?m)$` match only before
  `\n`, so `bar$` does not match a CRLF line (need `bar\r$`).
- Unicode/emoji: matching and ranges are byte-based; regex chars are Unicode scalar
  values (see §1, §4).
- Env vars: every action flag has an env equivalent (`UPPER`, `LOWER`, `REPLACE`, ...);
  boolean envs must be exactly `true`/`false` (`UPPER=1` → clap error exit 2:
  `error: invalid value '1' for '--upper'\n  [possible values: true, false]`).

## 9. Composition / intersection of scopes

- Regex scope INTERSECTS with language scopes (actions apply only where both agree):
  `--python 'def' 'o' -- 'O'` replaces `o` only inside `def` blocks:
  `def foo():\n    x = 1\n\ndef bar():\n    y = 2\n` → `def fOO():` (rest unchanged).
  `--python 'strings' 'o' -- 'O'` touches only `o`s inside string literals.
- `-j/--join-language-scopes` ORs multiple language scopes but never affects the
  regex scope, which always intersects (per `--help`).
- Multiple regex matches within scope are each replaced independently, in one
  left-to-right pass (no re-scanning of replaced text).

## 10. Handy verified input→output table

| command (stdin piped) | stdout | exit |
|---|---|---|
| `echo 'Hello World!' \| srgn '[wW]orld' -- 'there'` | `Hello there!` | 0 |
| `echo 'Hello World!' \| srgn '[wW]orld'` | `Hello World!` (+ ERROR log on stderr) | 0 |
| `echo 'foo' \| srgn -u 'o'` | `fOO` | 0 |
| `printf 'foo\n' \| srgn -d 'foo'` | `\n` | 0 |
| `printf 'foo bar foo\n' \| srgn -d 'foo'` | ` bar \n` | 0 |
| `printf 'fooooo bar\n' \| srgn -s 'o'` | `fo bar` (+ ERROR log) | 0 |
| `printf 'hello world\n' \| srgn -t '\w+'` | `Hello World` | 0 |
| `printf 'café\n' \| srgn -n 'café'` | `cafe` (NFD + marks dropped) | 0 |
| `printf 'a != b\n' \| srgn -S '!='` | `a ≠ b` | 0 |
| `printf 'foo bar\n' \| srgn '(f)(o+)' -- '[$0][$1][$2][${1}]'` | `[foo][f][oo][f] bar` | 0 |
| `printf 'aaaa\n' \| srgn 'aa' -- 'X'` | `XX` | 0 |
| `printf 'abc\n' \| srgn 'x*' -- 'X'` | `abc` | 0 |
| `printf 'foo\n' \| srgn '(?=(o))' -- '[$1]'` | `foo` (zero-width ignored) | 0 |
| `printf 'foo\n' \| srgn '(f)o' -- '$3'` | (stderr Undefined variable '3') | 1 |
| `printf 'foo\n' \| srgn 'o' -- 'a\nb'` | `fa\nba\nb` (escapes interpreted) | 0 |
| `printf 'foo\n' \| srgn --fail-any 'foo' -- 'X'` | (stderr Some input was in scope) | 1 |
| `printf 'foo\n' \| srgn --fail-none 'zzz' -- 'X'` | (stderr No input was in scope) | 1 |

payload.resultSummary:
Spec written to `/workspace/probes/core-engine.md` (the requested filename exceeded the 255-byte filesystem limit, so I used the short form). Key findings:

- **The regex engine is fancy-regex, not plain Rust regex**: lookahead, lookbehind, and backreferences (`(a)\1`, `(?P=w)`, `\k<w>`) all work. Errors come in two verbatim families — `Parsing error at position N: ...` and the delegated `Error compiling regex: Regex error: error parsing pattern 0` (e.g. for `a{2,1}`, `[z-a]`); both print `Error: Failed building regex\n\nCaused by:\n    Invalid regex: ...`, exit 1.
- **Empty matches are silently discarded everywhere** — `''`, `x*`, and even `(?=(aa))` (non-empty group inside a zero-width match) produce no replacements, no `--only-matching` lines, and don't count for `--fail-any`/`--fail-none`. Matching is leftmost, non-overlapping.
- **`--only-matching`/`--line-numbers` are hidden flags** with two totally different formats: piped → `(stdin):[LINE:]start-end;start-end:content` with 0-based **byte** ranges (end-exclusive, post-action positions when actions ran, multi-line matches split per line); TTY → plain `N:line` or bare lines, **no ANSI colors ever**. `--line-numbers` prints ALL lines (non-matching get an empty range: `(stdin):2::baz qux`).
- **Quirks**: `-s/--squeeze` alone still emits the "No actions specified" ERROR log (timestamped `[...Z ERROR srgn] No actions specified, and not in search mode. Will return input unchanged, if any.`) despite working; search mode (language scope, no action) with zero matches hard-fails with `Error: Error applying: No input was in scope`, exit 1, even without `--fail-none`.
- Replacement: `$$` is the literal-dollar escape (not `\$`); valid escapes are `\n \t \r \f \b \\ \" \'`, anything else aborts with `Contains invalid escape sequences: '<whole string>'`; `$10` parses as variable `10`; a group that exists but didn't participate errors as undefined; `-L` mode leaves `$0`/`$1` literal but still interprets escapes. No trailing newline is never added; invalid UTF-8 → `Error: I/O error: stream did not contain valid UTF-8`, exit 1.

args.content:
# srgn — TypeScript & C prepared query scopes: behavioral specification

Binary under test: `srgn 0.14.1` (invoked as `/workspace/executable`; clap usage/error
lines print the argv0-derived name `executable`, except one custom error that hardcodes
`srgn` — noted below). All findings obtained by black-box observation only.

NOTE ON FILE NAME: the task-requested file name exceeded the 255-byte filesystem limit;
this shortened name is used instead.

---

## 1. Search-mode output format (language scopes, no actions)

Giving a language scope (`--typescript <value>`, `--c <value>`, `--*-query`,
`--*-query-file`) without any action puts srgn in **search mode**. Output on stdout,
one line per input line that contains at least one in-scope byte range:

```
<stdin-or-filename>:<line>:<start>-<end>[;<start>-<end>...]:<full original line content>
```

- `(stdin)` is the literal prefix when reading stdin; a real path (`files/one.ts`) when
  working on files via `-G`.
- `<line>` is 1-based.
- `<start>`/`<end>` are **0-based BYTE offsets within that line, start-inclusive,
  end-exclusive** (verified with multibyte input: `"héllo 😀"` string content gives
  `11-22` — bytes, not chars).
- Multiple disjoint ranges on one line are `;`-separated, ascending. Overlapping ranges
  (e.g. produced by `-j` joins of nested scopes) are **merged** into one range.
- The full original line text (including any `\r` of CRLF input) is printed after the
  last `:`.
- Lines are only printed if they contain ≥1 scoped byte. A multi-line scoped node prints
  every line it touches: first line `<startcol>-<linelen>`, middle lines `0-<linelen>`,
  last line `0-<endcol>`.
- Output preserves the input's final-newline state (no trailing newline added/removed).
- `--only-matching` produces byte-identical output in this mode (no observable effect).
- `--line-numbers` has no observable effect in search mode (already numbered).
- There is **no `--count` flag** in this build despite the README
  (`error: unexpected argument '--count' found` + tip `a similar argument exists: '--c'`, exit 2).

### TTY vs pipe

- Piped (or `--stdout-detection force-pipe`): format as above, no ANSI color codes ever.
- TTY (or `--stdout-detection force-tty`): **no byte ranges are shown**. stdin input
  prints `<line>:<content>`. File input prints a header line with the file name, then
  `<line>:<content>` lines, then a blank line; files separated by blank lines:
  ```
  files/one.ts
  1:const a = "x";

  files/two.ts
  1:const b = "y";
  ```
- No ANSI colors were emitted in either mode (checked with `script -qec ... | od -c`),
  including error messages.

### Action-mode note

With an action (replacement, `-d`, `--upper`, ...), stdout is the full transformed
document. With `--line-numbers` added in action mode, output switches to the annotated
form `(stdin):<line>:<ranges>:<modified-line-content>` showing only lines with matches.

---

## 2. Exit codes and error messages (verbatim)

| Condition | stdout | stderr | exit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Search mode, zero in-scope bytes (incl. empty input) | empty | `Error: Error applying: No input was in scope` | 1 |
| Action mode, zero in-scope bytes | input unchanged | empty | 0 |
| `--fail-any` and something matched | (normal) | `Error: Error applying: Some input was in scope` | 1 |
| `--fail-none` and nothing matched | (normal) | `Error: Error applying: No input was in scope` | 1 |
| `--fail-any`/`--fail-none` satisfied | normal | empty | 0 |
| Invalid prepared value (`--typescript bogus`) | empty | clap error (below) | 2 |
| `--typescript` + `--typescript-query` together | empty | clap conflict error (below) | 2 |
| `--c` + `--typescript` (two languages) | empty | `error: Can only use one language at a time.` | 2 |
| Invalid custom query syntax/node/field | empty | `Error: Error occurred while creating a tree-sitter query: ...` | 1 |
| Missing `--*-query-file` | empty | `Error: I/O error: No such file or directory (os error 2)` | 1 |
| Invalid UTF-8 on stdin | empty | `Error: I/O error: stream did not contain valid UTF-8` | 1 |
| No actions and no language scope (not search mode) | input unchanged | `[<RFC3339 timestamp> ERROR srgn] No actions specified, and not in search mode. Will return input unchanged, if any.` | 0 |

Verbatim clap errors (stderr; `executable` is argv0 here):

```
error: invalid value 'bogus' for '--typescript <TYPESCRIPT>'
  [possible values: comments, strings, imports, function, async-function, sync-function, method, constructor, class, enum, interface, try-catch, var-decl, let, const, var, type-params, type-alias, namespace, export]

For more information, try '--help'.
```
```
error: invalid value 'bogus' for '--c <C>'
  [possible values: comments, strings, includes, type-def, enum, struct, variable, function, function-def, function-decl, switch, if, for, while, do, union, identifier, declaration, call-expression]

For more information, try '--help'.
```
Values are case-sensitive; a near-miss appends a tip line between the possible-values
line and the blank line:
```
  tip: a similar value exists: 'comments'
```
The `~PATTERN` dynamic syntax exists only for some Go/Rust values; for TS/C e.g.
`--typescript 'class~K'` is an invalid value (with tip `a similar value exists: 'class'`).

Conflict error:
```
error: the argument '--typescript <TYPESCRIPT>' cannot be used with '--typescript-query <TREE-SITTER-QUERY-VALUE>'

Usage: executable --typescript <TYPESCRIPT> [SCOPE] [-- <REPLACEMENT>]

For more information, try '--help'.
```
(analogous for `--c` / `--c-query`).

Two-languages error — note the usage line here hardcodes `srgn`, not argv0:
```
error: Can only use one language at a time.

Usage: srgn [OPTIONS] [SCOPE] [-- <REPLACEMENT>]

For more information, try '--help'.
```

Custom query compile errors (all `Error: Error occurred while creating a tree-sitter query: Query error at <row>:<col>. ...`, exit 1):
- `--typescript-query '(('`:
  ```
  Error: Error occurred while creating a tree-sitter query: Query error at 1:3. Invalid syntax:
  ((
    ^
  ```
  (the query text and a caret pointing at the offending column are echoed)
- `--typescript-query 'identifier'` (bare word, invalid syntax):
  ```
  Error: Error occurred while creating a tree-sitter query: Query error at 1:1. Invalid syntax:
  identifier
  ^
  ```
- `--typescript-query '(bogus_node)'`:
  `Error: Error occurred while creating a tree-sitter query: Query error at 1:2. Invalid node type bogus_node`
- `--c-query '(declaration bogus: (identifier))'`:
  `Error: Error occurred while creating a tree-sitter query: Query error at 1:14. Invalid field name bogus`
- A syntactically valid query with **no `@capture`** (e.g. `(identifier)`) compiles but
  scopes nothing → `Error: Error applying: No input was in scope`, exit 1 in search mode.
- Custom query scopes = **every captured node, exactly as captured** (quotes NOT stripped;
  e.g. `(variable_declarator name: (identifier) @name value: (string) @val)` on
  `const STR = "double";` yields ranges `6-9;12-20` — `STR` and `"double"` with quotes).
- Prepared-value flag and custom query for the SAME language are mutually exclusive
  (clap error above), but prepared values of one language may be repeated freely.

---

## 3. Scope combination semantics (AND / `-j` OR)

- Repeating a language flag (`--typescript class --typescript method`) **intersects**
  scopes, left to right. Intersection is sequential narrowing: the next query is
  evaluated **only within the regions left in scope by the previous one** (behaviorally:
  everything outside the current scope is masked out, offsets preserved, and the next
  query's captures are found in what remains). Consequences:
  - `--typescript const --typescript var-decl` on `const s = "a";` → `6-13` (declarator
    inside declaration). OK.
  - `--typescript var-decl --typescript const` → nothing (`No input was in scope`):
    no `const` declaration survives inside a bare declarator region.
  - `--typescript class --typescript method` → methods. `--typescript method --typescript class` → nothing.
  - `--typescript strings --typescript strings` → **nothing** (TS string scopes exclude
    quotes/escapes, so the leftover fragments no longer parse as strings). But
    `--c strings --c strings` **works** (C string scopes include the quotes, so the
    masked text still parses as a string literal).
  - `--typescript comments --typescript comments` and `--typescript class --typescript class` work.
- `-j`/`--join-language-scopes` unions all language scopes (order irrelevant); overlapping
  ranges are merged in the output (`--typescript var-decl --typescript const -j` on
  `const s = "a";` → single range `0-14`).
- The regex positional scope always intersects, and intersection requires **full
  containment**: a regex match only partially overlapping a language-scope range is
  discarded entirely. `--typescript strings 'a";'` on `const s = "a";` → nothing
  (`No input was in scope`, exit 1 in search mode); `--typescript strings -d 'c";'` on
  `const s = "abc";` → output unchanged (exit 0). `--typescript strings 'a'` → `11-12`;
  `-d 'b'` → `const s = "ac";`.
- Deletion replaces scoped bytes with nothing; line structure (newline bytes) is kept, so
  deleted multi-line nodes leave empty lines behind. E.g. deleting `class` from
  `let a = 1;\nclass K {\n  m() {}\n}\nlet b = 2;\n` yields `let a = 1;\n\n\n\nlet b = 2;\n`.

---

## 4. TypeScript prepared queries — exact scope semantics

Ranges below verified on representative inputs; "whole node" means the tree-sitter node
span including its keywords but NOT any leading `export `/`export default `/`declare `
prefix and (for methods) NOT decorators.

Reference input fragment used for several entries (line numbers refer to this block):

```ts
1  // leading comment
2  /* block
3     comment */
4  import { foo } from "mod1";
5  import * as ns from 'mod2';
6  import def from `mod3`;
7  const STR = "double";
8  const TPL = `template ${STR} end`;
9  let x = 1, y = 2;
10 var v = 3;
```

### comments
Every `comment` node, full text including the comment markers. `//`, `///`, `//!`, and
`/* ... */` all match. Multi-line block comments span all their lines.
Lines 1–3: `1:0-18`, `2:0-8`, `3:0-13`.
Comments inside strings are not comments; string-like text inside comments is not strings.

### strings
String **content only**, excluding delimiters, and **fragmented** around escape sequences
and template interpolations:
- `"double"` on line 7 → `13-19` (`double`, no quotes).
- `'...'` and template `` `...` `` behave the same (content only).
- Template interpolations `${...}` are excluded; each literal fragment is a separate
  range: line 8 → `13-22;28-32` (`` `template ${STR} end` `` → `template ` and ` end`;
  backticks excluded). Nested templates inside interpolations contribute their own
  fragment ranges (`` `multi\nline ${a + `nested ${b}`} tpl`; `` gives line1 `11-16`,
  line2 `0-5;12-19;25-29`).
- Escape sequences split the content: `"esc \" quote"` → ranges for `esc ` and ` quote`
  (`11-15;17-23`); the `\"` bytes are NOT in scope.
- Applies anywhere a string literal appears: `require("x")`, dynamic `import("x")`,
  `export { x } from "x"` module specifiers all match `strings`.

### imports
Module specifier **content** (no quotes) of `import` statements only:
- `import { foo } from "mod1";` → `21-25` (`mod1`).
- Covers `import ... from '...'`, `import "side-effect";`, and `import type { T } from "..."`.
- Does NOT cover: template-literal specifiers (`` import def from `mod3`; ``),
  `export ... from "..."` re-exports, `require("...")`, dynamic `import("...")`.

### function
Whole `function` **declarations** including the `async` keyword, excluding any
`export [default]` prefix (range starts at `async`/`function`).
`export default function main() {}` → `15-33`.
- NOT matched: arrow functions (`const f = async () => {}`), function expressions
  (`const f = function() {}`), generator declarations (`function* g() {}`,
  `async function* g() {}`), ambient declarations (`declare function f(): void;`).

### async-function / sync-function
Partition of `function`: `async function ...` declarations vs non-async `function ...`
declarations. Same exclusions as `function` (generators matched by NEITHER).

### method
Whole method definitions (`method_definition` nodes) anywhere — class bodies AND object
literals — including modifiers (`public`, `static`, `private async`, `get`/`set`,
`async *gen`) starting at the first modifier, but EXCLUDING decorators on the method.
Object-literal methods match: `{ methodInObj() { return 1; }, }` → range covers
`methodInObj() { return 1; }` (trailing comma excluded).

### constructor
Method definitions named `constructor`, whole node. Matches even in object literals
(`{ constructor() {} }`). Also included in `method` results.

### class
Whole class declarations **including decorators** (a `@dec()` line above the class is part
of the range) but excluding `export [default]` prefix.
- `abstract class` declarations are NOT matched (different node type).
- Class expressions not tested exhaustively; declarations only observed.

### enum
Whole enum declarations, excluding `export`/`declare` prefixes, but a leading `const`
modifier IS included: `const enum Fast { X }` → `0-21` (whole line);
`declare enum Ambient { Y }` → `8-26` (from `enum`).

### interface
Whole interface declarations, excluding `export` prefix.

### try-catch
Whole `try` statements including `catch` and `finally` clauses (any combination:
try/catch, try/finally, try/catch/finally).

### var-decl
Individual `variable_declarator` nodes (name through initializer), excluding the
`let`/`const`/`var` keyword and the trailing `;` or `,`:
- `const STR = "double";` → `6-20` (`STR = "double"`).
- `let x = 1, y = 2;` → `4-9;11-16` (two declarators).
- Destructuring works: `const {a, b} = obj;` → `6-18`; `const [p, q] = arr2;` → `6-19`.
- C-style `for` initializers match: `for (let i = 0; ...)` → `9-14` (`i = 0`).
- `for (const k of keys)` / `for (... in ...)` declarators do NOT match (different node).

### let / const / var
Whole declaration **statements** including the keyword and trailing `;`, excluding
`export ` prefix:
- `let x = 1, y = 2;` → `0-17` (whole line).
- `  export const inner = 1;` → const gives `9-25` (`const inner = 1;`).
- `for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {}` → let gives `5-15` (`let i = 0;`).
- `for (const k of keys)` does NOT match `const`.
- `const enum E {}` does NOT match `const`.

### type-params
Whole type-parameter lists including angle brackets, on any construct (functions,
classes, interfaces, type aliases): `function sfn<T>` → `12-15` (`<T>`);
`interface Gen<T extends object>` → `13-31`; `type Pair<A, B> = ...` → `9-15`.

### type-alias
Whole `type X = ...;` declarations including `;`, excluding `export` prefix.

### namespace
Whole `namespace` blocks, excluding `export` prefix. Nested namespaces: the outer match
subsumes the inner (ranges merge in output).

### export
Whole export statements starting at the `export` keyword:
- `export { foo };`, `export default function main() {}` (whole line, `0-33`),
  `export class/interface/enum/type/namespace/const ...` (whole declaration),
  `export * from "mod-a";`, `export * as ns from "mod-b";`, `export { a as b };`.
- Inside a namespace, `  export const inner = 1;` → `2-25`.

---

## 5. C prepared queries — exact scope semantics

Reference input fragment:

```c
1  // leading comment
2  /* block
3     comment */
4  #include <stdio.h>
5  #include "local.h"
6  typedef unsigned int uint32;
7  enum Color { RED, GREEN = 2 };
8  struct Point {
9    int x;
10 };
11 union Value { int i; float f; };
12 int global = 42;
13 static const char *name = "hi";
14 int add(int a, int b);
15 static void helper(void) {
16   printf("in helper %d\n", global);
17 }
18 int add(int a, int b) {
19   int sum = a + b;
20   return sum;
21 }
```

### comments
All `comment` nodes incl. markers (`//` and `/* */`), like TypeScript.

### strings
**Whole string literals INCLUDING the double quotes**, and NOT fragmented by escapes:
`"hi"` → `26-30` on line 13 (quotes included); `"in helper %d\n"` → one range covering
all of it. Also matches the path of `#include` directives: `<stdio.h>` → `9-18`
(brackets included), `"local.h"` → `9-18` (quotes included).
- Character literals (`'a'`, `'\n'`) do NOT match.

### includes
Whole `#include` directive lines: `#include <stdio.h>` → `0-18`; both `<>` and `""` forms.

### type-def
Whole `typedef` declarations including the trailing `;`:
`typedef unsigned int uint32;` → `0-28`; also `typedef struct { int a; } Anon;`,
`typedef enum {...} E;`, `typedef union {...} U;` (entire statement).

### enum / struct / union
The specifier node (`enum_specifier` / `struct_specifier` / `union_specifier`) — matches
both definitions AND usages, and NEVER includes a trailing `;`:
- `enum Color { RED, GREEN = 2 };` → `0-29` (up to and including `}`).
- `enum Color c;` → `0-10` (`enum Color`).
- `struct Point { ... };` → lines 8–10, last line range `0-1` (`}` only; the `;` stays
  out of scope — deleting the struct leaves a lone `;` behind).
- `struct Point p;` → `0-12` (`struct Point`). `union Value u;` → `0-11`.
- Anonymous specifiers inside typedefs match: `typedef struct { int a; } Anon;` → `8-25`.

### variable
Whole `declaration` nodes (incl. `;`) that are not function definitions — at file scope,
block scope, and `for` initializers:
- `int global = 42;` → `0-16`; `static const char *name = "hi";` → `0-31`;
  `int arr[5] = {1, 2};` → `0-20`; `int *ptr;`; `struct Point p;`; `enum Color c = RED;`;
  `char s[] = "arr";`; `int (*fp)(int);` all match in full.
- Function **prototypes** match too: `int add(int a, int b);` → `0-22`.
- `for (int i = 0; ...)` → `7-17` (`int i = 0;`).
- Function parameters do NOT match.

### declaration
Byte-identical results to `variable` (same underlying `declaration` node set).

### function
"All function usages": `function_declarator` (name + parameter list) at declaration and
definition sites, plus whole `call_expression`s at call sites:
- `int add(int a, int b);` → `4-21` (`add(int a, int b)`).
- `static void helper(void) {` → `12-24` (`helper(void)`).
- `printf("in helper %d\n", global);` → `2-34` (whole call, no `;`).
- `count += add(i, 1);` → `13-22` (`add(i, 1)`).
- Function pointer declarators (`int (*fp)(int);`) do NOT match `function`.

### function-def
Whole function definitions including storage-class/specifiers and body:
`static void helper(void) {` starts at column 0 and spans through the closing `}` line.

### function-decl
All `function_declarator` nodes — both in prototypes AND in definitions:
`int add(int a, int b);` → `4-21`; `static void helper(void) {` → `12-24`;
`int add(int a, int b) {` → `4-21`; `int main(void) {` → `4-14`.
Also function-pointer declarators: `int (*fp)(int);` → `4-14` (`(*fp)(int)`).

### switch / if / for / while / do
Whole statement nodes including bodies, starting at the keyword:
- `if` covers the entire `if / else if / else` chain as one scope (with or without braces).
- `do` includes the trailing `while (...);`.
- Braceless bodies work for `if`/`for`/`while`/`do` (e.g. `while (1) g();` → `2-16`).
- QUIRK: a `switch` whose body is not a compound statement (`switch (1) case 1: break;`)
  is NOT matched (observed `No input was in scope`); with `{ ... }` it matches normally.

### identifier
All `identifier` nodes (not `type_identifier`, not `field_identifier`):
- `enum Color { RED, GREEN = 2 };` → `13-16;18-23` (`RED`, `GREEN`; `Color` is a
  type_identifier and is NOT matched).
- `#define MAX 10` → `8-11` (`MAX` matches).
- Declarator names, call targets, variable references match; struct/union/enum type
  names (`Point`, `Color` in `enum Color c` — wait: `enum Color c = RED;` gives
  `11-12;15-18`, i.e. `c` and `RED`; `Color` excluded), member/field names
  (`p.x`, `int x;` inside struct bodies) do NOT match.

### call-expression
Whole `call_expression` nodes: exactly the call-site subset of `function`
(`printf(...)`, `add(i, 1)`, `helper()`), without trailing `;`.

---

## 6. Input/encoding edge cases

- **Empty stdin** (0 bytes): search mode → `Error: Error applying: No input was in scope`,
  exit 1; action mode → empty stdout, exit 0.
- **No trailing newline**: preserved; search output's last line also has no trailing
  newline. Exit 0.
- **Unicode/emoji**: fully supported; reported columns are byte offsets (UTF-8), so
  multibyte content shifts end columns. E.g. TS string `"héllo 😀"` → `11-22`;
  C identifier `café` in `int café = 1;` → `4-9`.
- **Invalid UTF-8** anywhere on stdin: `Error: I/O error: stream did not contain valid UTF-8`,
  exit 1, no output (even with no language scope / plain actions).
- **CRLF**: lines split on `\n`; `\r` remains part of the printed line content
  (`// comment^M`) but never part of a scope range (`comments` on `// comment\r\n` →
  `0-10`). Deletion preserves CRLF untouched outside scopes.
- **Syntax errors**: silently tolerated (tree-sitter error recovery). No warning, exit
  follows normal rules. Whatever still parses is scoped: in
  `const x = ;\nfunction broken( {\n  "str";\n`, `--typescript strings` finds `"str"`
  content at `3:3-6`; in `int main( {\n  "str";;;\n  int = 5;\n`, `--c strings` finds
  `"str"` at `2:2-7`. Constructs that no longer parse simply don't match
  (`--c function` on the broken file → `No input was in scope`, exit 1).
- **Wrong language for the content**: no detection/validation; the chosen grammar just
  parses the text. C source `int x = "hi";` under `--typescript strings` → `9-11`
  (TS-style content-only range!); TS comment `// c` under `--c comments` → matches.
- **stdin + `-G` conflict**: when stdin is detected readable and `-G` is given:
  `[<timestamp> ERROR srgn] Detected stdin, and request for files: will use stdin and ignore files.`
  (stdin wins; files ignored).

## 7. Misc flag facts relevant to scoping

- Alias `--ts` for `--typescript` works (`--csharp` has `--cs`, `--rust` has `--rs`;
  `--c` has no alias).
- Env vars set scopes: `TYPESCRIPT=comments srgn`, `C=comments srgn` work identically to
  the flags (also `TYPESCRIPT_QUERY`, `C_QUERY`, `..._QUERY_FILE`).
- `--typescript-query-file q.scm` reads the query from a file; same semantics/errors.
- `-d`/`--delete` requires the positional SCOPE argument:
  `error: the following required arguments were not provided:\n  <SCOPE>` (exit 2);
  pass `.*` to delete the entire language scope.
- In action mode a language scope with zero matches is NOT an error (input returned
  unchanged, exit 0) — the `No input was in scope` error only fires in search mode
  (or when `--fail-none` is passed in action mode).

Binary under test: `srgn 0.14.1` (invoked as `/workspace/executable`; clap usage/error

`srgn` — noted below). All findings obtained by black-box observation only.

NOTE ON FILE NAME: the task-requested file name exceeded the 255-byte filesystem limit;

---

## 1. Search-mode output format (language scopes, no actions)

Giving a language scope (`--typescript <value>`, `--c <value>`, `--*-query`,
`--*-query-file`) without any action puts srgn in **search mode**. Output on stdout,
one line per input line that contains at least one in-scope byte range:

```
<stdin-or-filename>:<line>:<start>-<end>[;<start>-<end>...]:<full original line content>
```

- `(stdin)` is the literal prefix when reading stdin; a real path (`files/one.ts`) when
  working on files via `-G`.
- `<line>` is 1-based.
- `<start>`/`<end>` are **0-based BYTE offsets within that line, start-inclusive,
  end-exclusive** (verified with multibyte input: `"héllo 😀"` string content gives
  `11-22` — bytes, not chars).
- Multiple disjoint ranges on one line are `;`-separated, ascending. Overlapping ranges
  (e.g. produced by `-j` joins of nested scopes) are **merged** into one range.
- The full original line text (including any `\r` of CRLF input) is printed after the
  last `:`.
- Lines are only printed if they contain ≥1 scoped byte. A multi-line scoped node prints
  every line it touches: first line `<startcol>-<linelen>`, middle lines `0-<linelen>`,
  last line `0-<endcol>`.
- Output preserves the input's final-newline state (no trailing newline added/removed).
- `--only-matching` produces byte-identical output in this mode (no observable effect).
- `--line-numbers` has no observable effect in search mode (already numbered).
- There is **no `--count` flag** in this build despite the README
  (`error: unexpected argument '--count' found` + tip `a similar argument exists: '--c'`, exit 2).

### TTY vs pipe

- Piped (or `--stdout-detection force-pipe`): format as above, no ANSI color codes ever.
- TTY (or `--stdout-detection force-tty`): **no byte ranges are shown**. stdin input
  prints `<line>:<content>`. File input prints a header line with the file name, then
  `<line>:<content>` lines, then a blank line; files separated by blank lines:
  ```
  files/one.ts
  1:const a = "x";

  files/two.ts
  1:const b = "y";
  ```
- No ANSI colors were emitted in either mode (checked with `script -qec ... | od -c`),
  including error messages.

### Action-mode note

With an action (replacement, `-d`, `--upper`, ...), stdout is the full transformed
document. With `--line-numbers` added in action mode, output switches to the annotated
form `(stdin):<line>:<ranges>:<modified-line-content>` showing only lines with matches.

---
